ProgramName: Master of Accounting
Requirements: The application for the Master of Accounting (MACC) program at Washington University in St. Louis requires the submission of a current resume, a statement of purpose, and unofficial transcripts from all institutions attended. In addition, applicants must provide standardized test scores (GMAT or GRE), although waivers are available. The application also includes a video essay and at least one professional recommendation. An application fee is required, and interviews are conducted on an invitation-only basis.
Description: The Master of Accounting (MACC) program at Olin Business School prepares students for careers in public accounting, industry, consulting, financial services, and government. [4, 8] Students can choose from three degree formats and customize their experience through various elective courses. [7] The program is designed for both those deepening their accounting knowledge and first-time business students. [7] The curriculum, which can be completed in two or three semesters, consists of a minimum of 33 credit hours, including core courses, electives, and an experiential learning component. [12] The program is STEM-designated and focuses on financial statement expertise, business analytics, and communication skills. [9] Completion of the MACC curriculum meets the educational requirements to apply for the Missouri CPA exam. [12]
Accredidation: AACSB Accredited. [10]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Architectural Design
Requirements: Applicants to the Master of Science in Advanced Architectural Design program (MSAAD) must hold a Bachelor of Architecture (BArch) degree, or a Master of Architecture (MArch) degree from a NAAB-accredited degree program in the United States or its international equivalent. [2, 3] A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. [3] Required application materials include a resume or curriculum vitae, transcripts from all previous higher education institutions, two personal essays, a portfolio demonstrating architecture, design, or visual art work, and three references. [3]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts
Description: The Master of Science in Advanced Architectural Design is a 36-credit, three-semester, post-professional program for individuals who hold an accredited US professional architecture degree or its international equivalent. [1] The program is designed to allow students to pursue advanced design studies and research. [1] It encourages the conceptualization of design as a critical practice that shapes the world's technological, relational, and environmental evolutions. [2] The curriculum is described as highly flexible and individualized, featuring an Advanced Architectural Design Studio in each semester. [1] The program framework aims to explore both academic and professional concerns by asserting that architectural design is critical in addressing contemporary challenges and that its future agency lies in its ability to mobilize realities across different scales and time frames. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: Full-tuition scholarships are available.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Description: The Department of Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science offers a Master of Science degree in Aerospace Engineering with either a Thesis Option or Course Option. [9] The M.S. Thesis in Aerospace Engineering is a degree that allows students to deepen their expertise in a specific area through hands-on research. [2] Students choose a research topic in aerodynamics, propulsion, control systems, materials, systems-design & human-integration and work closely with a faculty advisor. [2] This degree provides the opportunity to develop specialized skills, solve real-world problems, and prepare for advanced roles in industry or academia. [2] The department focuses on several key research areas, including Autonomous and Intelligent Systems, Hypersonics, Multi-Functional and Extreme Environment Materials, Optical, Remote, and Quantum Sensing, Reacting Flows and Propulsion, Space Domain Awareness, and Space Flight and Operations, both Human and Robotic. [2]
ScholarshipType: Department Chair's Master's Fellowship, Tuition scholarship for students from affiliated schools

ProgramName: Master of Arts in American Culture Studies
Description: The American Culture Studies (AMCS) program at Washington University fosters a multidisciplinary approach to the study of United States history, material culture, social life, literature, politics, arts, and popular culture in local, national, hemispheric, and global contexts. The program prioritizes a hemispheric approach that explores US relations with Latin America, Canada, and Indigenous nations. It also emphasizes experiential and site-based learning, offering opportunities to work with St. Louis communities and organizations. Students are encouraged to shape their study around questions that matter to them, such as critical ethnic and Indigenous studies, environmental and racial justice, media and politics, and education and equity. [2, 4, 5]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Anthropology
Requirements: Applications must be submitted online to the Office of Graduate Studies in Arts & Sciences. Required Materials: ONLINE application form submitted through the SLATE application system that includes the following: 3 letters of recommendation uploaded electronically through the SLATE application system. Recommendation requests should be sent to recommenders via email through the SLATE application system. Transcripts from all institutions of higher learning attended are required. [2]
Fees: Full tuition remission for admitted PhD students. [11]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Applied Health Behavior Research
Requirements: To be considered for admission, applicants must submit the following: AHBR application, Application fee, Résumé/curriculum vitae, Personal statement, All college transcripts, and three letters of recommendation. [1] Registration is open to anyone with a four-year undergraduate degree from an accredited university or college in an appropriate field of study. [1] The GRE is not required for admission. [1, 4]
Concentration: ['Health Education, Program Planning and Evaluation (HEPPE)', 'Health Behavior Research (HBR)']
Description: The Master of Science (MS) in Applied Health Behavior Research (AHBR) is a 33-credit multidisciplinary program that focuses on the applied skills required for the development, management and evaluation of research studies and health behavior programs in academic, clinical and community settings. [1] Students choose one of two concentrations: Health Education, Program Planning and Evaluation (HEPPE): This concentration is designed for individuals who want to develop, manage and evaluate health programs in clinical or community settings. [1] Course work focuses on health behavior theory, program planning, program evaluation, health education and program management. [1] Health Behavior Research (HBR): This concentration is designed for individuals to develop theoretical knowledge and gain practical research experience in order to pursue careers in a variety of health-related fields and/or to manage research studies in clinical settings. [1] Course work focuses on health behavior theory, research methodology, analytic methods and research project management. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Art History and Archaeology
Requirements: To apply for admission to the Washington University GSAS, you must submit the following information: a completed on-line application and statement of purpose; three letters of recommendation (may be submitted on-line); official transcripts from all previously attended colleges or universities; official TOEFL scores for international students who did not obtain their BA from a university in the United States; and a writing sample (15-20 pages; a seminar paper, for example). [1]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Art History and Archaeology
Requirements: The application for the PhD program in Art History and Archaeology requires a completed online application and a statement of purpose. [3] Applicants must also submit three letters of recommendation, official transcripts from all previously attended colleges or universities (though unofficial transcripts are accepted at the initial stage), and a writing sample. [3] International students who did not earn their bachelor's degree from a U.S. university are required to submit official TOEFL scores. [3]
Fees: Students accepted into the PhD program receive full tuition remission. [8]
Fees.1: Full-time tuition for the 2025-26 academic year is $66,850, which is fully covered by the fellowship for PhD students. [16, 8]
Concentration: ['African Art and Archaeology', 'Ancient Mediterranean Art and Archaeology', 'Asian Art', 'Early Modern and European and Global Art and Architecture', 'Modern and Contemporary Art']
Description: The Department of Art History and Archaeology has a long tradition of training students in a wide range of areas; current faculty specialize in African Art and Archaeology, Ancient Mediterranean Art and Archaeology, Asian Art, Early Modern and European and Global Art and Architecture, and Modern and Contemporary Art. Through our relations with the Sam Fox School of Design &Visual arts we have additional strengths in visual art and design, and in the history, theory and practice of architecture. Our program currently has about 20 graduate students in residence, pursuing both the MA and PhD degrees. We welcome students interested in working at either level, and due to our relatively small size, we are able to mentor our graduate students closely and help prepare them for exciting professional opportunities.
ScholarshipAmount: Students accepted into the PhD program who remain in good standing are guaranteed six years of full funding. This includes an annual stipend and full tuition remission. [6, 8] Additional research grants of up to $5,000 are also available. [18]

ProgramName: Doctor of Audiology
Requirements:
Required application materials (all submitted online through application link above):

Online application form
Personal statement
Resume or CV
Brief asynchronous video interview (AuD and MSDE only)
Uploaded unofficial transcripts from all college/university coursework
Three letters of recommendation
Non-refundable application fee of $25
Description: The Doctor of Audiology (AuD) program at Washington University in St. Louis is a three-year course of study designed to prepare students as independent clinical audiologists. [7] The program, part of the Program in Audiology & Communication Sciences (PACS) at the School of Medicine, emphasizes hands-on learning, coursework from experts, and the integration of current research. [7, 5] Operating within the Department of Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery, it offers students an exceptional interdisciplinary learning environment. [7] From the start, students are involved in clinical experiences, lab activities, and have access to clinical learning labs. [7] The curriculum integrates coursework, clinical experiences, and research opportunities, culminating in a capstone project and a full-time clinical externship in the third year. [7] All students receive research training, and a research specialization track is available. [7]
Accredidation: The Doctor of Audiology (AuD) education program in audiology (residential) at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation (CAA) in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA), 2200 Research Blvd. #310, Rockville, MD 20850, (800) 498-2071 or (301) 296-5700. [10]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biochemistry, Biophysics, and Structural Biology
Requirements: The application for the Division of Biology & Biomedical Sciences (DBBS) requires the following components: contact information, demographics, indication of the DBBS program of interest, three letters of recommendation, academic history, and two DBBS-specific essays. [16] A 25-word description of current and/or recent research experience is also part of the application. [16] The GRE General Test is neither required nor accepted for admission. [16] For international applicants who are non-native English speakers, an English proficiency test (TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo) is required. [16] Admissions committees conduct a holistic review of applications, assessing coursework, grades, letters of recommendation, and essay responses. [25] Competitive applicants typically have an average of 12 months of cumulative laboratory research experience and a GPA between 3.0 and 4.0. [25]
Department: Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences (DBBS)
Fees.1: All PhD students in the DBBS are provided with a full-tuition scholarship.
Description: The  BBS Program brings together scientists who aim to understand biological systems ranging from single molecules to whole organisms at the level of chemical transformations and molecular interactions. Our students investigate diverse topics including protein dynamics, the molecular mechanisms of nucleic acid and cytoskeletal motors, membrane-bound ion channels, metabolic enzymes, immunological signaling, and much more. Learning more about how these molecules function leads to insights into a variety of biological contexts including host-pathogen interactions, cancer, metabolic regulation, immunological signaling, DNA-repair, and muscle function to name a few. [2]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biology and Biomedical Sciences
Requirements: A complete application includes: the application form, a statement of purpose, a resume or curriculum vitae, transcripts, and three letters of recommendation.
Department: Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology & Biomedical Sciences
Fees.1: All admitted students receive a full tuition waiver. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: $50,460/year stipend for the 2025-2026 academic year

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: Applicants to the MS BMEN program must meet the following criteria: Academic Background: A bachelor's degree in biomedical engineering or a related field (e.g., electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, biology or physics). Students with non-engineering backgrounds may need to complete prerequisite courses. GPA: A minimum GPA of 3.00 or better on a 4.00 scale. [2]
Fees.1: $66,850 per year for full-time students (9-21 units). [5, 26] For students enrolled in 8 or fewer units, the cost is $2,785 per unit. [5]
Description: Biomedical engineering combines intensive training in research methods, techniques, and practical skills with a solid science and engineering curriculum that provides breadth and depth in the field. A key aspect of biomedical engineering is its interdisciplinary nature; introductory courses in mathematics, biology, chemistry and physics, and foundation/concentration courses build the basis for creating the synergy among these disciplines that is required in the practice of biomedical engineering. [2]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: Applicants must have a grade point average of 3.0 or better in the last 60 semester credit hours of coursework with a major in a recognized science or engineering discipline. [3] All students should have had sufficient background in engineering, chemistry, biology, and physics prior to being admitted to the program. [3] It is expected that these students will have bachelor of science degrees with emphasis in either engineering, physical science, or biological science disciplines. [3] All students are required to have completed at least 1 year of engineering (calculus-based) physics, 1 year of chemistry, 1 year of biology, and mathematics up to Differential Equations or Engineering Analysis I. [3]
Concentration: ['Biomedical & Biological Imaging', 'Cardiovascular Engineering', 'Cellular & Molecular Bioengineering', 'Neural Engineering', 'Orthopedic Engineering', 'Regenerative Engineering in Medicine', "Women's Health Technologies"]
Description: Students pursuing a doctorate in biomedical engineering at Washington University in St. Louis will pursue research in one of seven interdisciplinary research programs that represent frontier areas of biomedical engineering and leverage strengths of our faculty and resources. [2] Our core faculty and more than 130 affiliated faculty work together in interdisciplinary research centers and pathways offering students the opportunity to learn in a diverse and rich spectrum of biomedical engineering research areas. [2] The doctoral degree requires a minimum of 72 credits beyond the bachelor's level, with a minimum of 36 being course credits (including the core curriculum) and a minimum of 24 credits of doctoral dissertation research. [3, 7] Students graduating with the PhD in Biomedical Engineering are prepared to pursue paths in research and development in academic and industry settings, and they are also ready to contribute to teaching and research translation. [7]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Business Analytics
Requirements: Admission is competitive. The Olin Admissions Committee carefully reviews each applicant on a number of factors, looking for individuals with strong academic ability, professional potential, leadership qualities, and communication and interpersonal skills. Each entering class is shaped by students with varied backgrounds, experiences, talents, and interests. You must have completed an undergraduate degree from an accredited institution (comparable to Washington University's four-year bachelor's degree) at the time of enrollment. Required documents include a complete online application, a one-page resume, a required personal statement, a required career essay, and unofficial academic transcripts. [11]
Concentration: ['Accounting Analytics', 'Customer Analytics', 'Fintech Analytics', 'Healthcare Analytics', 'Supply Chain Analytics', 'Talent Analytics']
Description: In the three-semester Master of Science in Business Analytics (MSA) program at Olin, we prepare students for today's world of big data. By combining technical programming skills with a rigorous approach to business problem-solving, MSA students gain the tools and the confidence needed coalitions to extract strategic insights from vast storehouses of data. Across every industry, businesses are collecting data — from retail inventory records to hospital patient data to credit card transactions and more — and relying on skilled analysts to stay ahead of business trends, build forecasts, and drive creative solutions to business problems.
Accredidation: Olin Business School has earned accreditation from the EFMD Quality Improvement System (EQUIS), the Association of MBAs (AMBA) and the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). [3]

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration
Fees.1: $36,375/Semester
Concentration: ['Brand & Product Management', 'Business Analytics', 'Consulting', 'Corporate Finance', 'Entrepreneurship', 'Financial Technology', 'The Business of Health', 'Leadership & Human Capital Management', 'Marketing Analytics', 'Operations & Supply Chain Management', 'Private Capital & Strategic Ownership', 'Wealth & Asset Management']
Description: Washington University's Olin Business School MBA represents a powerful blend of analytical rigor, personalized leadership development, and strong corporate integration within the United States business education landscape. [16] Located in St. Louis, a growing innovation and logistics hub, the program benefits from proximity to Fortune 500 corporations, healthcare enterprises, technology startups, and global supply chain networks. [16] Olin's emphasis on data-driven decision-making, experiential learning, and collaborative leadership positions graduates for high-impact roles across consulting, analytics, operations, finance, and technology-driven industries. [16] The curriculum integrates foundational management disciplines with advanced analytical capability. [16] Core courses establish strong grounding in finance, accounting, marketing, operations management, economics, organizational behavior, strategy, and business analytics. [16] Elective offerings enable specialization across business analytics, supply chain optimization, entrepreneurship, healthcare management, corporate finance, and digital transformation. [16] The STEM-oriented analytical emphasis strengthens graduates' quantitative reasoning and technological fluency, making them competitive for data-driven leadership roles. [16] Experiential learning plays a central role in skill development. [16] Consulting practicums, real-world client projects, simulations, and global immersion modules expose students to complex business challenges. [16]
Accredidation: Olin Business School has earned triple accreditation from the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), the Association of MBAs (AMBA), and the EFMD Quality Improvement System (EQUIS). [5, 9]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Business Administration
Requirements: A complete PhD application should include the following: Scanned copies of transcripts from all colleges and universities attended (uploaded in the application), Scanned copies of either GMAT or GRE score report (pdf uploaded in the application), Scanned copies of TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, GATEWAY, or Duolingo English Test score reports (pdf uploaded in the application), Three (3) letters of recommendation, Essay Questions (considered Statement of Purpose), Resume/CV, and an Application fee paid online. [2]
Fees: Full tuition remission is provided to students who receive the stipend for up to five years. [28]
Fees.1: Full tuition remission is provided to students who receive the stipend for up to five years. [28]
Concentration: ['Accounting', 'Business Economics', 'Finance', 'Marketing', 'Organizational Behavior', 'Strategy and Entrepreneurship', 'Supply Chain, Operations and Technology']
Description: Washington University's Olin Business School is one of the nation's leading research institutions, with a faculty whose research productivity consistently ranks among the highest in the business school community. Olin faculty members are recognized the world over for their important contributions to the creation of new knowledge, and they take great pride in their commitment to excellence in teaching. Olin PhD students are guided by highly productive researchers who are among the nation's top scholars. [12] Faculty work closely with students to help them hone their research skills, often building one-on-one mentoring relationships that include the co-authoring of research papers. [12] The development of strong problem-solving skills equips students to strategically address complex, unstructured business issues that result in innovative thinking and new ideas for research that have value to the academic community and application in the business world. [12]
Accredidation: Olin Business School is accredited by the three most recognized business school accreditation organizations: AACSB International, AMBA, and EQUIS. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: The annual stipend amount for the 2025-2026 academic year is $37,000.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Cancer Biology
Requirements: The Division of Biology & Biomedical Sciences (DBBS) employs a holistic approach to admissions, considering the entirety of the application. Applications are reviewed by committees of faculty members who assess coursework, grades, letters of recommendation, and essay responses using an NIH-style rubric. Competitive candidates typically have an average of 12 months of cumulative laboratory research experience and a GPA in the range of 3.0 to 4.0. [9] The application requires three letters of recommendation from research mentors, faculty advisors, and/or employers. [7] Instead of a traditional statement of purpose, applicants must respond to two specific essay prompts. DBBS does not accept a CV or personal statement in place of these essays. [7]
Department: Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences
ScholarshipType: All admitted PhD students receive a financial support package that includes a full tuition waiver and a stipend.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: A total of 30 required credits for coursework only or 24 credits + 6 credits research for research project and thesis options). Core courses include Transport Phenomena in Energy, Environmental and Chemical Engineering and Mathematical Methods in Engineering. Applicants should have a bachelor's degree in engineering, physical sciences, or life sciences. A minimum GPA of 2.75 is required for graduation.
ScholarshipType: Limited fellowships and research assistantships are available for full-time master's students.

ProgramName: Doctor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: Before beginning the application, please review the checklist items for details on required materials. All eligible applicants must have earned or will have earned an undergraduate degree by the start of their graduate program. Applications close at 11:59PM EST on the application deadline. An application will not be reviewed until the application has been submitted electronically and all required payments and supplemental materials have been received. [2]
Fees.1: PhD students are fully funded, including full tuition support and health insurance.
Concentration: ['Aerosol Science & Engineering', 'Engineered Aquatics Processes', 'Metabolic Engineering and Systems Biology']
Description: The Department of Energy, Environmental & Chemical Engineering at Washington University in St. Louis offers a PhD program that brings together an interdisciplinary group of faculty to address global challenges related to energy, environment, and health. The program provides integrated and multi-disciplinary scientific education in advanced areas. The research and educational activities are organized into clusters: Aerosol Science & Engineering, Engineered Aquatics Processes, and Metabolic Engineering and Systems Biology. [2] The typical educational background for admitted students is a degree in chemical, biomolecular, material, or environmental engineering, but the interdisciplinary nature of the research also accommodates students with backgrounds in chemical, atmospheric, and biological sciences, as well as other engineering fields. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: The minimum PhD financial support rate for the 2025-26 academic year is $37,853 annually.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry
Requirements: Requirements for the Chemistry PhD include: 72 units of graduate credit in courses and research; Incoming graduate students will be required to take proficiency exams to help advisors plan a student's first-year courses and teaching assignments; Satisfactory performance on oral cumulative examinations; Satisfactory performance on a pre-thesis research proposal and defense; Satisfactory performance on annual pre-thesis committee meetings; Demonstration of teaching competence; Dissertation research and preparation of a dissertation; Satisfactory performance on a final oral dissertation defense. [6, 19]
Description: The Department of Chemistry offers a PhD in Chemistry that prepares scientists for careers in research and teaching. The program offers pathways for graduate studies that span biological, organic, inorganic, physical, and nuclear chemistry. [3] Key to the success of the students and the Chemistry PhD program is the strong interpersonal connections that develop between our students and the faculty and that often lead to new research directions and bridges being built between disciplines. [3] As a result, doctoral students commonly pursue research at the interface of two or more subfields of chemistry. [3] Our department is made up of a close-knit group of teacher-scientists who provide a superior education in chemistry. Our students gain a strong foundation in the core areas of chemistry: organic, physical, inorganic, nuclear, and theoretical. [12] Special emphases in the department include emerging interdisciplinary fields as organometallic, bioorganic, biophysical, macromolecular, polymer, environmental, and materials chemistry. [12]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Chinese
Requirements: Applicants must submit transcripts from all undergraduate and/or graduate institutions attended. Unofficial transcripts should be uploaded at the time of application. Official transcripts will be required if an offer of admission is made. Three letters of recommendation are required, in English and submitted via the online application system. International applicants must submit their scores on the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or IELTS scores.
Description: In the fifth decade of its growth, the graduate programs in Chinese at Washington University offer in-depth training in Chinese literature with the option for a second field in another East Asian literature or in Chinese studies in another discipline. The research strengths of the internationally-recognized faculty include premodern poetry, religious and women's writings, narrative and dramatic literature of the late imperial period, and modern and contemporary literature from greater China. [10] Research areas cover book culture, gender questions, popular culture, translation theory and practice, and globalization and cosmopolitanism. [10] Students in the programs take a combination of advanced courses and seminars in Chinese literature, literary theory and analysis to enhance their investigative skills, and Chinese history and other fields to strengthen their grasp of the contexts in which literature was historically written and read. [10]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chinese and Comparative Literature
Requirements: Applicants must submit transcripts from all undergraduate and/or graduate institutions attended. Unofficial transcripts should be uploaded at the time of application. Official transcripts will be required if an offer of admission is made. Three letters of recommendation in English are to be submitted via the online application system. A personal statement, 2-3 pages in length, is also required. International applicants must submit their scores on the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or IELTS. [9]
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Chinese and Comparative Literature is a program offered jointly with the Comparative Literature program. Its focus is on the comparison of the contents, theoretical foundations, and methodologies of Chinese literature and a second literature, which can be Western or non-Western. This is done within the context of understanding the cultural and historical backgrounds of these literatures, as well as the critical and historical methods of modern literary study. [3] The program aims to provide a strong foundation in all periods and forms of Chinese literature, along with a focused area of research that can be supplemented with China-related courses from various departments such as Anthropology, Art History and Archaeology, Film and Media Studies, History, Religious Studies, and the School of Law. [7] It balances the theory and history of Chinese literature and culture and offers chances for interdisciplinary research. [7] Students are encouraged to focus on the literature and culture, including visual culture, from the late imperial period to the early 21st century, in line with the faculty's strengths. [7]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Classics
Requirements: The completed application form. Please be sure to include your years of Greek and Latin study, in addition to any other languages you have studied, in the section on language preparation. The Classics Admissions Committee looks for MA applicants to have the equivalent of (minimum) two years each of college-level Greek and Latin. For the purposes of initial review of applications, the Classics Admissions Committee accepts unofficial transcripts (inclusive of all undergraduate and postgraduate coursework) be uploaded to the application system. Three letters of recommendation. A personal statement of 1-2 pages. A scholarly writing sample of ca. 15 pages, representing your work on a topic in Classics or a related field. The ideal submission makes use of both secondary sources and ancient text(s) in the original.
Description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Classics is ideal preparation either for the PhD or for a career in secondary teaching, and it has a strong placement record in both areas. The program provides rigorous instruction in Greek and Latin languages and literatures, exposure to the subfields of Classics, opportunities to cultivate special fields of research, and teaching experience in departmental courses. [10] Students in the MA program work toward increased language proficiency, a deeper knowledge of Greek and Roman culture, literature, and history, and research experience. They are mentored by faculty with diverse specialties within the field and have opportunities to take courses in affiliated fields such as Comparative Literature, Philosophy, and Art History & Archaeology. [3] The Department of Classics is committed to the threefold study of Greco-Roman antiquity via its languages and literatures, its history, and its art and architectural remains. [10] Candidates may obtain an MA degree in Classics by completing 36 graduate units of credit, completing a reading list, and taking a series of examinations. [11]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Clinical Investigation
Requirements: Seven items are needed for a complete application: Application form; Current Biosketch or CV; Individual Development Plan – including a course plan; Research Plan; Mentor Letter of Support; Department Chair or Division Chief Recommendation Letter; Official Transcripts. [7] Candidates must have completed a Bachelor's degree. [7] Eligible applicants must be citizens, non-citizen nationals, permanent residents, or hold a valid US visa and a postdoctoral appointment at Washington University or one of the ICTS affiliates. [7] All applicants must be conducting clinical and translational research. [7] Applicants must have an established relationship with a senior faculty member prior to beginning the MSCI Program. [7]
Description: The Master of Science in Clinical Investigation (MSCI) at WashU Medicine is an innovative, 33-credit program that provides scholars with the necessary skills and knowledge to excel in clinical research and the academic environment. Housed in the Clinical Research Training Center, the MSCI is the largest master's degree program at WashU Medicine. The MSCI student body represents over 15 different departments and 45 divisions within WashU Medicine. WashU Medicine has awarded over 200 MSCI degrees since 2006. [3] The MSCI combines didactic coursework with a substantive research project, weekly seminars, and a formal mentorship program. [3] Scholars gain knowledge in the core competencies of clinical research and investigation, including study design, research implementation, statistical analysis, scientific communication, literature critique, leadership, Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) and rigor and reproducibility, as well as opportunities for community engagement relevant to MDs, PhDs, and doctoral students from various disciplines. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Clinical Research Management
Requirements: The Master of Science in Clinical Research Management is designed for experienced professionals working in academic research centers or private industry who seek greater depth and breadth of study in the science and business of clinical research. [8] Candidates for this master degree program typically hold or aspire toward leadership positions in academic research centers or related private sector organizations. [8] Likely candidates from academic research settings include clinical research investigators, coordinators, nurses, and sponsor representatives. [8] Private sector candidates include pharmaceutical industry project managers, monitors, and regulatory affairs staff, as well as staff in community physician offices and independent research agencies. [8]
Description: The Master of Science in Clinical Research Management is designed for experienced professionals working in academic research centers or private industry who seek greater depth and breadth of study in the science and business of clinical research. [3, 8] The curriculum encompasses in-depth coverage of essential skills and processes required for the management of studies that develop drugs, devices and treatment protocols for patient care. [2, 3] Major topics include regulatory requirements, ethical issues, product development, the business of clinical research, grant funding and manuscripts, epidemiologic principles and tools, research design, and data analysis, all in the context of human subjects in clinical trials. [2, 3]

[4]
Description: The Master of Science (MS) in Computer Engineering is best suited for students who are looking to focus on computer engineering (hardware) aspects. [13] The MS in Computer Engineering program can be a pure course option program, or it can incorporate either a project or a thesis. [13] If appropriate research experiences are included in the degree option, this can also lead toward future doctoral studies. [13] All students in the MS in Computer Engineering program must have previously completed (as documented by their undergraduate transcript), successfully test to place out of, or complete at the start of their program the following courses: CSE 1301 Introduction to Computer Science and CSE 2600 Introduction to Digital Logic and Computer Design (or equivalent courses offered at other institutions). [13] The Master of Science in Computer Engineering degree is jointly administered by the Department of Computer Science & Engineering (CSE) and the Department of Electrical & Systems Engineering (ESE). [7]
Accredidation: Washington University in St. Louis has been accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC) since 1913. [14] The Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering has not requested to be reviewed by ABET, but accreditation information for the Master of Science in Computer Engineering program is not mentioned on the official website. [14]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree, or equivalent, before enrolling. [18] A completed online application form and a non-refundable application fee are required. [14] Unofficial transcripts from all post-secondary institutions must be uploaded, with official transcripts required upon an offer of admission. [14] Three letters of recommendation are necessary for the application. [17] International applicants must report official English Proficiency test scores, with certain exemptions available. [17] All students in the MS in Computer Science program must have previously completed, successfully tested out of, or completed at the start of their program courses in Introduction to Computer Science and Data Structures and Algorithms. [12]
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition remission

ProgramName: Master of Science in Construction Management
Requirements: The Master of Architecture + Master of Construction Management (MArch+MCM) joint degree program prepares architectural students for the diverse roles within today's multidisciplinary design and construction process. Architecture students enrolled at the Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts can earn a MArch +MCM degree in considerably less time than pursuing each degree separately. [11]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Control Engineering
Requirements: All eligible applicants must have earned or will have earned an undergraduate degree by the start of their graduate program. [1] Applications require electronic copies of transcripts from all attended institutions, three letters of recommendation, a resume, and a statement of purpose. [3, 1]
Description: The Master of Science in Systems Science & Mathematics (MSSSM) at Washington University in St. Louis is an academic degree for students interested in pursuing a doctoral program or a professional career in industry. [2] The program focuses on an approach that treats a system of components as a whole rather than a collection of individual parts. [2] It is a modern and rapidly developing field in applied mathematics and engineering. [2] Students in the program study the identification, modeling, analysis, design, and control of complex systems. [2, 9] The program offers both a course option and a thesis or project option, requiring 30 credit units for completion. [3]
ScholarshipPercentage: 50% for the final year of the Bachelor's/Master's program

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Creative Writing
Requirements: Applicants must follow standard Office of Graduate Studies procedures and apply online. The online application will allow you to submit the following material: Application Fee, Applicant Information Form, Transcripts, 3 Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Writing Sample, Curriculum Vitae. [8]
Fees.1: Full tuition waiver
Description: The MFA Program at Washington University in St. Louis is a two-year program focused on MFA degrees in fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction. [9] The program is designed to be rigorous and challenging, fostering a close-knit community of support that extends beyond graduation. [14] At its core are workshops in fiction, creative nonfiction, and poetry, supplemented by craft courses in all genres and access to literature courses within the department and other courses in the College of Arts & Sciences. [14] The program culminates in the completion of a thesis, which is typically a volume of poems, a collection of short stories, a novel, a collection of essays, or a book-length nonfiction manuscript, and an oral examination focused on the thesis. [14] The program requires the satisfactory completion of 42 semester hours. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: A stipend sufficient for students to live comfortably is provided.
ScholarshipType: A&S Fellowship, Ann W. and Spencer T. Olin-Chancellor's Fellowship (OCF)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Cybersecurity Engineering
Requirements: Applicants should have a baccalaureate degree in computer science, software engineering, or an equivalent technically‐deep software‐oriented equivalent discipline from an institution of recognized standing. [1] Degrees or significant work experience in information technology, electrical engineering, or other related disciplines may also be suitable. [1] Applications will be evaluated on an individual basis by the department's graduate admission committee. [1]
Description: The Master of Science in Cybersecurity Engineering give students the skills, knowledge and expertise to work in the rapidly growing field of cybersecurity and design, engineer, and architect cybersecurity technology and systems. Cybersecurity has been and continues to be one of the most growth-oriented career fields in the computer science domain. Graduates of this program will be equipped with the theoretical and hands-on engineering expertise to solve complex cybersecurity problems affecting diverse enterprises worldwide.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Dance
Description: The Master of Fine Arts in Dance Program a leading-research university our MFA candidates have access to a breadth of resources to pursue opportunities that stretch the boundaries of how dance contributes to global intellectual and creative endeavors. We welcome returning professionals seeking to transition into higher education, outstanding recent undergraduates, and artists at all stages hoping to deepen their practice through three years of rigorous study. The overarching goal of this program is to develop each student’s personal artistic practice while encountering a global perspective on dance studies, performance, pedagogy, and choreography.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Data Analytics and Applications
Requirements: It is recommended that incoming students earn a baccalaureate degree in engineering or another STEM-related degree. In earning that degree, it is recommended that students take the following upper-level courses: Calculus Sequence and Differential Equations, Probability and Statistics, Matrix Algebra, and Introductory Computer Science. More advanced topics in Computer Science such as Data Structures are also helpful, but may be added after admission to the program.
Department: McKelvey School of Engineering's Sever Institute and WashU Continuing & Professional Studies (CAPS)
Description: Data is an essential component of many industries, and creating meaningful insights from the information pulled from that data can lead to better processes and outcomes. If a professional is looking to advance their career in this field, the Master of Data Analytics & Applications will provide the knowledge base and expertise they need to construct data systems that improve efficiencies and profit margins for organizations. [2, 5] Offered in collaboration between the McKelvey School of Engineering's Sever Institute and WashU Continuing & Professional Studies (CAPS), this flexible online program will help working professionals acquire the skills they need to advance in a data-driven environment. [2, 5] In this program, modern learners will acquire relevant and practical knowledge of the data analytics and applications field, improve their critical thinking and communication skills, and develop the leadership acumen needed to be successful in demanding senior management roles. [6, 5] This program can be completed entirely online. [2, 5]
ScholarshipType: Limited fellowship and research assistantship opportunities, Federal Student Aid (grants, loans, work-study)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Deaf Education
Requirements: Applicants for the Master of Science in Deaf Education must apply to and meet all criteria for admission to the Graduate School and all college requirements for admission and retention. [1] Individuals applying for admission to the Master of Science in Deaf Education must meet the following admission requirements: Bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university in the United States, or equivalent from a school in anot her country. [1] Grade point average of 3.0 or higher for all upper-division credits taken at the undergraduate level. Three letters of recommendation. [1] Interview with program faculty. Letter of Intent stating the desired option. [1] Proof of teaching certification for this option. The deadlines for submission of applications are July 15 (Fall Semester), November 15 (Spring Semester) and April 15 (Summer Semester). [1] Completed application, including personal statement. [2] Application fee (non-refundable) of $25. Transcripts (official or unofficial) from all college/university coursework, uploaded to the online application. [2] Official scores from the GRE, submitted to Institution Code 6929 (Washington University), Department Code 0602 (Audiology). [2]
Description: The The early identification of hearing loss and advanced hearing technologies have increased the national need for professionals with experience in listening and spoken language to work in early intervention and as teachers of the d/hh, creating opportunities for our graduates across the country and in a wide variety of settings. [4] With origins dating back to 1914, the program is recognized internationally as one of the most prestigious of its kind. [4] Our program's intensive curriculum, emphasis on immersion in practice teaching, and experienced faculty attract students nationally from a wide variety of backgrounds. [4] Two curriculum paths are available: The Certification Track is a four-semester curriculum that is rooted in the development of speech, language, and academics. [4] With that as a foundation, students study the factors necessary for high-quality education for children who are d/hh. [4] The Degree-Only Track is a two-semester intensive curriculum that provides advanced education and experience in deaf education. [4] This track is designed for qualified students with a degree and teacher certification in deaf education and for related professionals seeking to expand their training in deaf education. [4]
Accredidation: The WashU Medicine's MSDE (Certification Track) program is accredited by the Missouri Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE) and the Council on Education of the Deaf (CED). [11] The MSDE (Certification Track) program is recognized by DESE as an approved teacher training program, leading to initial teacher certification in the area of Deaf/Hard of Hearing (Birth-Grade 12). [11]

ProgramName: PhD Concentration in Dissemination and Implementation Science
Requirements: Students entering the PhD program must have a master's degree or equivalent in public health or a related discipline from an accredited college or university. [10] Applicants are required to demonstrate successful completion of a master's degree (or degree in-progress) in public health or a related discipline from a regionally accredited college or university. [10] Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended must be submitted directly to SOPHAS. [10] Three (3) letters of recommendation from professional and/or academic colleagues are required. [10]
Department: School of Public Health, Brown School
Fees.1: All students in the Public Health Sciences doctoral program receive full tuition remission. [2] All Social Work students admitted into the Brown School's doctoral program receive a financial package that consists of tuition coverage and five years of stipend support. [6]
Concentration: Dissemination and Implementation Science PhD Concentration
Description: The Dissemination and Implementation Science (D&I) doctoral concentration provides an opportunity for students interested in the transdisciplinary field to complete relevant coursework and mentored research. [1] The concentration aims to prepare next-generation public health and social work scholars for D&I competencies such as describing the objectives of D&I research for promoting health and addressing health equity, critically evaluating D&I theories, models, and frameworks, assessing the need for and process of adapting and tailoring interventions and D&I research strategies, designing studies that incorporate innovative and emerging methods and measures in D&I research, and describing the importance and methods for incorporating the perspectives of different partners in D&I. [1, 2] PhD students concentrate in D&I by completing D&I-related coursework, getting involved in the various D&I research training opportunities at Washington University, and conducting mentored dissertation research that contributes to the field. [1] The successful defense of the D&I dissertation is recorded in the student's final academic transcript. [1]
ScholarshipAmount: 37835/year

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Earth and Planetary Sciences
Requirements: Complete applications for admission, including all mandatory supporting documents, are required to ensure full consideration for fall admission. Please submit all supporting documents through the online application portal. These supporting documents include: Three recommendation letters; Statement of purpose*; Resume or C.V.; Transcripts of all previous undergraduate and graduate college; Test scores* (not required). [2]
Description: The graduate program in Earth and Planetary Sciences is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching in the broad field of the Earth and planetary sciences. The program provides students with a broad-based background in the geosciences, as well as the deep knowledge in a particular specialty required to perform original research. Students will learn how to design and execute experiments or conduct theoretical studies, how to analyze and interpret data, and how to communicate their results effectively. The program is tailored to the individual student’s interests and background.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in East Asian Studies
Doctor of Philosophy in Economics
Requirements: Applicants must present evidence of a baccalaureate degree or its equivalent, or show that they can expect such a degree by the time they begin graduate work. [4] Three letters of recommendation are also required, usually from professors who can judge the student's potential for high-quality academic work. [4] Results of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) must also be submitted. [4]
Description: The PhD in Economics at Washington University in St. Louis is designed for students with strong analytical abilities in mathematics and statistics who are seeking to complete a challenging doctoral degree. [10] The program aims to prepare high-quality PhD students for academic positions and for jobs in the private and public sectors. [10] The curriculum takes five years to complete and requires at least 30 units of 5000-level courses with a 3.0 grade point average. [9] Students must qualify to advance to the dissertation stage in three core fields: microeconomics, macroeconomics, and econometrics. [7, 9] This qualification can be achieved by earning a grade of A- or higher in the first-year coursework or by passing a qualifying exam. [7, 9] The Department of Economics emphasizes the development of analytical models and their application to important economic, social, and political issues. [8]
Accredidation: Washington University in St. Louis has been accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC) since 1913. [3] The HLC is an institutional accreditor recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. [3] In addition to university-wide accreditation, various professional schools at the university are accredited by their respective professional organizations. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Education
Description: The Master of Arts in Education (MAEd) at Washington University in St. Louis is offered as a dual degree program with the Master of Social Work (MSW) from the Brown School. It is not available as a standalone degree and must be completed within the 3-year dual-degree program. [11] The program is designed to prepare graduates for careers in education and social service-related activities within school systems. [5] The Educational Studies track provides a comprehensive understanding of the historical, social, and political context of K-12 education, preparing students for roles in policy, advocacy, and research at various levels. [5] The curriculum combines social work training, which addresses the psychosocial needs of children and families, with educational studies that focus on the broader issues within the U.S. education system. [5] Graduates are equipped to address both the social and emotional needs of students and their academic achievement. [5, 10] The program requires a total of 88 credit units to complete. [5]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Electrical Engineering is an academic master's degree designed mainly for both full-time and part-time students interested in proceeding to the departmental full-time doctoral program and/or an industrial career. [18] The program includes elective courses, enabling students to individually tailor their programs to provide emphasis in a particular specialization. [2] Areas of study include power systems, power electronics, electronics, control systems, computer engineering and communication systems. [2] The program has a thesis and non-thesis options. [2] Students pursuing the degree must complete a minimum of 30 credit hours of study consistent with the residency and other applicable requirements of Washington University in St. Louis and the McKelvey School of Engineering. [4]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: All eligible applicants must have earned or will have earned an undergraduate degree by the start of their graduate program. [4] A baccalaureate degree in engineering or the physical sciences/mathematics is required. [3] With few exceptions, admitted PhD/DSc students typically have had grade point averages of at least 3.5 out of 4.0. [3] An application will not be reviewed until it has been submitted electronically and all required payments and supplemental materials have been received. [4] Three (3) letters of recommendation are required. [4]

[2] You'll be required to complete a minimum of 72 credit hours of post-baccalaureate study consistent with the residency and other applicable requirements of Washington University in St. Louis and the Graduate School. [2] These 72 units must consist of at least 36 units of course work and at least 24 units of research, and may include work done to satisfy the requirements of a master's degree in a related discipline. [2]
CostPerCredit: $2,785/unit (applies to PhD students enrolled in 8 or fewer units, though tuition is covered by funding). [4]
MinimumGreScore: Admitted students typically have an average score greater than 90 percent on the quantitative section (new GRE scale) and 3.5 or greater on the analytical section.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition support and a generous stipend to cover living expenses are provided to all full-time PhD students. [2, 5, 9, 18, 20]
ScholarshipType: Full financial support, including tuition remission, health insurance, and a stipend. [2, 5, 9, 18, 20] Specific fellowships such as The Ann W. and Spencer T. Olin – Chancellor's Fellowship and the McDonnell International Scholars Academy are also available. [5]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in English and American Literature
Master of Science in Engineering Management
Concentration: ['Applied Data Analytics Emphasis', 'Computer Science & Security Emphasis', 'Managing, Leading & Innovating Emphasis']
Description: The competitive Master of Engineering Management program bridges the gap between technology and business by providing students with the technical expertise and leadership skills needed to advance their careers. [11] The 30-unit Master of Engineering Management is available for full-time or part-time students. [11] This program brings together Washington University faculty and industry-leading experts to help students learn to strategize, lead, make informed decisions, manage financials, and leverage both existing and emerging technology. [11] The courses prepare individuals to utilize common management tactics across all of the engineering disciplines. [11] Offered through Washington University's Sever Institute at the McKelvey School of Engineering, this nationally-ranked full-time Master of Engineering Management (MEM) graduate degree program will help you advance with the knowledge, leadership and skills needed to understand, shape and lead projects, as well as manage teams, engineering functions and companies. [9] The MEM qualifies as a STEM program. [9]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in French
Description: The Master of Arts in French at Washington University in St. Louis is tailored for students with broad, interdisciplinary academic interests who wish to combine their French studies with coursework from other departments into a cohesive academic plan. [3] The program encourages students to pursue non-traditional outcomes that reflect the core faculty's methodologies and scholarly expertise. [3] Key departmental strengths include Translation Studies, Francophone Studies and French as a Global Language, Cultural History of the Francophone World, Textual Studies, Book History and Digital Humanities, Gender Studies, and Pedagogy and Second Language Acquisition. [3] MA projects can result in outcomes such as a translation, a publishable academic research article, the creation of a digital edition or archive, a public humanities project, an online dictionary, or a bank of teaching resources. [3] Students are strongly encouraged to complement their MA with a Graduate Certificate in areas like Textual and Digital Studies, Secondary and Foreign Language Teaching, Cinema and Media Studies, Public Humanities, Feminist Studies, and Sexuality and Queer Studies. [3] Many MA students receive a Teaching Assistantship, providing them with valuable language teaching experience under the supervision of Second Language Acquisition faculty. [3] The program requires a total of 50 applicable credits to earn the Master of Arts in French. [3] Please note that the program is not accepting applications for the 2025-2026 or 2026-2027 academic years. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in French and Comparative Literature
Requirements: Applicants for graduate programs must have earned a bachelor's degree or its equivalent before enrollment. [2] The application is submitted online, and some supporting documents may need to be sent electronically or by mail. [2] It is important that all application materials are received by the program's deadline. [2] For some programs, an interview may be requested after a review of all application materials. [2]
Fees.1: The PhD program in French and Francophone Studies offers full-tuition scholarships. [9] While a specific dollar amount is not listed for the current year on the program page, a university announcement for the 2018-19 academic year stated the tuition for the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences was $52,400. [10]

This focus is combined with training in approaches, methods, and theories offered by the program in Comparative Literature and articulated by its core requirements. It is expected that students in the dual programs include one or more comparatist elements in their comprehensive examinations and dissertation. [10]
ScholarshipAmount: Currently, all graduate students in the department receive a living stipend of $36,050 and a full tuition scholarship. [9]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Germanic and Comparative Literature
Requirements: Applicants must earn a bachelor's degree, or equivalent, before enrolling in a Graduate program at Washington University in St. Louis. General application materials include an online application, application fee, transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, and letters of recommendation. [2] Specific programs may require additional items such as a resume/CV, statement of purpose, or writing samples. [2]
Concentration: Dual PhD in German and Comparative Literature
Description: The dual PhD degree in German and Comparative Literature requires study of German literature and culture, over the course of which the student virtually duplicates the courses and other preparations expected of a doctoral candidate in the German. Students additionally complete the 12-unit core requirement for the Comparative Literature PhD program, which includes COMPLITTHT 5200: Introduction to Comparative Literature. [3, 4] To earn a PhD at Washington University, a student must complete all courses required by their department; maintain satisfactory academic progress; pass certain examinations; fulfill residence and Mentored Experience Requirements; write, defend, and submit a dissertation; and apply to graduate via Workday Student. [3, 4]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Germanic Languages and Literatures
Requirements: This program is only for graduate exchange students from the University of Cologne. [8]
Concentration: MA in German Studies and Higher Education
Description: The graduate program in Germanic Languages and Literatures comprises a vibrant community of scholars and students dedicated to the advanced study of German-speaking literature and culture in its global contexts, both past and present. Our faculty conduct transformative research that is helping to shape the discipline in the 21st century. Our students enroll in innovative, interdisciplinary seminars, receive exceptional mentoring, and have the opportunity to participate in teaching and internship experiences that will prepare them for careers in academia and beyond. The master's program in German studies and higher education offers qualified students with a strong background in German the opportunity to combine advanced study of German language, literature, and culture with coursework in higher education administration.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Clinical Investigation with a Concentration in Dissemination & Implementation
Requirements: Candidates must have completed a Bachelor's degree. However most scholars are enrolled in a pre- or post-doctoral mentored research program at WashU Medicine or hold a post-doctoral appointment in health science at WashU or one of the ICTS affiliates – SLU, UHSP, and MU. Eligible applicants must be citizens, non-citizen nationals, permanent residents, or hold a valid US visa and a postdoctoral appointment at WashU or one of the ICTS affiliates. [1]
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Clinical Investigation is a 16-credit certificate program for young investigators committed to pursuing academic careers in clinical research. Students will gain knowledge in the core competencies of clinical research and investigation such as study design, research implementation, statistical approaches, responsible conduct of research, scientific communication and literature critique, leadership, and community engagement. [2, 3] On average, scholars complete the certificate requirements within one to two years. [2, 3] All coursework must be successfully completed within five years from the start of the first course. [2, 3] Credits cannot be transferred into the program. [2, 3] The evening course format allows for full or part-time enrollment that can accommodate clinical schedules. [2, 3] The certificate is available in four different tracks: Clinical Investigation, Translational Medicine, Genetics/Genomics, Dissemination and Implementation. [2, 3]
Accredidation: In support of improving patient care, Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis is jointly accredited by the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME), the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE), and the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), to provide continuing education for the healthcare team. [10]
CostPerCredit: $1560 per credit for the 2025-2026 academic year.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Higher Education (on pause as of Fall 2024)
Requirements: Current Washington University doctoral students who are interested in pursuing the Graduate Certificate in Higher Education may begin taking courses pursuant to the Certificate upon entry into the University. [2] Doctoral students interested in pursuing a Graduate Certificate in Higher Education must take a total of 12 total credit hours. [2] Options include taking either four courses or three courses (9 total credit hours) plus engagement in a (3-credit hour) Mentored Experience in Higher Education (MEHE) through the Department of Education. [2]

[3] Students will complete courses in three main areas: Foundations of Education, Assessment, and Evaluation; Diversity and Inclusion in Education; and Critical Issues in Higher Education. [2] Students can choose to take four courses (12 credit hours) or three courses (9 credit hours) along with a 3-credit hour Mentored Experience in Higher Education (MEHE). [3] The MEHE allows students to gain practical experience by working with an administrative or faculty supervisor on projects related to program development, evaluation, or improvement. [3]
Accredidation: Washington University in St. Louis is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). [12] While the university's overall accreditation is mentioned, no specific accreditation for the Graduate Certificate in Higher Education program is listed on the official website. [12, 13]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Hispanic Languages and Literatures
Requirements: In addition to the general Graduate School requirements, the Spanish Section of the Department of Romance Languages and Literatures requires the following materials which should be submitted as part of the Graduate School's online application: Curriculum vitae. Statement of intent (maximum 750 words) Biographical Statement (maximum 750 words) Three letters of recommendation, preferably by professors with whom the candidate has recently studied. Results of GRE (note that the GRE is optional) Results of the TOEFL or IELTS (non-native English speakers) Two writing samples (maximum of 20 pages each). [1]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in History
Fees: Full tuition remission for funded PhD students.
Fees.1: The full-time tuition for the 2025-26 academic year is $66,850. [6] However, the History Department provides full tuition remission for most doctoral candidates. [17]
Description: The graduate program in History at Washington University in St. Louis is committed to training students to do innovative research and supports them in pursuing a variety of careers. [3] Doctoral training is available in any chronological or geographical specialization covered by a tenured faculty member. [3] The program notes particular expertise in the history of Africa, American civil rights, Britain, Central Europe, East Asia, Empire, medieval Europe, and the early modern world. [11] Thematic clusters that draw on the expertise of faculty enable graduate students to bridge conventional historical fields and pursue interdisciplinary research, including areas like imperialism, colonialism, indigeneity; science, medicine, technology, environment; international, transnational, and global history; international urban history; race, ethnicity, and migration; and global early modern. [3] The department funds most doctoral candidates for six years at highly competitive levels and is committed to providing additional financial resources to support advanced research. [3] Most graduate students proceed toward qualification in no more than three years, taking basic and specialized courses while preparing for an exam covering three scholarly fields and developing a dissertation topic. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: An annual stipend of $37,582 for the 2025-2026 academic year is provided for PhD students with Arts & Sciences Fellowships in the Humanities. [26]
ScholarshipType: Most PhD students receive funding that includes full tuition remission and a stipend to cover living expenses. [14, 16] The department also offers travel and research grants. [19]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Human Resources Management
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent before enrolling. Applications are submitted online, and all materials should be received by the program's deadline. General application materials include an application form, application fee, transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions, and letters of recommendation. [2]
Description: Human resources managers are integral parts of the leadership teams charged with directing complex organizations and a diverse workforce. Managing people and organizations requires both functional skills in human resources as well as expertise in strategic planning and organizational development. The Master of Arts in Human Resources Management prepares individuals in a variety of employment settings to join other organizational leaders at the table of decision-makers. [5, 7] The program provides students with skills and information in key operational areas such as human relations and communications, compensation and benefits, training and development, employee and labor relations, and staffing and retention. [5, 7] In addition, the program teaches professionals how to contribute to organizational development, change, risk management and strategic planning. [5, 7]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Immunology
Requirements: Applicants submit a single application to the Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology & Biomedical Sciences (DBBS). The application consists of contact information, demographics, DBBS program of concentration interest, and three letters of recommendation. Instead of a personal statement or CV, applicants must respond to two essay prompts. All applicants must have a US bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. [15]
Department: Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences (DBBS)
Fees: For the 2023-2024 academic year, all full-time students in the Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences receive a full tuition scholarship. While a specific tuition fee for the 'Doctor of Philosophy in Immunology' is not listed, the standard graduate school tuition at Washington University can be substantial, and this scholarship covers the entirety of that cost.
Fees.1: $0 (Tuition is fully covered by a scholarship for all full-time Ph.D. students in the DBBS.)
Description: The Immunology program is a graduate training program at WashU, housed under the Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences (DBBS). [6] Immunology is the discipline of biology that examines the mechanisms of host defense against pathogenic agents. [6] The study of the immune system offers a unique opportunity to analyze a complex multicomponent system consisting of molecules and cells that have documented physiologic relevance. [6] Immunology has a strong foundation in biochemistry, molecular biology, and cell biology. [6] The primary objective of the program is to provide our students with a solid foundation of skills as a scientist overall and specifically in the conduct of immunology research. [6, 9] We recognized our program as a top program in the nation and we aim to retain that standing, along with our reputation for rigor and high standards. [6, 9]
ScholarshipAmount: All full-time Ph.D. students in the DBBS receive a stipend. For the 2023-2024 academic year, the stipend amount is $33,500.
ScholarshipPercentage: 100% of tuition is covered by a scholarship.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in International Affairs
Requirements: Admission to a graduate degree program must include a minimum GPA of a 3.0* or higher on a 4.0 scale, cumulatively, or in the last 60 hours of coursework reflecting completion of a bachelor's degree. Applicants who do not meet the GPA requirement should speak with a CAPS Representative. Transcripts are required from each institution that you have attended and taken courses, received your bachelor's degree, taken post-graduate courses, or where a higher-level degree was conferred. Official transcripts must be sent directly from the school's registrar to CAPS. Electronic transcripts should be forwarded to CAPS@wustl.edu. If the transcript you submit for consideration is from a college or university outside the United States, a course-by-course transcript evaluation is also required. Applicants to a master’s degree program must write a one-page Statement of Intent explaining your interests and goals in your chosen field of study.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Islamic and Near Eastern Studies
Requirements: The MA program in Islamic and Near Eastern Studies requires a minimum of 36 credits from graduate-level courses, which may include up to 6 units transferred from another institution. [13, 15, 16] Admission to the program normally requires proficiency in the Arabic language equivalent to one year of college-level study. [12] Students are expected to have successfully completed third-year Arabic before receiving the MA degree. [12] The program requires the completion of two major research papers, though students have the option of writing a Master's thesis instead. [13] At the end of their studies, degree candidates must successfully complete an oral examination.
Description: The MA program in Islamic and Near Eastern Studies offers students an opportunity for dedicated, interdisciplinary study of the history, literatures, and cultures of the Middle East from the Middle Ages to the present. [1, 3] It is designed for students who ideally have some college-level preparation in the field and who wish to deepen their expertise in preparation for a PhD program. [1, 3] It is also well-suited for those planning on professional careers in education, law, publishing, business, government, and private agencies whose work touches upon some aspect of Islamic and Near Eastern Studies. [1, 3] Our faculty offer graduate-level instruction in Islamic and Near Eastern history; Islam in world history; Islamic religion and law; anthropology of Islam; premodern Muslim political theory and practice; Near Eastern urban studies; and both classical and modern Arabic literatures. [1] Admission to the MA program normally requires proficiency in Arabic language equivalent to one year of college-level study. [1] After a typical two years of coursework, students will be expected to have completed third-year Arabic successfully before receiving the MA degree. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Japanese
Requirements: General requirements for the Master of Arts in Japanese include a bachelor's degree or equivalent. [5, 8] Applicants must submit transcripts from all undergraduate and/or graduate institutions attended. [9] A personal statement of 2-3 pages is required. [9] Three letters of recommendation in English are also required. [9] Additionally, a writing sample, typically an analytical essay of 20-25 pages on a relevant topic, must be submitted. [9] For international applicants, scores from the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or IELTS are necessary. [9] Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required. [9]
Description: The Japanese section of the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures provides a limited number of highly qualified graduate students with the opportunity to pursue intensive programs of study leading to the MA in Japanese, the PhD in Japanese language and literature, and the dual PhD in Japanese and a comparative literature. [8] The goal of these programs is to produce scholars well-trained in Japanese language, firmly grounded in the linguistic and literary traditions, and thoroughly conversant with critical discourses (indigenous and western) relevant to their fields. [8] The East Asian Languages and Cultures Master's program is a two-year MA designed to give students a dynamic and expansive engagement with East Asia. In addition to the option of concentrating on a single cultural area (China, Korea, or Japan) students can choose a transnational, transhistorical, and multidisciplinary pathway that encourages exploration across literature, history, media, and cultural studies. [9]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Japanese and Comparative Literature
Requirements: Applicants must submit transcripts from all undergraduate and/or graduate institutions attended. Unofficial transcripts should be uploaded at the time of application. Three letters of recommendation are required, in English and submitted via the online application system. A personal statement, 2-3 pages in length, is also required. International applicants must submit their scores on the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or IELTS. [4]
Description: The 'Doctor of Philosophy in Japanese and Comparative Literature' is a dual PhD program. The East Asian Languages and Cultures doctoral programs combine the study of Chinese, Japanese or Korean literature and cultural history as its major component with courses in two minor fields: in literary theory and critical methodology, in studies in one or more other disciplines, or in a second East Asian literature and/or culture.
