[2] The goal of these programs is to produce scholars well-trained in Japanese language, firmly grounded in the linguistic and literary traditions, and thoroughly conversant with critical discourses (indigenous and western) relevant to their fields. [4] All students will have a range of teaching experiences as part of their professional training, with extensive hands-on instruction in pedagogical methodologies. [2] Students who complete the program at the PhD level have extended first-hand exposure to the modern societies whose languages, literatures, and cultures they study and significant teaching experience in both the language and the literature classroom. [4]

ProgramName: Juris Doctor
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution by the time they enroll in the law school. The application is submitted through the Law School Admission Council (LSAC), and a Credential Assembly Service (CAS) report is required. This report includes the applicant's LSAT score, transcripts, and letters of recommendation. While there is no minimum GPA or LSAT score, the admissions committee evaluates a candidate's academic performance, the rigor of their undergraduate program, and their LSAT score. They also consider factors such as work experience, community service, leadership roles, and other personal achievements. International applicants may need to submit a TOEFL score.
Description: The Juris Doctor (JD) at Washington University in St. Louis is a three-year, full-time program. The first year of the curriculum is prescribed and includes foundational courses in Civil Procedure, Constitutional Law, Contracts, Criminal Law, Property, and Torts. Additionally, first-year students take a Legal Practice course that runs for two semesters, which includes training in legal writing, research, and professional skills. For the second and third years, students are able to choose from a wide variety of advanced and specialized courses, allowing them to tailor their education to their specific interests.
Accredidation: The American Bar Association's Section of Legal Education and Admissions to the Bar has accredited Washington University School of Law.

ProgramName: Master of Landscape Architecture
Requirements: Admissions decisions are based on the applicant's portfolio, academic records, personal essays, and references. [1]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts, Graduate School of Architecture & Urban Design
Fees.1: In the 2023-24 school year, full-time tuition for students in the Graduate School of Architecture & Urban Design, which includes the Master of Landscape Architecture program, is $29,513 per semester. [24] There are also additional student activity and health and wellness fees. [24]
ScholarshipAmount: Full-tuition scholarships are available.

ProgramName: Master of Laws in Intellectual Property and Technology Law
Description: The Master of Laws (LLM) in Intellectual Property & Technology Law (IP/TL) is a one-year graduate degree program that responds to the demand for knowledgeable and skilled intellectual property professionals who have already earned a basic law degree. [2] The IP/TL curriculum allows students to study introductory and advanced intellectual property law and to scrutinize the politics affecting those areas of the law under the guidance of leading scholars in the field. [2] Students participate in practical skills courses taught in small groups by teams of experienced intellectual property lawyers. [6] The IP/TL LLM student body is drawn from two distinct sources. [2] First, we admit JD graduates from across the United States who desire to focus their legal expertise through one year of intensive study of intellectual property law. [2] Second, we admit experienced intellectual property attorneys from abroad who want to broaden their knowledge to include U.S. and international intellectual property. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Laws in Taxation
Description: Our Master of Laws (LL. M.) in Taxation degree program is designed for practicing lawyers and graduate law students who want to gain a specialized understanding of the complexities of tax law in the United States. [7] This knowledge can help position you for career advancement at your current company or across a wide range of industries. [7, 5] WashU Law offers a competitive online Master of Laws (LL. M.) program for law professionals and law school graduates who want to expand their understanding of specific aspects of U.S. tax law. [5, 7]

ProgramName: Master of Laws in U.S. Law for Foreign Lawyers
Requirements: Those who wish to apply to our program must submit a resumé, statement of purpose (400-500 words), and transcripts. Transcripts can be unofficial at the time of application, and official transcripts must be received before the start of classes. [8]
Description: The Master of Laws (LLM) in U.S. Law for Foreign Lawyers at WashU is designed for law students who are interested in increasing their knowledge of U.S. or international law to more effectively practice in today's global legal environment. [7] LLM students join a student body drawn from diverse legal cultures and learn from faculty who are experts in both U.S. and international law. [7] LLM students design their own curriculum to suit their academic and career goals. [7] They may concentrate in specialized fields such as corporate or environmental law, or they may select a general course of study to increase their breadth of U.S. and international legal knowledge. [7] Earning the LLM in U.S. Law may permit WashU Law graduates to sit for several states' bar examinations if students choose to pursue appropriate course work. [7] This includes the New York State bar exam, which is the most popular bar among foreign lawyers. [7] This LLM program is an ideal environment for experienced attorneys and recent law graduates alike to pursue any of a number of significant professional and academic goals, such as the following: Gaining practical and Theoretical Knowledge Of u_s_ And international Law; Developing expertise In A specialized field Of Law; Strengthening one's ability To represent clients who have business dealings In the United States Or with u_s_ companies And firms; Improving one's representation Of American clients who conduct business abroad; Building An international network Of professional contacts; Refining one's English skills And understanding Of American culture. [7]
Accredidation: The American Bar Association (ABA) has accredited the law school. [6]

ProgramName: Master of Legal Studies
Description: The Master of Legal Studies (MLS) program at Washington University in St. Louis is designed for non-lawyer professionals who wish to gain a deeper understanding of the U.S. legal system to enhance their careers, without the intention of practicing law. [7, 8] The program involves a customized curriculum that can be tailored to a student's specific needs, allowing them to either specialize in a particular area or take a broad range of law courses for a general understanding of the legal system. [12] To complete the MLS degree, students are required to earn 24 academic credits. [12] It is mandatory for students to successfully complete the "Introduction to U.S. Law and Methods" course, which can be taken online before the program begins or during the first semester. [12] Students are also encouraged to enroll in a traditional first-year law course to understand the Socratic method and common law analysis. [12] The online MLS program offers the same rigorous curriculum as the in-person program and is taught by the same distinguished faculty. [7]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mathematics
Requirements: Applicants to graduate programs at Washington University in St. Louis must hold a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. [2] The general application process is conducted online and typically requires the submission of transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, and letters of recommendation. [2] Specific programs may have additional requirements, such as a resume or curriculum vitae, essays, writing samples, or an interview. [2] For international applicants whose native language is not English, proof of English proficiency through a standardized test like the TOEFL is necessary. [2]
Description: The Department of Mathematics offers a comprehensive doctoral program in mathematics. The completion of the doctoral degree requires about five years of full-time study, and virtually all students receive full financial support (stipends and tuition waiver) during their study. Our graduate programs are designed to give our students a broad perspective in advanced mathematics through a solid foundation of fundamental courses. [9] No one can earn a doctorate merely by completing specified courses of study. The doctoral candidate must demonstrate high scholarship and the ability to perform significant original research in mathematics. [11] The student must complete all courses required by their department; maintain satisfactory academic progress; pass certain examinations; fulfill residence and Mentored Experience Requirements; write, defend, and submit a dissertation; and apply to graduate via Workday Student. [11]
ScholarshipAmount: $36,000 for 12 months (in the 2024-2025 academic year)
ScholarshipType: University Fellowship, Teaching Assistantship, Research Assistantships, NSF support, Dissertation Fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: A bachelor's degree is required for admission. Applicants must complete an online application and pay an application fee. Unofficial transcripts from all attended institutions, three letters of recommendation, and a resume/CV are also required. [10]
Fees.1: $33,425/semester
Description: The Department of Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science offers a Master of Science (MS) degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or Materials Science and Engineering. The department also offers a Master of Engineering in Mechanical Engineering for those coming from fields closely related to mechanical engineering. The MS degrees can be incompleted using either a course option or a thesis option. For the thesis option, the student will work closely with a faculty advisor on the thesis project.
ScholarshipType: Limited fellowship and research assistantship opportunities

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: All applications are evaluated based on a number of factors, including: Undergraduate and/or graduate grades, Publications, Statement, Reference letters, Results of the Graduate Record Exam (GRE general test).
Fees: McKelvey will provide tuition remission for the length of the student's program as long as academic progress is being made. [15]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Molecular Biophysics
Requirements: Applicants submit a single application to the Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology & Biomedical Sciences (DBBS). Instead of a general Statement of Purpose, applicants must respond to two specific essay prompts. The application requires three letters of recommendation and unofficial transcripts from each college/university attended. The GRE is not required or accepted. [2, 3, 4]
Description: The Molecular Biophysics concentration is designed to provide doctoral students with a background in physico-chemical principles of biomolecular structure and dynamics, in addition to applications of biophysical methods to biomolecular systems. [2] Molecular biophysics brings together elements of biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics to describe and understand biological processes. [2] It is a fusion of two scientific cultures: the systems and processes of biochemistry and molecular biology are joined with the principles and quantitative laws of physical chemistry. [2] The goal is to develop a quantitative and predictive understanding of biology at a detailed molecular level. [2] The Program in Molecular Biophysics, established in 1990, seeks to train students who understand biological processes and who can take advantage of the sophisticated physical techniques necessary to probe those processes at a detailed molecular level. [2, 3] An important feature of the Program in Molecular Biophysics is its emphasis on multidisciplinary, interactive approaches to the study of biological systems. [2, 3] The program was renamed to “Computational and Molecular Biophysics” in 2009 to better indicate the importance of both computational and experimental methods in investigating problems in molecular biophysics. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Molecular Cell Biology
Requirements: The Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences (DBBS) oversees the admissions for the Molecular Cell Biology PhD program. All applications are submitted through the online application system. The application requires a personal statement, a description of significant research experiences, a resume or CV, and letters of recommendation. Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions are also required.
Description: The Molecular Cell Biology Program is a graduate training program at WashU, housed under the Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences (DBBS). The goal of research within the Molecular Cell Biology program is to uncover the molecular mechanisms of fundamental cell biological processes. Such processes include cell motility and adhesion, cell cycle, transcription, translation, molecular trafficking, signal transduction and cellular metabolism at homeostasis and in disease states. [2, 3] A common theme which unites these diverse endeavors is the desire to push the limits of our understanding to the highest possible molecular resolution. [9] Ultimately, we seek mechanistic knowledge of the cell to benefit human health. [9]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Molecular Genetics and Genomics
Requirements: Applicants submit a single application to the Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology & Biomedical Sciences (DBBS). The application consists of contact information, demographics, noting a program of concentration interest, three letters of recommendation, transcripts from each college/university attended, and responses to two essay prompts. [2, 4] DBBS does not accept a personal statement or CV in lieu of the essay questions. [2] The GRE General test is not required or accepted. [2, 3] To earn a PhD, a student must complete all required courses, maintain satisfactory academic progress, pass examinations, fulfill residence and Mentored Experience Requirements, and write, defend, and submit a dissertation. [8]
Department: Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences
Fees.1: All students in the Doctor of Philosophy in Molecular Genetics and Genomics program receive a full tuition waiver. [12]
Description: The Molecular Genetics and Genomics is a graduate training program at Washington University in St. Louis, housed under the Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences (DBBS). [3, 5, 6] Molecular geneticists seek to understand how genes are inherited, modified, expressed and regulated. [2] The field of genetics and genomics has been astonishingly successful in deciphering the genetic code and providing us with a clear picture of the nature of the gene, but much remains to be learned about fundamental genetic mechanisms and how specific gene mutations lead to disease. [5, 6] Laboratories in the Molecular Genetics and Genomics (MGG) program leverage human genetics, model organism genetics, and genomic and computational approaches to address key outstanding questions in all areas of biomedical research with a focus on human disease. [5] Integrating wet and dry bench approaches, students in the MGG program advance our understanding of the genetic, cellular, and molecular basis of how cells, tissues, and organs develop and function and how alterations in these processes lead to disease. [5]
ScholarshipAmount: All accepted PhD students receive a full funding package that includes a stipend, tuition waiver, and health insurance.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Molecular Microbiology and Microbial Pathogenesis
Requirements: Competitive candidates will possess an average of 12 months of laboratory research experience, a GPA of 3.0-4.0 (US scale), and rigorous STEM coursework. Three strong letters of recommendation are also required. The admissions committee looks for applicants with significant research experience, intellectual curiosity, academic ability, and maturity. [11]
Department: Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences (DBBS)
Description: The Molecular Microbiology & Microbial Pathogenesis (MMMP) program at Washington University in St. Louis is designed for individual student needs, with a strong emphasis on laboratory research complemented by coursework, seminars, and journal clubs. [1, 5] The program provides comprehensive and modern training in understanding microbes and the diseases they cause. [1, 5] It encompasses two main research areas. The first, Molecular Microbiology, utilizes genetics, cell biology, biochemistry, and biophysics to explore fundamental biological questions such as environmental sensing, cell-cell signaling, and the bacterial cell cycle. [1] The second area, Microbial Pathogenesis and Host Defense, focuses on the molecular biology and biochemistry of pathogenic organisms like bacteria, fungi, viruses, and parasites, with an emphasis on virulence mechanisms and host-parasite interactions. [1, 4] The program is housed within the Roy and Diana Vagelos Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences (DBBS). [2]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Movement Science
Department: School of Medicine, Program in Physical Therapy
Fees: All Movement Science students receive full tuition. [3]
Fees.1: All Movement Science students receive full tuition. [3]
Description: The Movement Science Program offers training to investigate and improve movement in people with chronic diseases such as stroke, diabetes, low back pain, Parkinson disease, hip disorders and obesity. [6] Studies span the full spectrum of investigation levels, from fundamental discovery through clinical application. [6] Our students become part of the next generation of scientists improving human health through movement. [6] They go on to pursue postdoctoral fellowships, academic faculty positions, and careers in industry. [6] The focus of the interdisciplinary doctoral program in movement science is to prepare future researchers and faculty members who can enhance the profession of physical therapy. [4] The PhD in Movement Science offers the opportunity to study at the biological intersection of mechanics, energetics, and neural control systems. [6]
ScholarshipAmount: All admitted students are provided a monthly stipend for four years. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Music in Music
Concentration: The Department of Music offers a Master of Arts (MA) in Music with concentrations in Musicology and Music Theory. The musicology program provides focuses in historical musicology and ethnomusicology, while the music theory program centers on the creative analysis and critical examination of music and musical discourse. [14]
Description: The Department of Music at Washington University in St. Louis offers graduate programs (MA and PhD) that integrate musicology, ethnomusicology, and theory. The department emphasizes individual attention with a low student-to-faculty ratio and fosters a supportive community. Graduate coursework provides advanced study in these areas, and students have opportunities for interdisciplinary study through certificate programs. The program also provides supervised teaching experience and opportunities for independent teaching.
Accredidation: Washington University in St. Louis is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [16] Specific accreditation for the music program is not mentioned on the official university website.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Music
Requirements: The Department of Music offers the Doctor of Philosophy in Music and the Master of Arts in Music, with emphasis in either musicology or music theory. [8, 10]
Description: The Department of Music at Washington University in St. Louis offers a Ph.D. in Music with concentrations in Musicology and Music Theory. The program has an integrated view of musical scholarship, and graduate coursework exposes all students to advanced study in musicology, ethnomusicology, and theory. [2] The university also provides opportunities for interdisciplinary study with certificate programs in areas such as American Culture Studies, Women and Gender Studies, and Film and Media Studies. The department emphasizes a supportive community with a low student-to-faculty ratio, ensuring individual attention. [2] All students admitted to the Ph.D. program are granted generous six-year funding packages, which include additional support for language study, research, and conference travel. [3] The program also offers supervised teaching experience and opportunities for independent teaching. [2] The PhD in Musicology requires 72 units of graduate study, keyboard proficiency, reading knowledge of two foreign languages, and the completion and defense of a dissertation. [10]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Neurosciences
Requirements: The Doctor of Philosophy in Neurosciences is part of the Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences (DBBS). [18] To earn a PhD, a student is required to complete all courses mandated by their department, show satisfactory academic progress, pass examinations, meet residence and Mentored Experience Requirements, and write, defend, and submit a dissertation. [6] Applicants are expected to have a strong educational background and research experience. [3] Competitive applicants typically have about 12 months of laboratory research experience, a GPA between 3.0 and 4.0, and have taken rigorous STEM coursework. [10] Three letters of recommendation are also required. [5]
Description: WashU has a long-standing tradition of excellence in neuroscience. Historic milestones include Erlanger's pioneering work on nerve conduction velocity and its relationship to axon diameter, as well as the 1950s discovery of the first neuronal trophic factor, nerve growth factor, by Levi-Montalcini, Cohen, and Hamburger. Today, a large and collaborative faculty is engaged in nearly every area of modern neuroscience, from molecular studies of ion channels to positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of the human brain, and the genetics of neurological diseases. Faculty from a variety of departments—includ​e​g​ ​​Neuroscience, Anesthesiology, Biochemistry and Molecular Biophysics, Biology, Biomedical Engineering, Cell Biology and Physiology, Developmental Biology, Genetics, Molecular Microbiology, Neurology, Neurosurgery, Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences, Pathology and Immunology, Physics, Psychiatry, Psychological & Brain Sciences, and Radiology—serve as advisors for thesis research and as teaching faculty. The diverse expertise of the faculty ensures students gain exposure to a wide range of neurobiological challenges and research methods. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Nonprofit Management
Requirements: To be considered for admission, you must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. A 3.0-grade point average in undergraduate course work is recommended, but prior academic performance is not the sole criterion for admission. The admissions committee also considers your personal statement, professional experience, and letters of recommendation.

ProgramName: Doctor of Occupational Therapy
Fees: The total cost of tuition for the incoming Doctor of Occupational Therapy (OTD) class in fall 2026 is $143,100. This is comprised of $18,000 per semester for six semesters, $9,000 for each of the two fieldwork experiences, and $17,100 for the doctoral capstone. [3]
Fees.1: $143,100 for the three-year program. [3]
CostPerCredit: $995 per credit hour for the online post-professional OTD program. [7]
ScholarshipType: All applicants are considered for merit-based scholarships during the admissions process. A limited number of graduate assistantships are also awarded. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy
Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy-Neuroscience-Psychology
Requirements: Applicants must earn a bachelor's degree, or equivalent, before enrolling. The PNP program is a track within the Ph.D. program in Philosophy, and the university does not accept students interested in pursuing only an MA. Applicants need not have majored in philosophy but must demonstrate a strong competence in and aptitude for philosophy. The application deadline is December 1, 2025.
Fees: Successful applicants are eligible for support for up to six years (contingent on continued successful performance in the program). Stipends are available.
Fees.1: For the PNP PhD program, successful applicants are eligible for support for up to six years, which includes stipends. [1]
Concentration: Philosophy-Neuroscience-Psychology (PNP) is a track within the Ph.D. program in Philosophy.
Description: The Graduate Program of Philosophy-Neuroscience-Psychology is a track within the Ph.D. program in Philosophy. [2] PNP supplements graduate training in philosophy with additional course work and research on modes of inquiry, empirical results and theoretical perspectives of psychology and the neurosciences. The aim of the Program is to turn out first-rate philosophers with a strong ancillary competence in areas pertaining to Neuroscience and Psychology. [2] The PNP PhD program reflects a growing awareness among philosophers of mind of the importance of an informed interdisciplinary approach to understanding the mind and brain. [3] Key elements of such an interdisciplinary approach include knowledge of the sciences of the mind including findings from cognitive neuroscience, psychology and artificial intelligence, as well as philosophical perspectives on these sciences and on the mind. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Physics
Requirements: For admission to the PhD program, a Bachelor's degree is required. Three letters of recommendation, academic transcript(s), and a statement of purpose are also required. [3, 2] The GRE General exam and the GRE Physics subject exam are not required. [2] Students applying from non-English speaking countries are required to demonstrate proficiency in English via the TOEFL (minimum score of 90) or IELTS (minimum score of 6.5). [2]
Fees: Students who are admitted to the PhD program in Physics receive a complete financial support package including full tuition.
Fees.1: full tuition
Concentration: ['Astrophysics, particle-astrophysics and space sciences', 'Condensed matter, materials, and quantum information', 'Biophysics']
Description: The Department of Physics at Washington University in St. Louis aims to prepare its graduate students for a broad range of careers, from academia and teaching to high-tech and industry. [10] Students first develop a solid and broad base of physics knowledge through our core curriculum and departmental colloquia. Upper level courses and departmental seminar series provide more specialized exposure. [10] Learning and research take place in both formal and informal settings with a wide range of colleagues, including faculty members, postdoctoral fellows, research scientists, and graduate student peers. [10] Research covers a wide area of experimental and theoretical physics, and benefits from collaborations with scientists in other departments on the Danforth Campus and at the School of Medicine. [1] The department is a major participant in the McDonnell Center for the Space Sciences and the Institute of Materials Science & Engineering as well as the newly formed Center for Quantum Sensors. [1]
ScholarshipAmount: Students who are admitted to the PhD program in Physics receive a complete financial support package including full tuition and a stipend/salary for the academic year. [4]
ScholarshipType: Financial support is guaranteed by the department for the first five years for students who are making satisfactory progress towards their PhD.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Plant Biology
Requirements: Requirements for admission to the Plant and Microbial Biosciences graduate program include a baccalaureate degree, generally in the natural or physical sciences or a field of engineering, and a strong background in biology with courses in mathematics, general chemistry, organic chemistry, and physics. [1] An essential criterion for admission is evidence of potential as an independent research scientist, as demonstrated by undergraduate or postgraduate research. [1] Instead of a general personal statement or statement of purpose, applicants must respond to two specific essay prompts. [6] DBBS does not accept a CV or publication in lieu of the two essay questions. [6] Three letters of recommendation are also required. [6]
Description: The Plant and Microbial Biosciences (PMB) Program trains PhD students to have a strong background in modern biology, as well as research training specific to vascular plants, mosses, algae, photosynthetic prokaryotes, and other microbes as experimental organisms to address both fundamental and applied biological questions. [2] Research in PMB covers a diverse array of topics including: Interactions between plants, microbes, and their environment; Assembly and regulation of membrane-associated complexes; Cytoskeletal organization and regulation; Cell morphology and cell division; Structural biology and biochemistry; Cell and organelle size; Metabolic engineering of natural products, biomaterials, and biofuels; Microbial ecology and evolution; Biogeochemical cycles and earth history; Astrobiology. [2] PMB is fully integrated with the eleven other graduate programs that comprise the Vagelos Division of Biology and Biomedical Sciences and emphasizes interdisciplinary collaboration among faculty and students. [2] Students in PMB receive training not only in plant and microbial systems, but also in imaging, biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, systems biology, geochemistry, molecular evolution, and ecology, from leaders in the field. [4]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Political Economy and Public Policy
Doctor of Philosophy in Political Science
Requirements: Required application materials include a writing sample, personal statement, and three letters of recommendation. For international applicants who are not native English speakers, TOEFL scores are also required. [11]
Concentration: ['American politics', 'Comparative politics', 'Formal theory', 'International politics', 'Normative theory', 'Political methodology', 'Race and ethnic politics', 'Political economy']
Description: Washington University's PhD program in political science is designed to prepare students for academic careers in research and teaching at major institutions across the country. [3] While our program stresses the importance of political methodology (applied statistics) and formal theory (game theory and mathematical modeling), our program is designed to train all students in these methods, regardless of their mathematical background. [3] We provide professional training in the discipline through our professional development seminar and we encourage our students to attend professional meetings and participate in convention programs. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Population Health Sciences
Requirements: The MPHS program is designed for: Physicians: residents; fellows; attendings (MD degree), Clinical doctorates: those with doctoral-level degrees including, but not limited to: PhD; DO; OTD; DPT; DNP; PharmD, and Medical students and health sciences students. [2] All applicants must submit the following: Admissions application, Curriculum vitae or resume, Personal statement, and Letter(s) of recommendation or support. [1] External applicants must provide current official scores of the GRE or MCAT. [1] International applicants must submit current official scores of the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or ECFMG English Language Certification. [1]
Fees.1: $1,560.00 per credit
Concentration: ['Clinical Epidemiology', 'Health Services', 'Psychiatric and Behavioral Health Sciences', 'Quantitative Methods']
Description: The Master of Population Health Sciences (MPHS) program equips clinicians and clinical doctorates with the advanced population-based clinical outcomes research expertise that is necessary for successful careers as independent clinician-researchers. [1] The full-time, 10-month format integrates easily into a clinical career. Part-time study options are also available for those with clinical duties. [1] The goal of the MPHS program is to ensure our students can transfer and apply the sophisticated population health research methods skills learned in the program throughout their careers. [1] This is accomplished through core quantitative courses with an emphasis on epidemiology and biostatistics, applied coursework that focuses on the long-term application of skills by developing research study protocols and performing systematic reviews, and elective courses ranging from Randomized Controlled Trials to Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis and Comparative Effectiveness Research. [1]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Psychology
Requirements: Applicants must earn a bachelor's degree, or equivalent, before enrolling in a Graduate program at Washington University in St. Louis. Applications are submitted online. General application materials include an application fee, transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, and letters of recommendation. [2] Specific programs may have additional requirements. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Public Health
Concentration: ['Epidemiology and Biostatistics', 'Generalist', 'Global Health', 'Health Policy Analysis', 'Mental and Behavioral Health']
Description: Our Master of Public Health program equips students to address the most pressing health issues through research and analysis, guided by an advanced understanding of the social, political and environmental factors that influence health outcomes. Courses are taught by faculty members recognized for their contributions to advancing population health. [20] Our curriculum is founded on the understanding that issues in public health are too complex for any one discipline to solve. The MPH program's interdisciplinary emphasis equips students to identify the numerous factors that affect public health and strategically work across disciplines to create sustainable, comprehensive solutions. [20] The Brown School's public health program welcomes students dedicated to advancing health equity—resulting in healthier individuals, families, communities and systems. [21]
Accredidation: The Master of Public Health program is an accredited program. [18] The program is in the process of transitioning to a School of Public Health and has plans to submit an application to become a School of Public Health in June of 2024. [18]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Public Health Sciences
Requirements: Students entering the PhD program must have a master's degree or equivalent in public health or a related discipline from an accredited college or university. All applications for the PhD in Public Health Sciences must be completed through SOPHAS, the centralized public health application service. [4]
Fees.1: All students in the Public Health Sciences doctoral program receive full tuition remission. [3]
Concentration: PhD students develop an individualized research area based on one of three concentration options through coursework and mentored training opportunities.
Description: Our PhD program in Public Health Sciences prepares students to think critically as public health scientists, succeed as investigators, and understand and address public health challenges locally, nationally and globally. It provides research experiences and mentoring from day one in the program; a curriculum that builds methodological and analytical skills as well as deep knowledge of the field's underpinnings and history; and professional acculturation and network building. Graduates transition to leadership roles in academia, policy research, and public health settings. Doctoral students complete innovative coursework in public health foundations, statistical analysis, an array of research methodologies, and their individualized areas of interest. Our program requires 74 credits earned by taking courses and completing mentored research and teaching experiences.
Accredidation: The School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
ScholarshipAmount: All students in the Public Health Sciences doctoral program receive five years of a guaranteed stipend that is adjusted periodically.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Social Work
Requirements: Applicants to the PhD in Social Work must have a master's degree in social work or related discipline. [2] We review all applications holistically, assessing an individual's overall preparation for rigorous doctoral study. [2] Application requirements include: Application Fee, Academic Transcripts, Curriculum Vitae, Three (3) Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose and Objectives, Writing Sample, English Language Proficiency. [2]
Concentration: ['Dissemination and Implementation Sciences (D&I)', 'Systems Science for Health Equity (SS4HE)']
Description: The PhD in Social Work at the Brown School at Washington University in St. Louis is designed to prepare students to become leading scholars who will shape the future of social work. The curriculum emphasizes substantive, theoretical, and methodological preparation. The program requires 74 credits, with 21 credits being transferred from a student's MSW program or a graduate degree from a related field. The first year of study covers basic principles in research, statistics, and measurement, along with theoretical study to enhance social science knowledge. The program also includes required teaching and research practica to complement the individualized curriculum and prepare students for independent teaching and research.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition remission plus a stipend is provided to all admitted PhD students.

ProgramName: Master of Social Work
Requirements: General application requirements for graduate programs at Washington University in St. Louis are determined by each individual program. For example, the School of Continuing & Professional Studies (CAPS) requires a completed online application, a minimum GPA of 3.0, a one-page Statement of Intent, and two letters of recommendation. [14] Specific programs may have additional requirements. [14]
Fees.1: $24,605/Semester for the 2025-2026 academic year. [5]
Concentration: ['Children, Youth, and Families', 'Health', 'Mental Health', 'Social and Economic Development', 'Social Impact Leadership', 'School-Based Social Work specialization', 'Sexuality and Sexual Health specialization', 'Violence and Injury Prevention specialization']
Description: The Master of Social Work (MSW) program at Washington University in St. Louis's Brown School is a top-ranked program that prepares students for leadership in social work. The curriculum is evidence-based and can be individualized to each student's interests. The program is designed to equip students with the skills to make a positive impact on the lives of others through direct practice, policy, and research. Students will learn to address complex social issues and are prepared to work in a variety of settings, including schools, hospitals, and community organizations.
Accredidation: The Master of Social Work program at the Brown School is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based partial-tuition scholarships, including named scholarships such as the Brown School Global Social Work Scholars Award and the Danforth Foundation St. Louis Urban Fellows Scholarship. [7, 20]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Spanish
Doctor of Philosophy in Spanish and Comparative Literature
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Spanish doctoral program, applicants must submit an online application, a Statement of Purpose, a writing sample of around 20 pages, three letters of recommendation, and certified copies of transcripts. [7] The Statement of Purpose should detail the applicant's educational background, experiences leading them to pursue a PhD, potential research interests, alignment with the program, and future goals. [7] For applicants whose native language is not English, a TOEFL score is also required. [7] It is noted that transcripts and recommendation letters not in English must be translated by a certified translator. [7]
Fees: All students admitted to this program receive a full-tuition scholarship. [19]
Fees.1: All students admitted to this program receive a full-tuition scholarship. [19]
Concentration: Dual PhD in Hispanic Studies & Comparative Literature
Description: Completing a doctorate in a dual program with Comparative Literature means gaining the expertise to think about literature across languages and cultures, geography, historical periods, and means of production and transmission. [4] The dual programs require a focus on a "home" literature, in which the student normally duplicates the courses and other preparations expected of a doctoral candidate in that literature or program. It calls for 45 units of course work in Hispanic Studies & 12 units in Comparative Literature. [4]
ScholarshipAmount: All admitted students receive a living stipend of $36,050 and a full-tuition scholarship. [19]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Speech and Hearing Sciences
Requirements: Your submitted application will be considered complete and placed under review once all required materials have been submitted. Required application materials (all submitted online through application link above): Online application form, Personal statement, Resume or CV, Uploaded unofficial transcripts from all college/university coursework, Three letters of recommendation, Non-refundable application fee of $25. [1]
Concentration: hearing science and audiology, language and education, or auditory neuroscience
Description: prepares students for academic and research careers, with students generally focusing on one of three areas: hearing science and audiology, language and education, or auditory neuroscience. Established in 1947, the program operates in collaboration with the Department of Otolaryngology, with research topics including basic science, applied and clinical science and clinical outcomes research.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Statistics
Concentration: Master's Degree in Statistics for Political Science PhD Students
Description: The new Department of Statistics and Data Science (SDS) strives to be a world-class department with outstanding scholars who will transform the university's intellectual community not only through their own activities and achievements but also through synergistic collaborations with existing faculty and an and departments across Arts & Sciences, the McKelvey School of Engineering, and all of the other schools at the university. The SDS department offers two master's degree programs in statistics and one doctoral degree in statistics. Our masterʼs and PhD graduates regularly secure competitive positions at universities, at government institutions, and as statisticians and data scientists in industry. [11] One of the most attractive features of our program is the friendly and supportive atmosphere that develops among our graduate students. [11] These programs provide students with the analytical background needed to prepare them for diverse careers, from positions in government and business to further PhD studies. The regular MA in Statistics consists of 36 units of course work to be completed in three to four semesters. MA students must take (or have taken) the six required courses in statistics or their equivalents listed in the tables below. [11] In addition, they can choose from a wide range of electives that includes several courses from other departments. [11] MA students can also challenge themselves to take the more advanced Statistics PhD qualifier courses to prepare them for further PhD programs upon graduation. [11] High-achieving students may also choose to complete a master's thesis. [11]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Supply Chain Management
Requirements: Applicants for graduate programs must have a bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. [3] Applications are submitted online, and applicants should consult the specific program website for detailed deadlines and a complete list of required materials, as these can vary. [3, 10] Generally, the application may include transcripts from all attended institutions, a statement of purpose, and letters of recommendation. [3, 5]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Systems Science and Mathematics
Requirements: Applications are ready for final consideration after the required items from the application checklist have been submitted. This includes electronic or scanned copies of transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, and a resume. [3]
Fees.1: The tuition for full-time graduate students in the McKelvey School of Engineering for the 2025-2026 academic year is $66,850. [3] When a student takes 9 or more units, a flat-rate tuition is applied. [2]
ScholarshipPercentage: A 50% scholarship is available for students in the Bachelor's/Master's program during their final master's year. [9]
ScholarshipType: Limited fellowship and research assistantship opportunities are available for full-time master's students. [2] The university also lists a "Department Chair's Master's Fellowship". [2]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Systems Science and Mathematics
Requirements: To be considered for admission into a graduate degree program, applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution prior to starting the graduate program. [3] The PhD in Systems Science and Mathematics is designed for full-time students interested in an academic, laboratory or industrial research and development career. [2] Students must complete a minimum of 72 credit hours of post-baccalaureate study, consisting of at least 36 units of course work and at least 24 units of research. [2] Doctoral students seeking financial aid must take the general sections of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). [10] Three letters of recommendation are required. [4] International students must also submit TOEFL scores. [10]
Description: The PhD in Systems Science and Mathematics is an academic doctoral degree designed for full-time students interested in an academic, laboratory or industrial research and development career in a specialized area of systems, control or applied mathematics. [2] Students pursuing the degree must complete a minimum of 72 credit hours of post-baccalaureate study consistent with the residency and other applicable requirements of Washington University in St. Louis and the Graduate School. [2] These 72 units must consist of at least 36 units of course work and at least 24 units of research, and may include work done to satisfy the requirements of a master's degree in a related discipline. [2, 3] Our PhD students are fully funded, including full tuition support and health insurance. As a doctoral candidate, you will also receive a generous stipend to cover living expenses. This support is guaranteed as you continue to make satisfactory progress towards your degree. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Urban Design
Requirements: Application materials for the Master of Urban Design include a resume or curriculum vitae, transcripts from all previous higher education institutions attended, two personal essays, a portfolio demonstrating architecture, design, or visual art work, and three references. English language proficiency test scores are required for applicable international students. [9]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts
Description: The Master of Urban Design program at Washington University in St. Louis introduces students to a variety of urban conditions from local to global, with a detailed focus on sustainable urbanism. [2] Through a core sequence of three studios and seminars, students will develop the skills to create design proposals for a wide range of urban conditions in the contemporary metropolitan landscape. [2] Urban design is approached across all scales, from the mega-region to the district, from the district to the street, and ultimately to the design of the public realm as a space for lively and vibrant community life. [2] The program is designed for individuals who hold a professional or pre-professional degree in architecture, landscape architecture, or planning. [2] Coursework covers the history and theory of urban form, urban sustainability, the morphology and metabolism of urban form, basic principles of urban planning, ecological systems, infrastructural urbanism, spatial justice, and community-engaged design. [4] The studio sequence starts with a community-focused project in St. Louis, then investigates a growing North American city through systems-based thinking and design, and concludes with the required Global Urbanism Studio, which is an immersive study abroad experience in collaboration with global design and sustainability experts. [4]
Accredidation: STEM-designated
ScholarshipAmount: Full-tuition scholarships are available through the Sam Fox Ambassadors Graduate Fellowship Program, which also includes a $1,000 annual creative activity and research stipend. [10, 11, 24]
ScholarshipPercentage: 94% of graduate students at the Sam Fox School receive financial aid. [5]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships and scholarships, teaching and/or technical assistantships, and loan assistance. [24]

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Visual Art
Requirements: Admissions decisions are based on the applicant's portfolio, academic records, statement of objectives, and references. Applicants should have completed a BFA or equivalent academic preparation with a minimum GPA of 3.0. [4] Application materials include a Curriculum vitae, PDF copies of unofficial transcript(s), a concise statement of objectives (500 words or fewer), a portfolio of 20 samples of your best work, and names and contact information for three references. [4] Applicants are NOT required to submit GRE scores. [4]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts
ScholarshipAmount: The Sam Fox Ambassadors Graduate Fellowship Program offers 10 full-tuition scholarships plus a $1,000 creative activity and research stipend annually to outstanding candidates.
ScholarshipPercentage: Over 92% of students received financial support.

ProgramName: Certificate in Applied GeoAI
Certificate in Creative Writing
Requirements: Admission to CAPS undergraduate certificate programs requires a high school diploma or equivalent. [6] The creative writing courses at the School of Continuing & Professional Studies (CAPS) are open to all students with writing skills comparable to those typically learned in English Composition 1110 and 2030. [9, 10] Newly admitted students will complete reading and writing assessments to determine whether any foundational coursework in those areas is needed to ensure success in the chosen program of study. [6]
Description: The creative writing courses at the School of Continuing & Professional Studies (CAPS) are open to all students with writing skills comparable to those typically learned in English Composition 1110 and 2030. CAPS offers a 16-unit Certificate in Creative Writing for those who want to explore in depth and achieve significant mastery in the art of writing fiction or creative nonfiction. [4, 5, 8] Instructors in this program are experienced professional writers, most of whom are associated with the WashU Graduate Writing Program and the Department of English. [4, 5, 8] All of the craft courses are taught using the workshop model, with open discussion and detailed, constructive criticism of each student's writing. [4, 5, 8] Students are able to complete this certificate online. [4, 5, 8] However, course availability may vary depending on the semester. [4, 8, 9] Students may specialize in fiction or creative nonfiction. [4, 9, 10] Each student will take the 3-unit foundational course “Writing Across the Genres” (CAPS-ECOMP 1300) in their first term in the program and, in successive terms, four 3-credit, advanced-level (3000 or higher) courses, including two courses devoted to mastering the craft of writing in the chosen specialty genre, one course primarily in reading and analysis of the literature in that genre, and one course in a second genre. [4, 9, 10] The student's final course in the program will be taken for 4 credits rather than the usual 3, and it will include a 1-credit meta-commentary assignment. [9, 10, 12] This assignment requires students to step back from the particular course and describe (in 1500 words) what they have learned about the differences between and similarities among the genres investigated and how these have affected their choice of genre. [10]

ProgramName: Certificate in Geographic Information Systems
Description: Our Postbaccalaureate Certificate in GIS is designed to advance the skillsets of aspiring and experienced professionals in geospatial and related fields. Through courses that explore fundamental spatial concepts, trends in geospatial technology, and problem-based GIS applications, students will become more knowledgeable and skillful users of geographic information technologies. Graduates of this program will have a strong foundation in geographic information analysis and the tools to apply to a variety of fields. [1]

ProgramName: Certificate in Leadership & Organizational Development
Description: The Certificate in Leadership and Organizational Development focuses on teaching students to develop and apply effective, adaptive, and inclusive leadership skills for successful organizational development. Students in the program learn principles in group behavior, management, and teambuilding as well as how to successfully employ those principles in the workplace. Students are able to complete this certificate online, however, course availability may vary depending on the semester. [3]
Accredidation: Business-related programs at WashU Continuing & Professional Studies (CAPS) are not accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International) at WashU. [3, 8]
ScholarshipType: Need-Based High School ACCESS Scholarship, Non-Degree Student Scholarship, CU Complete Scholarship, Boundless Opportunity Scholarship

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Accounting
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Business Administration, prospective students must submit a completed Common Application or Coalition Application, a $75 application fee or fee waiver, official high school transcript, a counselor recommendation, and teacher recommendations. Students who apply to WashU will select a primary academic division, such as the Olin Business School.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Business Administration (BSBA) is a full-time degree program. The curriculum covers the core functional areas of business, and students will choose at least one major course of study in a field of business. Accounting is one of the available majors. This major provides a path to a career in business, with accounting professionals being in high demand. The program offers job security, diverse career paths, and flexible, transferable skills.
Accredidation: The Olin Business School at Washington University in St. Louis is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) International.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African and African-American Studies
Requirements: The undergraduate admissions committee reviews each application in a holistic and individualized manner. Some of the things assessed during this process include academic potential and preparation, personal characteristics and qualities, accomplishments, and involvement. [18]
Description: The Department of African and African-American Studies' (AFAS) major and minor programs are dedicated to the rigorous, interdisciplinary study and understanding of the histories, cultures, and societies of people of African descent in Africa and in the diaspora. The AFAS curriculum is designed to give students a comprehensive or specialized introduction to the field of Black Studies. The curriculum is comparative and cross-cultural, and it is built upon the premise that an understanding of Black history and culture is an integral part of a liberal arts education. Students who major or minor in AFAS design a course of study and experiential learning that focuses on either a particular area of interest (e.g., health and wellness, arts and culture, or global studies) or a more comprehensive examination of Black culture and life.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Culture Studies
Requirements: The successful completion of a minimum of 12 years of primary and secondary studies is required for admission to any program of study leading to a bachelor's degree at WashU. A secondary school diploma or equivalent is required. Other requirements include original academic transcripts or certified copies, a description of the grading system, examination results, school-leaving certificates, certified English translations of all of the above, grades and class rank (if your school ranks students), a counselor recommendation and one teacher evaluation, and a 250-word response to the question “Please tell us what you are interested in studying at college and why.” [1]
Concentration: ['Race & Ethnicity', 'Gender & Sexuality', 'Ability & the Body', 'Place, Space, & the Environment', 'Popular Culture', 'Citizenship, Nationhood, & Identity', 'Archives & Texts', 'Audio, Visual, & Material Studies', 'Journalism & Ethnography', 'Law, Politics, & Policy Studies', 'Digital Methods']
Description: The American Culture Studies (AMCS) program fosters multidisciplinary study of American historical, social, political, material, and cultural contexts. [4] AMCS at Washington University is a multidisciplinary program that provides both a broader context for study in different fields and a deeper understanding of American culture in all of its complexities. [5] Of particular interest are the political, social, and material dimensions of American culture—past and present—and issues of race, gender, sexuality, and class that spur so much cultural debate and expression. [5] To address these areas, the program has several initiatives, including: modern segregation, race and popular music, American intimacies, and visual and material culture. [5] As an American culture studies (AMCS) major, you will study many different fields to gain a deeper understanding of American culture in all of its complexities. [6] AMCS students explore culture-related topics and issues that demand multiple perspectives and methodologies. [6] They also consider the mutual relevance of various disciplines to any single object of study in American culture while developing the knowledge and skills necessary to study a wide array of cultural objects. [6]
Accredidation: Washington University has been accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC) since 1913. [11] In addition to the university-wide accreditation, each of WashU's professional schools are accredited by their school's professional organization. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Ancient Studies
Requirements: Application for first-year admission is handled through the Common Application or Coalition Application. This includes the application, a fee or fee waiver, high school transcript, counselor recommendation, and teacher recommendations. While a formal resume (CV) is not explicitly required, applicants are expected to list their extracurricular activities. WashU is test-optional, meaning applicants can choose whether to submit ACT or SAT scores. For the Bachelor of Arts in Ancient Studies, there are no additional application requirements to declare the major beyond being an admitted student. The major itself requires the completion of 24 credit units with a grade of C- or better in those courses.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Requirements: For a student's application file to be complete, we must receive the following materials by the deadline for the decision plan selected: Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (or waiver), a teacher recommendation, a school report, official transcripts, and essays. [10] Standardized testing is optional. [10]
Description: Anthropology is the appreciation of and commitment to understanding all aspects of human diversity, past and present, and is devoted to the proposition that the diversity among humankind is comprehensible and enriching. In today's global era, Anthropology is increasingly relevant as we seek to explore and explain differences and similarities among the world's cultures. The Department of Anthropology at Washington University is comprised of world-class scholars whose research interests represent three subfields of the discipline: sociocultural anthropology (including linguistics), archaeology, and biological anthropology. Excellence in teaching and attention to undergraduates is a hallmark of the Anthropology Department. The department offers a major and minor in anthropology, as well as an optional global health and environment track. The program provides one of the most flexible and well-rounded undergraduate majors in the liberal arts and is an unrivaled preparation for professional study (law, business, medicine) and a springboard to careers in wide-ranging fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology (Global Health and Environment Track)
Requirements: Admission to Washington University is for an undergraduate division, not a specific major. The university conducts a holistic review and considers an applicant's academic performance (transcript, course selection, grades), counselor and teacher recommendations, essays, and extracurricular involvement. A high school diploma or its equivalent is required. [4] Applicants must indicate their preferred academic school and potential majors. [6] For the 'Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology (Global Health and Environment Track),' this is a track within the Anthropology major and is declared after matriculation. [14]
Fees: $64,500 per year for the 2024-2025 academic year. Note that this is subject to change for the 2026-2027 academic year.
Description: As an anthropology major in the global health and environment specialization, you will study the most important contemporary issues facing health care and the environment. [2] You will focus on global health, which concerns itself with the broad ways that humans address and cope with issues of health, illness, and well-being in cross-cultural and cross-temporal perspectives. [2] Because issues of health, healing, and wellness are situated in an environmental context (especially the natural physical environment but also the human built and created environment), it is essential that the study of human health be understood within a broad environmental framework. [3] Within Global Health and Environment, students will also have the opportunity to look at the human body within an evolutionary framework, understanding how evolution has shaped the human body and contributed to contemporary patterns of health and disease through course work in human anatomy, paleoanthropology, osteology, genetics, biological development and studies of non-human primates. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Applied Mathematics
Description: The Major in Applied Mathematics has much in common with the Major in Mathematics, but it places particular emphasis on those areas of mathematics that are important for applications in science, engineering, and computing. This is an excellent choice for students who plan to pursue graduate work in applied mathematics, as well as for those interested in pursuing career paths requiring a strong foundation in mathematical analysis and scientific computing. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Science (Chemical Engineering)
Requirements: To be considered for admission, applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (which is waived for those applying for financial aid), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [3] Important components of the application include academic performance (transcript), counselor and teacher recommendations, essays, and extracurricular and community involvement. [3]
Description: In addition to the accredited Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering, another way to explore chemical engineering is to pursue the course of study leading to the Bachelor of Science in Applied Science (Chemical Engineering). This degree serves students who wish to be exposed to key chemical engineering principles yet seek a more flexible curriculum. [1] In addition to the general requirements for a McKelvey Applied Science Degree, the Bachelor of Science in Applied Science (Chemical Engineering) requires students to take chemical engineering coursework as described below. [1] Students must complete 25 units of core coursework and at least 8 units of chemical engineering electives. The core courses provide a foundation in both chemical engineering and key technical skills, and the electives allow the student to explore chemical engineering areas of interest. [1]
ScholarshipAmount: up to full tuition

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Science (Electrical Engineering)
Description: Students who do not plan to pursue a career in electrical engineering but who seek a strong foundation in the principles of electrical engineering may choose the Bachelor of Science in Applied Science (Electrical Engineering). [2] The program ensures that the student learns the foundations of electrical engineering through breadth requirements. [2] In addition, there is flexibility in selecting upper-level courses to meet the student's individual objectives. [2] This program also may be attractive for students interested in obtaining multiple degrees, because the requirements are less strict than for the BSEE degree. [2] Historically, students have matched a degree in electrical engineering with degrees in other engineering disciplines, in the natural sciences, in music, in history and in business; other combinations are possible. [3] This also may be an attractive option for students planning graduate studies in a variety of disciplines, including medicine, law or business. [3]
Accredidation: This applied science degree is not accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. [2, 3]
ScholarshipAmount: Up to full-tuition scholarships

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Science (Mechanical Engineering)
Description: Die Studienrichtung Bachelor of Science in Applied Science (Mechanical Engineering) bietet Studierenden einen Abschlussweg, um technisches Wissen im Maschinenbau mit mehr Flexibilität bei der Kurswahl zu erwerben. Das Programm bietet eine substanzielle und konsistente Ausbildung im Maschinenbau mit maximaler Flexibilität. Dieses Programm ist von Vorteil, wenn Sie ein flexibleres Programm als das akkreditierte BSME-Studium anstreben. Es eignet sich besonders für ein Doppelstudium in Kombination mit Mathematik, Physik, Chemie, Biologie, Wirtschaftswissenschaften oder einer anderen Ingenieurdisziplin. Das Programm kann so geplant werden, dass es eine Grundlage für eine Graduiertenarbeit in biologischen, medizinischen oder Managementbereichen bietet.
Accredidation: Der Bachelor of Science in Applied Science ist ein nicht-professioneller Abschluss und ist nicht vom Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET) akkreditiert. [2, 5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Science (Systems Science & Engineering)
Requirements: Admission to WashU is based on a holistic and individualized review of each application, assessing academic potential, personal characteristics, and accomplishments. To apply, students must submit either the Common Application or Coalition Application, a $75 nonrefundable fee (which is waived for students applying for financial aid), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. For applicants to the McKelvey School of Engineering, it is strongly recommended that their high school curriculum includes four years of mathematics (with calculus), as well as chemistry and physics. [2]
Fees: $68,240 for the 2025-26 academic year for full-time undergraduate students.
Description: The systems science and engineering program at the McKelvey School of Engineering prepares students to view an entire system of components as an entity piuttosto che as an assembly of individual parts. [1] Each component is designed to fit properly with the other components rather than to function by itself. The engineering and mathematics of systems is a rapidly developing field. [1, 4] It is one of the most modern segments of applied mathematics, as well as an engineering discipline. [1, 4] It is concerned with the identification, modeling, analysis, design and control of systems that are potentially as large and complex as the U.S. economy or as precise and vital as a space voyage. [1, 4] This program provides the student with the opportunity to prepare their academic career with maximum flexibility but also with enough organization to ensure substantive, consistent training in systems science methodology and outlook. [2, 3] This program is recommended if students wish to pursue a program that does not follow conventional lines. [2, 3] It is an especially advantageous degree for a double major in association with mathematics, physics, economics or another engineering discipline. [2, 3] The program can be planned to provide a desirable background for graduate work in biological, medical or management fields. [2, 3]
Accredidation: This applied science degree is not accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. [1, 2, 3]
ScholarshipType: Need-based and merit-based scholarships are available.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Arabic
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission, which is required before declaring a major in Arabic, applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. This includes a nonrefundable $75 fee (though fee waivers are available), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. The application process also includes essays. [6]
Description: As a major in Arabic, you can expect to gain proficiency in the language, study the area's literary and cultural landmarks, and gain familiarity with Near Eastern history and civilizations. [5] Whether you favor the study of language, literature, religion, history, or politics, you will find a way to deepen your appreciation of these complex and diverse societies and cultures. [5] This major is housed in the Department of Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Studies. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Archaeology
Description: The undergraduate program in archaeology at Washington University provides students with a broad understanding of the human past. The program is interdisciplinary, with faculty from the departments of Anthropology, Art History and Archaeology, Classics, and History. Students learn about the methods of archaeological research, including excavation, survey, and laboratory analysis. They also have opportunities to participate in fieldwork projects in various parts of the world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Architectural Design
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to the Sam Fox School, you must select a major within the College of Architecture or the College of Art on your application. The main factors considered for admission are your academic record and your artistic and intellectual promise. You are required to have graduated from high school and received recommendations from teachers or other school officials. A portfolio is optional for first-year applicants to the College of Architecture but is required for transfer students. The portfolio should consist of 10-20 pieces of your most recent work. [4]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts, College of Architecture

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Architectural Design
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Architectural Design, you must apply to the College of Architecture at Washington University in St. Louis through the general undergraduate admissions process. A portfolio of 10-20 works is recommended for applicants to the College of Architecture and is required for scholarship consideration. [2]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts, College of Architecture
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Architecture is a more flexible course of study that allows students to take additional architecture design studios or to pursue courses in other areas of interest across the University. All architecture students take similar courses during their first three years; courses during the fourth year will differ depending on the student's choice of degree option. In the first year, students engage in a beginning design studio focused on environmental questions and the exploration of materials and media, an introduction to architecture practice through case studies, and an introduction to architectural representation. The second year includes a design studio focused on technological questions, interdisciplinary track electives, architectural history courses, and an ecological systems course. The third year features a design studio focused on social questions and honing knowledge of assemblies, structure, sustainability, landscape, and the urban environment, along with a building systems course and an architectural theory course. All years include additional coursework in the liberal arts.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art History and Archaeology
Requirements: As students apply to an undergraduate school and not directly to the major, the application requirements are for general admission. The university uses the Common Application, which includes a personal essay. Applicants must also submit their high school transcript. There is no specific mention of a separate resume or writing sample being required for general undergraduate admission.
Description: Art history provides the opportunity to explore the fine arts, architecture, and visual culture as well as the social, aesthetic, and personal values that helped to shape these disciplines. [5] Students are introduced to the study of art history and archaeology through general introductory courses that focus on American, Asian, and European art as well as world archaeology. [5] In more advanced courses, students enjoy studying original works of art owned by Washington University's Mildred Lane Kemper Art Museum, the Saint Louis Art Museum, the Pulitzer Arts Foundation, and local private collectors. [5] Students are also invited on annual field trips organized by the faculty to visit cities with major museum collections. [5] A variety of career paths are available to majors in art history and archaeology. [5] Many graduates earn advanced degrees in both related and unrelated fields and work in museums or academia or for art publishers, commercial art galleries, auction houses, nonprofit organizations, and other arts-related organizations. [5]
ScholarshipAmount: Up to full tuition, with some specific awards like $3,000.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Studio Art
Requirements: Primary considerations for admission are artistic and intellectual promise, as well as the applicant's academic record. Applicants must have graduated from high school and received recommendations from teachers or other school officials. A portfolio submission of 10-20 works is required for all College of Art applicants and must be submitted via SlideRoom. [2, 5] General application components also include essays and extracurricular/community involvement. [14] While not required, a challenging high school curriculum including honors, AP, or IB courses is typical for applicants. [14]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts
Description: The undergraduate studio art program at WashU includes a bachelor of fine arts degree (BFA), a bachelor of arts degree (BA), or a second major. In their first year, students take core studios including drawing, 2D design, 3D design, digital studio and a weekly seminar. These foundation courses set the stage for more advanced coursework when students can choose between concentration areas. Studio courses are supplemented by readings and seminars that acquaint you with the field of contemporary art and in developing an understanding of where your interests fit in the historical arc. [2] As your education progresses, so will your course flexibility. You can choose between studios in core areas—Painting, Sculpture, Printmaking, and Photography—as well as ones in hybrid media, time arts, public art, socially engaged practice, and much more. You will also take professional practice seminars, taught by our dedicated career specialist, in which you'll develop essential skills like writing an artist statement, preparing a CV, applying for opportunities, and presenting a public lecture on your work. [4] In the senior capstone course, BFA in Studio Art students commit to an artistic position evidenced through studio production, presentation, and writing. You'll deliver a public presentation about your work and participate in the BFA in Studio Art Thesis Exhibition. [2]
Accredidation: The College of Art subscribes to the standards for the Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) degree and Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree as set forth and accepted by the College Art Association of American (CAA) and the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD). [4]
ScholarshipAmount: The Conway/Proetz Scholarships in Art offer one full-tuition scholarship and up to five $10,000 scholarships annually. [1]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available, including the Conway/Proetz Scholarships in Art for students who demonstrate outstanding academic performance and promise. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Communication Design
Requirements: Your WashU Pathway will include a current checklist of your support materials: School report and official transcript, Teacher evaluation, Counselor recommendation, Optional – Self-reported or official SAT or ACT scores, TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test for students whose first language is not English, Portfolio (required for students applying to the College of Art, strongly encouraged for students applying to the College of Architecture). The portfolio should be submitted using SlideRoom. [13]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Communication Design at Washington University in St. Louis trains designers and illustrators to cultivate intelligent, creative practices.
