The program encourages a broad approach to communication design, with students starting with a foundation in drawing and design studios. Beginning in their sophomore year, students explore image-making for graphic design, type, letterform, and more. [6] The curriculum allows students to learn how to design interfaces for mobile and web, create motion graphics and animations, illustrate stories and comics, and develop interactive experiences. The BFA is described as a studio-intensive program that includes a capstone project where students can showcase their specialization in illustration, graphic design, or interaction design. [6] BFA in Communication Design seniors pursue a capstone project that results in a work such as an illustrated book, zine, screen-based presentation, or graphic novel, which is then displayed in a public exhibition. [6] To receive the BFA degree, a student must meet the university's requirements, which include a total of 121 units of coursework. [9]
Accredidation: The College of Art subscribes to the standards for the Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) degree as set forth and accepted by the College Art Association of American (CAA) and the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD). [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Fashion Design
Requirements: To be considered for admission, applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (or waiver), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [16] A portfolio is also required for applicants to the College of Art, which houses the Fashion Design program. [11]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts, College of Art
Fees: $62,950 per year for the 2024-2025 academic year
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Fashion Design at Washington University in St. Louis is housed within the Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts. The program is founded on the principles of art and design, with a curriculum that emphasizes sustainability, technology, and interdisciplinary studies. It aims to challenge students to create a meaningful and intelligent narrative about fashion and clothing in various contexts, from the personal to the industrial. Students are taught to design for the human body in all its diversity and to apply these design concepts to apparel, accessories, and footwear. The program guides students through the entire creative process, from the initial research phase to the development of the final product.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology
Requirements: Washington University in St. Louis receives applications through the Common Application or Coalition Application. Students must have earned a high school diploma or its equivalent. [8] The university considers an applicant's academic and personal history, taking into account individual context, circumstances, and opportunities. [8] Most applicants have taken advantage of advanced courses like AP, IB, or dual enrollment if offered at their high schools. [8]
Concentration: ['Ecology and Evolution', 'Genomics and Computational Biology', 'Molecular Biology and Biochemistry', 'Neuroscience', 'Environmental Biology', 'Microbiology']
Description: The major program in biology provides a thorough education in the history of scientific discovery in biology, the logical and statistical procedures used to formulate and test biological hypotheses, and the technical skills needed to conduct contemporary biological research. The biology major program emphasizes the hierarchical nature of biological complexity and the major structures and functions that emerge at the molecular, cellular, organismal, populational and ecosystem levels. [11] Each student masters at least one dimension of contemporary research in sufficient detail to describe the major hypotheses currently being tested and to demonstrate techniques used to test those hypotheses. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology (Ecology and Evolution Track)
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission, important components include the student's academic performance (transcript), counselor and teacher recommendations, essays, and extracurricular and community involvement. [2]
Description: As a biology major in the ecology and evolution specialization, you will study the vital processes of all organisms and the environments in which they flourish. The ecology and evolution specialization focuses on the relations of organisms with each other and their physical surroundings and how those relations are shaped and changed over time. [3]
ScholarshipType: Washington University offers both merit-based and need-based scholarships for undergraduate students. [1, 5, 7, 9, 10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology (Genomics and Computational Biology Track)
Requirements: Application requirements are for general undergraduate admission to Washington University in St. Louis, not for this specific program track. The university requires submission of an application, official high school transcripts, and recommendations. [1] Portfolios may be required for specific programs like Art. The university has a test-optional policy regarding SAT/ACT scores. [5]
Description: As a biology major in the genomics and computational biology specialization, you will study the vital processes of all organisms and the environments in which they flourish. In the genomics and computational biology specialization, you will focus on the structure, function, evolution, and mapping of genomes. You will also use biological data to better understand relations among biological systems. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology (Microbiology Track)
Requirements: To have a complete application, Washington University in St. Louis requires the Common Application or Coalition Application, a $75 fee (which can be waived), essays, a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [6] Standardized testing is optional. [6]
Description: The major program in biology provides a thorough education in the history of scientific discovery in biology, the logical and statistical procedures used to formulate and test biological hypotheses, and the technical skills needed to conduct contemporary biological research. The biology major program emphasizes the hierarchical nature of biological complexity and the major structures and functions that emerge at the molecular, cellular, organismal, populational and ecosystem levels. Each student masters at least one dimension of contemporary research in sufficient detail to describe the major hypotheses currently being tested and to demonstrate techniques used to test those hypotheses. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology (Molecular Biology and Biochemistry Track)
Description: As a biology major in the biochemistry and molecular biology specialization, you will study the vital processes of all organisms and the environments in which they flourish. Within the biochemistry and molecular biology specialization, you will work with the structure and function of life's essential macromolecules. You will focus on the chemical processes that these macromolecules facilitate within living organisms. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology (Neuroscience Track)
Requirements: To apply, students must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. Important components of a student's application include their academic performance (transcript), counselor and teacher recommendations, essays, and a list of extracurricular and community involvement. [6] A 250-word response to the question 'Please tell us what you are interested in studying at college and why' is also part of the application. [9]
Description: For students with interests in the Biological Bases of Neuroscience, the Neuroscience Track of the Biology Major is recommended.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: Washington University in St. Louis has a test-optional policy for undergraduate admissions. Applicants are not required to submit standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) to be considered for admission. For students who choose to submit scores, Washington University will consider the highest score for each section across all test dates. There are no specified minimum ACT or SAT scores for admission. Admission to the university is competitive, and applicants are expected to have a challenging high school curriculum, including honors, AP, and IB courses if available.
Description: Biomedical engineering is an interdisciplinary field in which the concepts, methods and techniques of engineering are applied to solving problems in biology and medicine. It applies quantitative, analytical and integrative方法from a molecular level to that of the whole organism to further our understanding in basic biological processes and to develop innovative approaches for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of disease. A student majoring in biomedical engineering will have the opportunity to participate in the world-class research activities of engineering and medical faculty in biomaterials, imaging, cardiovascular engineering, cell and tissue engineering, molecular cellular and systems engineering, neural engineering, regenerative engineering, and women's health technologies. [3, 7] The Department of Biomedical Engineering at Washington University in St. Louis (WashU BME) seeks to provide a first-class engineering education that prepares students for a variety of careers and a cutting-edge graduate program that advances knowledge and technology with the goal to improve human well-being. [3, 7] The program's overall educational objective is to prepare graduates for various career paths, including pursuing careers in the biomedical engineering industry, undertaking advanced study, or completing professional degrees in fields like medicine, dentistry, or law. [2, 3, 7]
Accredidation: The BS in biomedical engineering program at Washington University in St. Louis is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org/, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Biomedical Engineering. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business and Computer Science
Department: Olin Business School and McKelvey School of Engineering
Description: Students in this program will be equipped with the fundamental knowledge and perspectives of computer science and business and will have unique opportunities to converge these two disciplines. The Bachelor of Science in Business and Computer Science is an integrated joint degree program offered through the Olin Business School and the McKelvey School of Engineering at Washington University in St. Louis. [1] As one of the only such joint programs in the country, the Bachelor of Science in Business and Computer Science features unique curricular and cocurricular elements that help to create a distinctive program. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: Washington University in St. Louis does not list specific application requirements for the Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering. Applicants are subject to the general undergraduate admissions requirements. The university uses a holistic review process and considers academic achievement, extracurricular involvement, and personal essays. There is no mention of a required resume or statement of purpose for general first-year admission.
ScholarshipType: The university offers need- and merit-based scholarships. [25]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year admission to Washington University in St. Louis include the Common Application or Coalition Application, an official high school transcript, a school report, one teacher evaluation, and a counselor recommendation. Applicants must also submit a 250-word response to a provided question about their academic interests.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: Admission to Washington University is based on a holistic review of each applicant. To apply, students must use the Common Application or Coalition Application. Required components include official high school transcripts, a personal essay (the Common or Coalition Application essay), and a 200-word response to a WashU-specific question about their academic interests. [3] All applicants, regardless of whether they submit standardized test scores, will receive full consideration. [3]
Description: Studying chemistry provides students with the opportunity to explore the structure and constitution of the microworlds of atoms and molecules, the chemical and physical transformations that occur there, and the principles that govern these changes. Our program provides a strong foundation in the core areas of chemistry: organic, physical, inorganic, nuclear, and theoretical. Special emphases in the department include such emerging interdisciplinary fields as organometallic, bioorganic, materials, and computational chemistry. The department is a community of scholars that includes 19-full time faculty members, 17 staff members, 130 graduate students, 40 postdoctoral fellows and research scientists, and 120 chemistry majors. Each student works closely with a faculty member to design and carry out an original research project. Students may participate in interdisciplinary research at the School of Medicine or the McKelvey School of Engineering. Research internships at local companies can also be arranged.
Accredidation: In addition, WashU's undergraduate and graduate level teacher certification programs are accredited by the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE) and are authorized to offer coursework and to recommend candidates for certification in the following content areas: ... Secondary Education (Grades 9-12) in ... Chemistry ... [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry (Biochemistry Track)
Requirements: For general undergraduate admission to Washington University in St. Louis, applicants are typically required to submit high school transcripts, a counselor recommendation, and at least one teacher evaluation. [9] While the university has a test-optional policy, students can choose to submit SAT or ACT scores. [3] Once enrolled, to major in Chemistry with a Biochemistry Specialization, students must complete a total of 61-62 credit units, and a minimum grade of C- is required in each course to count toward the major. [15]
Description: As a chemistry major in the biochemistry specialization, you'll study the structure and constitution of the microscopic world of atoms and molecules, the chemical and physical transformations that occur in it, and the principles that govern these changes. Within the biochemistry specialization, special attention is given to the chemical processes that occur within living organisms. [13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chinese Language and Culture
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Arts in Chinese Language and Culture program follows the general undergraduate admission process for Washington University in St. Louis. The university uses a holistic review process and does not require separate application materials for this specific major.
Description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures offers a unified major and minor in East Asian Languages and Cultures which allows students to explore three linguistic and cultural traditions: Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. Students may pursue a focused approach to their studies by studying one of our languages and may choose among the range of non-language courses to enhance their grounding in the East Asian nation of their choice. Students may also choose to study across disciplinary and geographic boundaries. The emphasis in the East Asian Language and Culture programs (with concentrations on Chinese, Japanese or Korean), is on achieving high competency in the relevant language and learning how to read texts from the target culture—literary, philosophical, cultural, historical, or even visual—with an informed appreciation of the contexts in which they were produced. [9] The goal of all of these studies -- language, textual and interdisciplinary -- is to acquire the cultural sensitivities needed to become sophisticated scholars and educated global citizens, as well as to provide a deeper appreciation of our common cultural experience and the intrinsic value of humanistic study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classics
Requirements: Applicants are required to have earned a high school diploma or its equivalent. The admissions review takes each applicant's individual context, circumstances, and opportunities into account. Most applicants take advantage of honors, Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, and/or Dual Enrollment courses, if offered by their high schools. [8]
Description: The major in Classics at Washington University in St. Louis is centered on the study of Latin and/or ancient Greek languages. Students gain direct access to the thoughts and lives of ancient Greek and Roman people by reading original texts. The curriculum teaches the interpretation of diverse ancient literary and historical writings, fostering a deep understanding of their original context. Majors in Classics delve into significant questions regarding power, gender, art, religion, education, and cultural change, thereby developing strong critical and writing abilities. The university's resources for classics studies include a large library collection on the ancient world, as well as collections of Greek papyri, art, and the Wulfing Coin Collection.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Arts
Requirements: To be considered for admission to Washington University, applicants must demonstrate a strong academic record and a passion for learning. While there are no specific GPA requirements, a competitive academic profile is essential. The university considers a variety of factors in its holistic review process, including standardized test scores (SAT or ACT), extracurricular activities, and personal essays. [4] For a student's application file to be complete, the university must receive the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee, a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [6]
Description: As a comparative arts major, you'll study the relationship between literature and one or several other arts—music, drama, dance, the visual arts, and film—across national, cultural, and linguistic borders. [2] Courses track universal themes such as individual identity, memory, human suffering, violence, beauty, ethics, and dreams across nationalities. [2] Since knowing the language is essential to understanding a given literature and culture, all majors study a second language and literature at an advanced level. [2] This major is housed in Comparative Literature. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature
Requirements: The undergraduate admissions committee reviews each application in a holistic and individualized manner. Important components of a student's application include the student's academic performance (transcript), including course selection and grades; counselor and teacher recommendations; essays; and extracurricular and community involvement. [3]
Concentration: ['General languages and literature', 'Advanced language and literature with work in a third language', 'Literature and a related discipline (such as sociology, history, music, or film)', 'Translation concentration', 'Film concentration']
Description: The Department of Comparative Literature brings into sharper focus literatures and cultures from around the world by holding them under a comparative light. [2] It expands the boundaries of national traditions and brings them into dialogue with each other. [2] Our curriculum seeks to prepare students for reading and research in the languages and histories of different societies and periods. It also emphasized cultural and critical analysis, literary theory and interdisciplinarity. [2] Literary theory in all its forms helps to break down the borders between national literary fields, as well as between literary studies and other disciplines. [2] Indeed, the discipline of Comparative Literature asks, often, just what "literature" is, and how it functions as a product of (and response to) our imaginations, our languages, and our social and economic lives. [2] The undergraduate major in Comparative Literature is designed for students whose curiosity about literature is wider than a single national tradition. [2] In our courses, we think about how literature (very broadly defined) functions in our imaginations, our languages, and our social, political, and economic lives. [2] The major in Comparative Literature requires students to enroll in a set of core courses offered by the department, to complete electives in the department, and to enroll in additional literature courses, or other courses approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies, offered by other departments. This flexibility to combine literature courses from several departments and to address literature from multiple traditions is the hallmark of the Comparative Literature major. [2] Literature is read in translation, we study translation itself, and the department encourages language study by automatically counting Language Center courses towards the flexible electives in the major. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
Requirements: For a first-year application to be complete, Washington University in St. Louis requires the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (with waivers available), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [6]
Description: Computer engineering encompasses studies of hardware, software, and systems issues that arise in the design, development, and application of computer systems. Computer engineers are a good fit for jobs that involve the interplay between hardware and software. They are well suited to address the particular challenges that exist as computing systems interact with the real, physical world. This includes sensing, actuation, timing, security, and computing systems with widely varying form factors, ranging from servers to mobile devices to the "internet of things."
Accredidation: The Computer Engineering Bachelor of Science program, administered jointly by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering and the Department of Electrical Engineering, is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Computer Engineering and Similarly Named Computing Programs. [4]
ScholarshipAmount: Awards that range up to the full cost of attendance.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: General application requirements for undergraduate admission to Washington University in St. Louis include the Common Application or Coalition Application, an application fee or waiver, official high school transcripts, and teacher recommendations. Specific program-level requirements for admission are not specified; students are admitted to the university and then declare their major.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (BSCS) is designed for students planning a career in computing. Students working toward a BSCS degree must meet all requirements for an applied science degree from the McKelvey School of Engineering. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science + Economics
Requirements: The university's bulletin and admissions pages do not specify application requirements such as a resume, statement of purpose, or writing sample for general undergraduate admission. For admission to the Bachelor of Science program, transfer applicants must submit high school transcript(s), an application, official transcripts of all previous college work, a Transfer Academic Evaluation (letter of recommendation), and a Transfer Registrar Report (College Report). [8] An application fee of $75 or a fee waiver is also required. [8]
Department: McKelvey School of Engineering and College of Arts & Sciences
Description: The College of Arts & Sciences and the McKelvey School of Engineering have developed a new major that allows students interested in both economics and computer science to combine these two complementary disciplines efficiently, without having to pursue them as two separate majors. [3, 4, 8, 10, 11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science + Math
Description: This major, developed through a collaboration between the McKelvey School of Engineering and the College of Arts & Sciences, efficiently captures the intersection of the complementary studies of computer science and math. [5, 6]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science + Math program has not requested to be reviewed by ABET. [11] Washington University in St. Louis has been accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC) since 1913. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Dance
Requirements: Prospective students for the Bachelor of Arts in Dance should follow the general application procedures for first-year admission to the College of Arts & Sciences. While not required, applicants to arts programs may supplement their application with a portfolio or resume.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Dance at Washington University in St. Louis treats dance as a global phenomenon with culturally specific and individual differences in expressive form. The curriculum emphasizes the study of dance as both an independent and collaborative art. Students in the program are encouraged to develop their capacity to move and think creatively and to recognize movement as an essential element of personal identity. [8] The program offers a liberal arts course of study with intensive studio work in the technique and theory of modern dance, ballet, and composition, complemented by seminars that examine dance as a global phenomenon with forms reflecting culturally specific historical, aesthetic, and anthropological features. [7] Coursework integrates practice with the study of the historical, cultural, scientific, and aesthetic dimensions of dance. While there are required courses in all aspects of the dance major, students can tailor their studies to emphasize one of four areas: Embodied Practice, Creative Process, History/Theory, or Movement Science/Somatics. [11] The program also provides a broad range of elective courses, including stagecraft, improvisation, anatomy for dancers, musical theater dance, pedagogy, and various world dance forms. [7]
MinGPA: C- or better in all required and elective dance courses

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Drama
Requirements: To apply for first-year admission to Washington University, applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, a $75 application fee (or waiver), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. Essays are also required as part of the application. [3] Application to the Bachelor of Arts in Drama program itself is not a separate process from the general university application; students declare their major after matriculation. [10, 15] A portfolio is not required for applicants to the College of Arts & Sciences (where the Drama program is housed), but performing arts supplements can be submitted optionally for a fee. [9]
Concentration: ['Drama General', 'Acting', 'Directing', 'Costume Design', 'Lighting Design', 'Scenic Design', 'Playwriting', 'Theatre, Performance & Society']
Description: The drama curriculum provides an exemplary liberal arts course of study by combining practical creative work in acting, directing, design, and production with intensive scholarly exploration of the literature, history, and theory of performance, understood as a fundamental mode of human communication. [10] Our theater arts faculty are highly accomplished directors, actors, designers and playwrights who are devoted to the mission of university teaching. [10] Our scholarly theater and performance studies faculty are world-recognized leaders in their fields with extensive publishing, editing, and lecturing credentials. [10] In all areas of drama at Washington University, students are encouraged to take the lead in artistic creation, problem solving, collaboration, and scholarly research. Our students act, write for, direct, design, and manage major productions. [10] They delve into archives and library stacks, and communicate their findings in speech and writing, gaining intellectual self-confidence and independence. In every aspect of our work, the drama faculty provide challenges and guidance for students with a mind toward their self-realization as artists, thinkers, and leaders. [10]
ScholarshipAmount: Up to the full cost of tuition

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth and Planetary Sciences (Geology)
Requirements: To have a complete application file, Washington University in St. Louis requires the submission of the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (which is waived for students applying for financial aid), and all required additional materials as outlined by the Office of Undergraduate Admissions, including a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [5] Important elements of the application include academic performance (transcript), counselor and teacher recommendations, essays, and extracurricular involvement. [5] Portfolios are required for applicants to the College of Art and recommended for the College of Architecture. [5]
Description: The Department of Earth, Environmental, and Planetary Sciences (EEPS) an interdisciplinary field that applies principles of biology, chemistry, physics, and math to investigate topics that range from early life on Earth and the structure of Earth's deep interior to the nature of contaminant transport and the evidence for water on Mars. The curriculum is broad, and the requirements are flexible enough to accommodate diverse needs and interests. Many courses present hands-on, problem-oriented experiences, including ample opportunity for fieldwork, laboratory work, and the use of state-of-the-art computational facilities and research instrumentation. All majors are required to complete certain core courses as well as electives and a capstone experience that must be presented at the Spring EEPS Undergraduate Symposium.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth and Planetary Sciences (Geophysics)
Requirements: Application requirements are not specific to the major but are for general admission to Washington University in St. Louis. First-year applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. Required materials include a high school transcript, a counselor recommendation, and one teacher evaluation. [7] The university has a test-optional policy regarding SAT or ACT scores. [7] A portfolio is required for students applying to the College of Art and is strongly encouraged for the College of Architecture. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies
Requirements: Admission to Washington University is selective and competitive. Important components of an application include the student's academic performance (transcript), counselor and teacher recommendations, essays, and extracurricular and community involvement. [5] Most successful applicants have taken advantage of honors, Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, and/or Dual Enrollment courses if offered by their high schools. [5] A high school diploma or its equivalent is required. [5]
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies includes two years of language training in one of the three East Asian languages (Chinese, Japanese, or Korean), in addition to coursework in aspects of East Asian society and culture. It has been designed as a flexible program for students who want basic language training as well as the opportunity to study a variety of topics and approaches to the culture and history of East Asian countries. Our undergraduate degree programs build the foundation for careers in business, international relations, cultural exchanges, and other occupations with a focus on East Asia.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Requirements: Application requirements are for general undergraduate admission to Washington University in St. Louis, not for a specific major. Students typically declare their major after matriculating. The university uses a holistic review process. As of Fall 2026 admissions, the university has a test-optional policy, meaning applicants can choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores. [9, 4] Students who do not submit scores will not be penalized. [9]
Description: The Economics program explores the problems of a modern economy and introduces the methodological tools that economists use. It emphasizes the development of analytical models and their application to important economic, social and political issues, such as inflation, unemployment, taxation, inequality, poverty, pollution, government decision-making, and regulation. [14] Our faculty, which is made up of leading teacher-scholars, includes specialists in game theory, microeconomics, macroeconomics, industrial organization, monetary economics, financial economics, and public finance. [14] The study of economics contributes to a broad liberal arts education and helps students develop superior problem-solving skills. [14] It is an excellent course of study to pursue, whether students plan to enter the workforce after graduation or are considering graduate work in law, engineering, or the social sciences. [14] Economics also provides exceptional preparation for careers in business, either immediately after graduation or after completing master's-level graduate work in business (e.g., MBA, MS Finance). [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Economics
Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Computer Science
Requirements: To apply for first-year admission, students must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. These applications include a personal essay and a section to list extracurricular activities.
Department: College of Arts & Sciences and McKelvey School of Engineering
Description: The College of Arts & Sciences and the McKelvey School of Engineering have developed a major that allows students interested in both economics and computer science to combine these two complementary disciplines efficiently, without having to pursue them as two separate majors. [5, 7, 8] Engineering students who declare this major must fulfill the distribution requirements and all other requirements for the BS in Applied Science degree in the McKelvey School of Engineering. Arts & Sciences students who declare this major must fulfill the distribution requirements and all other requirements for a BA degree in addition to the specific requirements listed below. [5, 7] It is possible to earn the Financial Economics Specialization in conjunction with this major (prime or second), and interested students should consult with the Academic Coordinator in the Department of Economics. [5, 7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Education
Requirements: Admission to WashU is both selective and competitive. The university receives applications from far more students than it is able to admit each year. Students who come to WashU have challenged themselves academically and personally during their high school years and are required breakouts to have earned a high school diploma or its equivalent, including home-schooled students and students holding a GED. Most applicants take advantage of honors, Advanced Placement and International Baccalaureate, and/or Dual Enrollment courses, if offered by their high schools. Important components of a student's application also include the following: The student's academic performance (transcript), including course selection, grades, and class rank, if provided by the secondary school; Counselor and teacher recommendations; Essays; Extracurricular and community involvement, including positive impacts on home and community (students who work for pay and/or have time-consuming family responsibilities should include this in their activity list); Standardized testing, if provided.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
Description: The Department of Electrical and Systems Engineering (ESE) offers students the opportunity to acquire in-depth knowledge and understanding of the fundamental principles in electrical and systems engineering. This education provides our graduates with a broad range of career opportunities in industry, government, and academia.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering (BSEE) degree program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the General Criteria and Electrical Engineering Program Criterion. [16]
CostPerCredit: $2,843 for each credit unit beyond 21 units

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English Literature
Description: The BA in English Literature seeks to help students develop linguistic and cultural fluency in literatures in English, the current global language, as well as competence in core and advanced critical thinking, analysis, communication, and research. The program aims at producing graduates who will contribute to the cultural, commercial, and intellectual welfare of their home country, and who will foster cultural exchange and understanding regionally and globally. The BA in English Literature prepares students for professional careers in education, research, publishing, business, and many other fields. Program objectives include reading and discussing a substantial number of complex works of literature and criticism, writing numerous analytical and informal assignments, interrogating the relationships between literary works and their historical and cultural contexts, and investigating the connections made by literature between individuals across time and space.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English Literature (Creative Writing)
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Arts in English Literature with a Creative Writing specialization is not a separate process from the general first-year application to Washington University in St. Louis. Students are admitted to an undergraduate division, such as the College of Arts & Sciences, and then declare their major. To complete the specialization, students must take five creative writing courses in a specific sequence, in addition to the other requirements for the English Literature major. All majors are also required to complete a portfolio capstone project to graduate. [11]
Concentration: English Literature Major, Creative Writing Specialization
Description: There is the option of completing an English Literature major with a creative writing specialization. [1] To do so, students must take five creative writing courses, including at least three upper-division courses. [1] Students will specialize in one particular genre — poetry, fiction, or creative nonfiction — and, ultimately, take a three-course sequence (2000-, 3000-, and 4000-level courses) in that genre while taking at least one course outside of the chosen genre. [1] Undergraduates who major in English explore literature as readers and writers in small classes that focus on the individual student. [3] The department's commitment to cross-fertilizing creative and critical literacy is genuine and longstanding. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Analysis
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Analysis is done through the general undergraduate admissions process for Washington University in St. Louis, not through a separate application to the major itself. Applicants can use either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. [5] General application requirements include the application form, high school transcript, and letters of recommendation. [3, 5] The university has a test-optional policy, meaning SAT or ACT scores are not required for full consideration. [5]
Description: The major in Environmental Analysis is a flexible, interdisciplinary 49-credit program that equips students with the scientific, social, and policy perspectives needed to address urgent environmental challenges. [3] It focuses on developing critical skills and competencies in interdisciplinary environmental problem-solving and is ideal for students seeking training focused on the environment and sustainability. [4] Through coursework in areas such as climate science, urban sustainability, environmental health, environmental justice, and ecological economics, students develop skills in scientific literacy, systems thinking, spatial analysis, field and laboratory methods, and evidence-based policymaking, along with strong communication abilities. [3] Experiential learning is central: students conduct fieldwork, GIS and lab analyses, take part in negotiation simulations, and work with community partners on real sustainability projects. [3] Capstone and reflective courses help students synthesize these experiences, preparing them to analyze complex problems and lead with creativity and scientific insight in careers across sustainability, policy, science, public health, advocacy, and entrepreneurship. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering (BSEnvE) degree program requires the satisfactory completion of a minimum of 126 units. This includes 26 units of physical and biological sciences, 21 units of mathematics and engineering computing, 43 units of core environmental engineering courses, 21 units of humanities, social sciences, and technical writing, and 15 units of environmental engineering and science electives. [19] For admission to the university, applicants must submit an online application, an official high school transcript, and one required essay. [11]
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering (BSEnvE) degree program is designed to provide students with comprehensive training in environmental engineering fundamentals. [11] The program of study consists of 26 units of physical and biological sciences (i.e., biology, chemistry, and physics); 21 units of mathematics and engineering computing; 43 units of core environmental engineering courses; 21 units of humanities, social sciences and technical writing; and 15 units of environmental engineering and science electives. [11] The environmental engineering electives permit students to tailor their studies toward specific goals. [11] Environmental engineers apply scientific and engineering principles to assess, manage and design sustainable systems for the protection of human and ecological health. [12] The designs and technologies that they develop provide safe and sufficient public water supplies, enable effective and efficient treatment and resource recovery from wastewater and other wastes, and control pollutant releases that protect water, soil and air quality. [12] Their broad training in basic sciences, mathematics, computational approaches, as well as a strong engineering foundation prepares environmental engineers to apply technological solutions within specific environmental and societal contexts. [12] Graduates are prepared to enter professional practice and to pursue graduate study in environmental engineering and allied fields. [7]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the General Criteria and the Environmental Engineering Program Criteria. [6, 11, 12, 13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Finance
Requirements: Application requirements are for first-year admission to the undergraduate school, not a specific major. Applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, which includes a personal essay, a list of extracurricular activities, a secondary school report, a counselor recommendation, and teacher evaluations. Official transcripts are also required.
Description: The Olin Business School offers a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration (BSBA) degree. BSBA students may select a major from the following disciplines: Accounting, Economics and Strategy, Entrepreneurship, Finance, Health Care Management, Marketing, Organization and Strategic Management, and Supply Chain, Operations, and Technology. The Finance major within the BSBA program equips students with the foundational knowledge and skills for careers in the financial industry.
Accredidation: The Olin Business School at Washington University in St. Louis holds triple accreditation from the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), the Association of MBAs (AMBA), and the EFMD Quality Improvement System (EQUIS). [3, 4, 5, 6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in French
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in French program is governed by the general undergraduate admissions process of Washington University in St. Louis. The university states that admission is both selective and competitive, and successful applicants have typically challenged themselves academically and personally. Applicants are required to have a high school diploma or its equivalent. [8] Most applicants have taken advantage of honors, Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, and/or Dual Enrollment courses if offered by their high schools. [8]
Description: As a French major, you will study great texts with an eye to gender roles, traditions, communities, individual freedom, social obligations, and many other topics of critical importance today You will also undertake a rigorous study of the French language. This major is housed in the Department of Romance Languages and Literatures. [11] Our courses initiate students into various modes of French cultural production and analysis, preparing them to study abroad. Such experiences enable them to pursue careers in international business, medicine, law, diplomacy, and the arts. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Germanic Languages and Literatures
Requirements: Students interested in studying German may declare German as their major or second major. Majors and second majors are required to complete 25 units of course work (GERMAN 2020 and above), at least 12 of which must be at the 4000 level, with a grade of C- or higher. [13] If students begin German at Washington University and follow the regular sequence of courses (GERMAN 1010 → GERMAN 1020 → GERMAN 2010), they will be ready to begin the German major after three semesters. [13] With the exception of GERMAN 3400 and its 1-unit discussion section (GERMAN 3401), only courses taught in German will count toward the major. [13] All majors and second majors are required to participate in the senior assessment interview in the final semester of their senior year. [14]
Description: The Department of Germanic Languages and Literatures at Washington University offers a diverse and challenging program of study that entails both the attainment of a proficiency in the language and a critical engagement with the history, culture, politics, and society in German-speaking countries from the Middle Ages to the present. [6] Such study is by its nature interdisciplinary, and thus, coursework in German can complement and enhance other field of study in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. [6] The department offers both a major and a minor in German studies for undergraduates. [6] As a Germanic languages and literatures major, you will study the German language intensively and explore German literature and culture from the Middle Ages to the present. [2] Additionally, you will have the opportunity to study German film, history, philosophy, and gender studies. [2] Many German majors choose to study abroad, either for a semester or a full academic year. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Healthcare Management
Accredidation: The Olin Business School, which offers the Bachelor of Science in Business Administration program, has earned triple accreditation from the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), the Association of MBAs (AMBA), and the EFMD Quality Improvement System (EQUIS). [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Hebrew
Requirements: Admission to WashU is both selective and competitive. The university receives applications from far more students than it is able to admit each year. Students who come to WashU have challenged themselves academically and personally during their high school years and are required to have earned a high school diploma or its equivalent, including home-schooled students and students holding a GED. Most applicants take advantage of honors, Advanced Placement and International Baccalaureate, and/or Dual Enrollment courses, if offered by their high schools. The undergraduate admissions committee reviews each application in a holistic and individualized-manner, with a goal of getting to know each student through the application process. [5]
Description: As a major in Hebrew, you can expect to gain proficiency in the language, study the area's literary and cultural landmarks, and gain familiarity with Near Eastern history and civilizations. [4] Whether you favor the study of language, literature, religion, history, or politics, you will find a way to deepen your appreciation of these complex and diverse societies and cultures. [4] This major is housed in the Department of Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Studies. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission, which includes applying to the Bachelor of Arts in History program, important components include the student's academic performance (transcript), counselor and teacher recommendations, essays, and extracurricular and community involvement. [2] A high school diploma or its equivalent is required. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Project in the Humanities
Requirements: The Interdisciplinary Project in the Humanities is a rigorous, interdisciplinary program for students seeking honors. The major combines 1) an introductory core - a concentrated study of texts central to the European and American philosophical, religious, and literary traditions and 2) an area of concentration - an advanced sequence of courses and research tailored to the special interests of each student in the program. [3]
Description: The Interdisciplinary Project in the Humanities is a rigorous, interdisciplinary program for students seeking honors. The major combines 1) an introductory core - a concentrated study of texts central to the European and American philosophical, religious, and literary traditions and 2) an area of concentration - an advanced sequence of courses and research tailored to the special interests of each student in the program. Accredidation: Information about the university’s accreditation can be found on the Office of the Provost website (https://provost.wustl.edu/assessment/accreditors/). Washington University in St. Louis is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International and Area Studies
Concentration: ['Development', 'Eurasian Studies', 'European Studies', 'Global Asias', 'Global Cultural Studies', 'International Affairs']
Description: As a global studies major, you will develop a broad understanding of the world, while exploring the diversity and richness of other cultures. Majors complete a four-semester sequence of language instruction in your chosen language program, and you choose a concentration in one of six specific areas: development, Eurasian studies, European studies, global Asias, global cultural studies, and international affairs. [13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Italian
Requirements: Application requirements are for admission to Washington University's undergraduate programs, not for a specific major. Students are admitted to one of the four undergraduate schools and then declare a major, typically during their sophomore year. [21] Declaration of a major like Italian generally requires a student to be in good academic standing and to complete the department's declaration process.
Description: As an Italian major, you will study the great Italian texts and will do so with an eye to gender roles, traditions, communities, individual freedom, social obligations and many other topics of critical importance today. You will also undertake a rigorous study of the Italian language. This major is housed in Romance Languages and Literatures. [13] Not only do our students achieve a high level of proficiency in Italian language with practical application for living and working in Italy, but we also offer extensive preparation in Italian literature, film, and culture, as well as opportunities for travel and study abroad. [8] The Italian program boasts an exceptionally dynamic and caring faculty expert in a range of established and cutting-edge subjects, including migration studies, medical humanities, Medieval and Renaissance literture, film studies, queer studies, museum studies, and the Slow Food movement. [8] Our small class sizes, interactive and proficiency-based language courses and popular culture courses draw students from the School of Engineering, Olin Business School, the Sam Fox School of Design and Visual Arts, and all major disciplines in Arts & Sciences, from biology to history and from literature to economics. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Japanese Language and Culture
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year students include the Common Application or Coalition Application, a $75 application fee or fee waiver, a transcript, a school report, a counselor recommendation, and one teacher recommendation. An essay, which is part of the Common or Coalition Application, is also required.
Description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) offers a unified major and minor in East Asian Languages and Cultures, which allows students to explore three linguistic and cultural traditions: Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. Students may pursue a focused approach to their studies by studying one of our languages, and they may choose among the range of non-language courses to enhance their grounding in the East Asian nation of their choice. Students may also choose to study across disciplinary and geographic boundaries. Majors who opt to focus their requirements in one of our three East Asia civilizations may earn a specialization in Chinese, Japanese or Korean that will appear on the transcript after graduation. [6, 11] Our language programs offer a full sequence of courses in Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. [6] The emphasis in the East Asian Language and Culture programs is on achieving high competency in the relevant language and learning how to read texts from the target culture—literary, philosophical, cultural, historical, or even visual—with an informed appreciation of the contexts in which they were produced. [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Studies
Requirements: To apply for first-year admission, students must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, a $75 nonrefundable application fee (or waiver), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [5] The application includes essays. [5] Admission to Washington University is selective and competitive, and the review process is holistic, considering academic potential, personal characteristics, and accomplishments. [5]
Concentration: ['Comparative Jewish and Islamic Studies', 'Modern Middle Eastern Studies']
Description: Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Studies is an academic department, unique in North America, in which Jewish Studies and Islamic Studies are integrated. It is an interdisciplinary department whose purpose is to explore the historical experience, literary, religious and cultural expression, and political and material life of the Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern civilizations. [3] Whether you favor the study of language, literature, religion, history, or politics, you will find in our courses a way to deepen your appreciation of these complex and diverse societies and cultures. [3] You will also be encouraged to explore the interaction of Jews and Muslims with neighboring societies and cultures in the Middle East, Europe, North Africa, and other parts of the world. [3] As a major in Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Studies (JIMES), you can expect to gain proficiency in a language, study the area's literary and cultural landmarks, and gain familiarity with Middle Eastern history and civilizations. [2] You will focus on one of two concentrations: Comparative Jewish and Islamic Studies or Modern Middle Eastern Studies. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Korean Language and Culture
Concentration: East Asian Languages and Cultures Major, Korean Specialization
Description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) offers majors and a minor that allow for cross-cultural and interdisciplinary approaches to the study of East Asia. Students can choose either to focus on one of our three linguistic and cultural traditions — Chinese, Japanese, and Korean — or to explore different traditions and societies by taking courses about multiple religions regions*. The emphasis in the EALC programs (with specializations in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean) is on achieving high competency in the relevant language and learning how to read texts from the target culture — literary, philosophical, cultural, historical, or even visual — with an informed appreciation of the contexts in which they were produced. [4] Our language programs also foster the ability to negotiate meaning in a culturally and contextually appropriate manner through the development of high levels of proficiency in speaking, listening, reading, and writing. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Latin American Studies
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate study at Washington University in St. Louis, prospective students must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (which can be waived), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. The application review is holistic, considering academic performance, recommendations, essays, and extracurricular involvement. [7]
Description: As a Latin American studies major, you will pursue an in-depth study of Latin America across diverse disciplines, theoretical approaches and historical periods. The major offers a sound, updated, and competitive approach to the study of the region both in its specificity and in its connections to the world, through the study of Latin America's processes of internationalization and its changing position in global scenarios.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics
Requirements: For undergraduate admission, the necessary components include the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 application fee, and an optional writing supplement. [5] Graduate program applicants must have earned a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. [8] Application materials for graduate studies are submitted online and specific requirements may vary by program. [8]
Description: At Washington University, the Linguistics program offers an undergraduate major and minor. The core of the Linguistics program focuses on the study of how languages are structured. [15] Students examine how words are built from sounds, how sentences are built from words, and how all of this structure manages to communicate meaning. [15] With a good understanding of these formal properties, students can pursue other questions about language. [15] How does language change over time? Do diverse languages have more in common than meets the eye? What functions does language play in society? What is its relation to thought? What are its biological and psychological underpinnings? And just how do children manage to acquire language so well in the first place? [15] Linguistics takes a scientific approach to the study of language and develops skills in data analysis and scientific experimental methods. [15] Linguistics students may or may not speak many languages, but they definitely will learn how to collect and analyze data about languages in an effort to answer these questions. [15]
CostPerCredit: If students enroll in more than 21 units per semester, they will pay additional tuition of $2,843 for each credit unit beyond 21 units. [27]
ScholarshipAmount: Up to full tuition. [24]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available. [23]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Leadership and Strategic Management
Requirements: Application is for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Business Administration (BSBA) program at the Olin Business School, not a specific major. Students declare a major, such as Organization and Strategic Management, in their sophomore year. [14, 15] The admissions process is a holistic review that considers academic achievement, extracurricular activities, personal essays, and recommendations.
Description: Learn how to lead in any industry and shape the workplace of the future. Courses address the fundamentals of leadership as well as specific critical issues facing our organizations today, including government regulation, mindfulness and performance, and global strategy. [1] Organization and Strategic Management (OSM) prepares students to be an effective leader grounded in a strong value system. [2] OSM includes the study of the intersection of leadership, strategy and organizational behavior, which prepares you for a wide variety of careers. [2] Both qualitative and quantitative skills are imperative in OSM to strategically develop, manage and structure the people of the organization. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics
Requirements: To complete an application, Washington University in St. Louis requires the Common Application or Coalition Application, a $75 nonrefundable fee (which is automatically waived for students applying for financial aid), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [5] The university's admission process is selective and competitive, and they look for students who have challenged themselves academically through honors, Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, or Dual Enrollment courses if available at their high school. [5] Important components of the application include academic performance (transcript), counselor and teacher recommendations, essays, and extracurricular and community involvement. [5]
Description: As a mathematics major, you will study numbers and their operations, interrelations, combinations, generalizations, and abstraction. When you study mathematics, you are really exploring the "language of science"— not just the traditional physical sciences and engineering, but also the quantitative side of economics, biology, the behavioral sciences, business, and architecture. [10] Other majors view mathematics as an interesting concentration in their liberal arts education, even though they plan to enter professional fields such as medicine or law. The Mathematics program gives majors and minors a broad introduction to the subject. [14] To fit students' varying academic interests and professional goals, the department offers majors in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, and Mathematical Sciences, along with two dual majors in Mathematics and Computer Science and in Mathematics and Economics. Majors are encouraged to complete additional work (perhaps even a minor or a second major) in other related areas. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics and Statistics
Requirements: To be considered for first-year admission, a student's application file must be complete with the following materials: the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (which is automatically waived for students applying for financial aid), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [11] Admission is selective and competitive, and the review process is holistic and individualized, assessing academic potential, personal characteristics, and accomplishments. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics and Computer Science
Requirements: Washington University in St. Louis accepts the Common Application or the Coalition Application. Applicants must also submit a high school transcript, a counselor recommendation, and at least one teacher recommendation. The university has a test-optional policy for ACT and SAT scores.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics and Economics
Description: Mathematics and statistics are essential in all aspects of economics. At the same time, Economics is a natural application outlet for statisticians and mathematicians. The dual-degree major in Mathematics and Economics will allow students interested in both disciplines to efficiently combine them without pursuing them as two separate majors. Upon completion, majors will be able to follow career paths in economics that require solid quantitative training. The combination of the two fields could also provide a well-grounded basis to pursue doctoral studies in other areas in the social sciences and public policy, business, and law school.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Description: The curriculum prepares the student for professional prac­tice or post­gradu­ate ed­u­ca­tion in a broad spec­trum of me­chan­i­cal and other en­gi­neer­ing or pro­fes­sional fields. It pro­vides crit­i­cal knowl­edge in solid me­chan­ics, fluid me­chan­ics, ther­mo­dy­nam­ics and heat trans­fer, ma­te­ri­als sci­ence, dy­nam­ics and con­trol, and de­sign. It in­cludes 34 units of math­e­mat­ics and ba­sic sci­ences, 58 units of en­gi­neer­ing top­ics, and 28 units of gen­eral ed­u­ca­tion for a to­tal de­gree re­quire­ment of 120 units. The general education requirement includes 18 units of social science and humanities. Core courses must be taken for credit (i.e., for a grade). The social science and humanities courses may be taken on a pass/no pass basis. The un­der­grad­u­ate pro­gram pro­vides the nec­es­sary foun­da­tions in these ar­eas and the op­por­tu­nity to spe­cial­ize in top­ics of par­tic­u­lar in­ter­est. Spe­cial­iza­tion is ac­com­plished via the ju­di­cious choice of en­gi­neer­ing elec­tives taken as 3000-, 4000-, or 5000-level courses ap­proved by the stu­dent's ad­vi­sor. At the end of the four-year pro­gram, the stu­dent is ready to go on to grad­u­ate ed­u­ca­tion or into re­search or pro­fes­sional prac­tice.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Mechanical Engineering program criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Music, prospective students must first apply for general admission to Washington University. There is not a separate application or audition required for the B.A. in Music program at the time of university admission. [13, 16] The general application requirements include the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (with waivers available), a teacher recommendation, a school report, official transcripts, and essays. [3] While a resume is not explicitly required, the application considers extracurricular and community involvement. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music
Description: The Bachelor of Music is a pre-professional degree, which combines core coursework in performance, music history, music theory, musicianship, and keyboard skills with advanced studies in a specific area of interest. [31] Students earning this degree must complete significant coursework in the Music Department according to their area of concentration, and they must pass a piano proficiency exam. [31]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Marketing
Requirements: To be considered for admission, applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, a $75 nonrefundable application fee (or a fee waiver), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. Description: Our marketing major immerses you not only in the fundamentals of market research but also in such niche topics as business experiments, pricing strategies and innovations. Experiential learning opportunities allow you to learn the art and science of sales well before you graduate.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to full tuition scholarships are available. [19]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available. [13, 15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Operations and Supply Chain Management

Applicants can use the Common Application or Coalition Application. ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy

[22]
Concentration: ['Philosophy Research Specialization', 'Law and Policy Specialization', 'Philosophy of Science Specialization']
Description: As a philosophy major, you will consider the central questions of human life, such as: “what is truth?”; “is there a God?”; and “what is a just society?” These philosophical ponderings are basic to the ways in which we think about ourselves and our world. Courses in philosophy focus on the writings of great thinkers, past and present, who have sought a better understanding of human beings and the world. Majors can also choose from 3 specializations of more specific study: philosophy research, law and policy, and philosophy of science.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy (Law and Policy Track)
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission, applicants must submit their high school transcript(s), an application, and a nonrefundable $75 application fee (or fee waiver). [6] For the Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy with a Law and Policy specialization, majors must complete at least one course in each of the three Core Areas (History of Philosophy; Value Theory; and Metaphysics, and Epistemology). [10] Additionally, all philosophy majors are required to complete a capstone experience, either by writing an honors thesis or by taking the Philosophy Capstone Course (PHIL 3990). [10]
Description: This specialization is especially recommended for students who intend to pursue a career in law or public policy. The specialization involves taking certain specific courses for the major (and possibly a few extra courses) that will provide the student with additional preparation and a competitive edge when applying to law school, postgraduate programs in public policy, and related jobs. [6, 7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy-Neuroscience-Psychology
Requirements: The general application requirements for first-year admission include the Common Application or Coalition Application, a school report and official transcript, a teacher evaluation, and a counselor recommendation. [3]
Description: Philosophy-Neuroscience-Psychology (PNP) is an interdisciplinary program that provides an opportunity to examine the mind from multiple perspectives. Students who choose to major in PNP will learn to bring some of the newest findings in science to bear on some of the oldest questions in philosophy; they will also see new questions emerge and learn to pursue those questions as well. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics
Requirements: Admission to Washington University is selective and competitive. The university reviews each application in a holistic and individualized manner. The admissions committee assesses academic potential, personal characteristics, and accomplishments. Applicants are required to have a high school diploma or equivalent. Recommended secondary school coursework includes four years of English, four years of mathematics, three to four years of history or social science, three to four years of laboratory science, and at least two years of the same foreign language. [21]
Description: The goal of the major program is to provide undergraduate students with an outstanding education in physics as preparation for successful careers in graduate school or in the workplace.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate programs at Washington University in St. Louis, applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. [3] The university uses a holistic review process. [5] Required documents include high school transcripts. [5] WashU has a test-optional policy, meaning the submission of SAT or ACT scores is at the applicant's discretion. [8] For international applicants where English is a second language, proof of English proficiency through tests like TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo is required, though waivers can be sought. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Description: The Department of Political Science offers a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science. The program provides a systematic look at fundamental problems that face human society, such as world peace, government policies aimed at economic stability and growth, and the management of environmental quality. The curriculum also delves into control over political competition, the potential for social and political change through law, and the wealth gap both in the U.S. and internationally. The major's purpose is to address these issues while raising broad theoretical questions that connect contemporary political debates with a 2,000-year-old theoretical tradition. Students can choose to pursue a general political science major or select from one of eight concentrations: American politics, comparative politics, data analytics, international relations, political theory, public law, public policy, and race, ethnicity, and politics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychological & Brain Sciences
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission, you generally need a secondary school diploma or its equivalent. The recommended high school curriculum includes 4 years of English, 4 years of mathematics, 3-4 years of laboratory science, 3-4 years of history or social science, and at least 2 years of the same foreign language. [1] The application is submitted through the Common Application, which includes an essay.
Concentration: ['Cognition in Children', 'Cognitive Neuroscience', 'Experimental Psychopathology', 'Lifespan Development', 'Personality and Individual Differences', 'Reading, Language, and Language Acquisition']
Description: As the science concerned with the study of behavior, psychology includes diverse areas of study, including: biological bases of behavior; brain-behavior interactions; learning; memory; cognition; motivation; sensation and perception; the study of social interactions, persuasion, and attitudes; aging and development; personality; clinical, abnormal, and health psychology; and leisure and work experiences. Our mission is to educate our Psychological & Brain Sciences majors in the discipline's core aspects, questions, theories, and approaches. A major in our department can include more focused study in a specific area, and possibly the completion of one of our concentrations.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Field-Specific, Identity-based, Community service, Military-affiliated, Employer-sponsored

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychological & Brain Sciences (Cognitive Neuroscience)
Requirements: Acceptance into the major is contingent upon an application and approval by the major committee for students already enrolled at Washington University. A brief, one-page statement explaining why the cognitive neuroscience major is appropriate for the student is requested as part of this internal application process. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies
Requirements: The major in Religious Studies requires a minimum of 30 units, with 24 units being at the 3000 level or higher. All grades for the major must be C- or better. The requirements include: 6 units of required foundational courses (REST 1501 and REST 3635), a 3-unit senior capstone experience (such as REST 4801 or an honors thesis), and 21 units of elective courses, of which 18 must be at the 3000-level or higher. [18]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Romance Languages and Literatures
Requirements: The major in Romance languages and literatures requires a minimum of 42 units at the 3000 and 4000 levels, distributed among French, Italian, and Spanish. Students must earn a grade of B- or better in these courses, with an overall B average. [2] The program also necessitates a writing-intensive course and a capstone experience, with further details available on the department's website. [2]
Description: Romance Languages and Literatures offers vibrant programs in French, Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish. Our language courses have long been popular with undergraduates, including those interested in international travel and those who anticipate a global dimension to their future careers. All of our classes focus on culture writ large: we study great texts, and we do so with an eye toward gender roles, traditions, communities, individual freedom, social obligations, and many other topics of critical importance today. We offer concentrations in French, Italian, Spanish, and introductory Portuguese, as well as a composite major in Romance Languages. Our undergraduate programs in French, Italian, and Spanish include a compelling series of language, literature, culture, and civilization courses that introduce students to the global Hispanic, Francophone, and Italophone communities. [8] The curriculum affords students the opportunity to become fluent in a foreign language, enrich their historical and cultural understanding, and acquaint themselves with influential intellectual, literary, and artistic traditions. [8] Students also benefit from linguistic and cultural immersion opportunities through our many summer, semester, and year-long study abroad programs. To prepare our students to take full advantage of such opportunities, our faculty provides an innovative range of courses that combine the study of literature with contemporaneous developments in philosophy, science, music, art, and theory. For undergraduates interested in cross-language study, students may elect to major in Romance Languages and Literatures. This major requires advanced coursework in French, Italian, and Spanish, with one of the three languages as the focus of primary emphasis. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology
Description: As a major in sociology, you will explore the ways in which social relations and settings shape a range of individual and group experiences and outcomes, with an emphasis on how various forms of inequality are created and propagated through time. Reflecting the diversity of social settings that motivate sociological inquiry, majors will develop a sociological lens through which they can better understand the baseline determinants of inequality, social order, and change. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish
