Requirements: For an application file to be considered complete, Washington University in St. Louis requires the submission of the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (which is automatically waived for students applying for financial aid), and all necessary additional materials as specified in the Office of Undergraduate Admissions guidelines. [9] These materials include a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [9] Important elements of a student's application also consist of their academic performance (transcript), including course selection, grades, and class rank (if provided); counselor and teacher recommendations; essays; and extracurricular and community involvement. [9]
Description: Speaking Spanish is the key to unlocking the cultures, traditions, and experiences of 20 different countries throughout the world. From the medieval knights and Don Quixote through the modern novels by prize-winning authors and the world of film, the Spanish faculty at the Department of Romance Languages and Literatures guides students of Spanish into the unexpected territories of Europe and Latin America, territories that are as rich geographically as they are culturally.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Systems Science & Engineering
Requirements: Washington University in St. Louis accepts the Common Application or Coalition Application. Applicants are expected to have a strong college preparatory program that includes four years of English, and three to four years of mathematics, science, history/social science, and a foreign language. Specific requirements for the Bachelor of Science in Systems Science & Engineering are not listed separately from the general undergraduate admissions requirements.
Concentration: ['Biomedical Engineering', 'Chemical Engineering', 'Computer Science & Engineering', 'Electrical Engineering', 'Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science']
Description: The Systems Science and Engineering program is ideal for students interested in math, physics and computing; business, finance or financial engineering; or applied mathematics. The Bachelor of Science in Systems Science & Engineering (BSSSE) program lays the engineering and mathematical foundations for modeling, analyzing and designing complex systems and highlights their applications in contemporary engineering and scientific application domains. [2] The systems science and engineering program at the McKelvey School of Engineering prepares students to view an entire system of components as an entity piuttosto than as an assembly of individual parts. [4] Each component is designed to fit properly with the other components rather than to function by itself. The engineering and mathematics of systems is a rapidly developing field. It is one of the most modern segments of applied mathematics, as well as an engineering discipline. It is concerned with the identification, modeling, analysis, design and control of systems that are potentially as large and complex as the U.S. economy or as precise and vital as a space voyage. [4]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Systems Science and Engineering (BSSSE) degree program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the General Criteria. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Urban Studies
Bachelor of Arts in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
Requirements: Important components of a student's application include their academic performance (transcript), counselor and teacher recommendations, essays, and extracurricular and community involvement. [14] Washington University in St. Louis accepts the Common Application. [13]

ProgramName: Associate in Arts
Requirements: The Associate in Arts degree is open only to WashU employees and partner program students. To receive an Associate in Arts degree from WashU Continuing & Professional Studies (CAPS), students must be admitted to degree candidacy; complete a minimum of 60 units of college-level work with a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or higher; and satisfy specific writing, course distribution, and residency requirements.

ProgramName: Associate in Arts in Pre-Nursing
Requirements: The Associate in Arts degree is open only to WashU employees and partner program students. [2, 4] Formal admission is required for all students seeking undergraduate degrees at the School of Continuing & Professional Studies (CAPS). [1] The program is designed for students to complete prerequisites for a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN). [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Accounting
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. The required supporting materials include a School Report and Official Transcript, a Teacher Evaluation, and a Counselor Recommendation. Additionally, applicants must provide a 250-word response to the question, "Please tell us what you are interested in studying at college and why." [17, 18] A portfolio is required for students applying to the College of Art and strongly encouraged for those applying to the College of Architecture. [18]
Description: The Accounting Minor (Non-BSBA) requires a total of 15 credits. The prerequisites for the minor include courses in Calculus, Microeconomics, and Statistics. [4] The required courses are Principles of Financial Accounting, Principles of Managerial Accounting, and Intermediate Financial Accounting I: Finance-related topics. [4] Students must also complete at least 6 credits of accounting electives from a provided list. [4]
Accredidation: The Olin Business School, which houses the accounting program, is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International). [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: The minor in aerospace engineering requires a minimum of 15 units of courses. The minor in aerospace engineering is available to all undergraduates. To find out more about this minor, contact the department chair or the advisor for the minor in aerospace engineering. [5]
Description: Whether students are intent franchising a profession in aviation or simply enthusiastic about space and flight, a minor in aerospace engineering can satisfy their scientific curiosity, prepare them for a job, or uncover contributions. The minor in aerospace engineering is available to all undergraduates, but it is most attractive to those pursuing a degree in mechanical engineering. The minor in aerospace engineering requires a minimum of 15 units of courses selected from the list below; it is possible to earn the minor without increasing the number of units (120) required for the Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering (BSME). Aerospace engineering deals with the analysis, design and performance of flight vehicles such as transport and military aircraft, helicopters, missiles and launch vehicles, and spacecraft. Students learn about aerospace engineering by taking courses in aerodynamics, aircraft flight dynamics and control, aerospace propulsion, aerospace structures and aerospace vehicle design. Students may also have the opportunity to gain experience in aerospace engineering design through collaborative programs with local companies such as Boeing. Aerospace engineers from industry teach courses as adjunct instructors at Washington University, and many Washington University faculty members have extensive aerospace industry experience.

ProgramName: Minor in African and African-American Studies
Requirements: The minor in African and African American Studies requires a total of 19 units of coursework with a minimum grade of C- or higher. Students are required to take AFAS 1002 Foundations in African & African-American Studies (1 unit) and AFAS 2550 Introduction to Africana Studies (3 units). The remaining 15 units must be selected at the 3000 level or above, in consultation with an advisor. A maximum of 6 credits earned through study abroad or transfer may be applied. [3]
Description: As an African and African-American studies (AFAS) minor, you will explore the social, political and intellectual history as well as the literature, culture, and artistic life of various peoples in the world who are African or of African descent. [2] Courses are offered in the humanities, social sciences, and the performing arts. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in American Culture Studies
Requirements: Total Units Required: 15 units, at least 9 of which must be at the 3000 level or higher. All courses counting toward the AMCS minor must be taken for a letter grade, and students must receive a grade of C– or higher. [2]
Concentration: ['Race & Ethnicity', 'Gender & Sexuality', 'Ability & the Body', 'Place, Space, & the Environment', 'Popular Culture', 'Citizenship, Nationhood, & Identity', 'Archives & Texts', 'Audio, Visual, & Material Studies', 'Journalism & Ethnography', 'Law, Politics, & Policy Studies', 'Digital Methods']
Description: The minor in American Culture Studies allows students to pursue an interconnected understanding of American history, culture, and society using multiple perspectives and methodologies from the humanities and social sciences. [2] American Culture Studies (AMCS) at Washington University is a multidisciplinary program that provides both a broader context for study in different fields and a deeper understanding of American culture in all of its complexities. [4, 10] Of particular interest are the political, social, and material dimensions of American culture—past and present—and issues of race, gender, sexuality, and class that spur so much cultural debate and expression. [10] To address these areas, the program has several initiatives, including: modern segregation, race and popular music, American intimacies, and visual and material culture. [10]

ProgramName: Minor in Ancient Studies
Requirements: Total Units Required: 15. Ancient Studies follows the Arts & Sciences minimum grade requirement of C- or better for courses that apply to the minor. [4] Students may apply up to a maximum number of 6 credits to their minor earned through study abroad and/or transfer credits. [4] Courses that count toward the minor may include CLASSICS 1000-4999, GREEK 1000-4999, or LATIN 1000-2999, as well as approved interdisciplinary courses. [4] Of the 15 required units, students must complete at least 3 additional units at the 3000 level or above. [4]
Description: The ancient studies minor requires the completion of 15 units. Ancient Studies is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to explore the ancient world. Students can create a program of study that is of particular interest to them. At least two of the five required courses must be in the Department of Classics. Students are encouraged to take courses from other departments, including the departments of Art History and Archaeology, History, Philosophy, and Religious Studies.

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology
Requirements: Total Units Required: 18 units. Students must earn a grade of C- or better. Pass/No Pass grades do not count for the minor. Students must complete 12 elective units, at least 9 of which must be at the 3000 level or higher. [7]
Description: As an anthropology minor, you'll study human existence in the present and the past to explore how and why humans vary in their behaviors, cultures, and biology. [12] Students choose to study anthropology because they want to understand some of the most intriguing and troubling issues faced by modern society: the origin and meaning of ethnic and gender differences; the role of institutions in social, political and economic life; learned vs. innate behavior; the similarities and differences among human societies; and the meaning of religion, community and family. [12] The department offers a major and minor in anthropology, as well as optional global health and environment tracks. [15] Anthropology minors may choose an optional specialization called Global Health and Environment (GHE) if the student's interests lie primarily within this area of anthropology. [8]
ScholarshipAmount: Up to full tuition

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology: Global Health and Environment
Requirements: For first-year U.S. citizen/permanent resident applicants, the required application components include a school report and official transcript, teacher evaluation, and a counselor recommendation. [3] A portfolio is required for students applying to the College of Art and strongly encouraged for those applying to the College of Architecture. [3]
Description: As an anthropology minor in the global health and environment specialization, you will study the most important contemporary issues facing health care and the environment. [2] You will focus on global health, which concerns itself with the broad ways that humans address and cope with issues of health, illness, and well-being in cross-cultural and cross-temporal perspectives. [2] Because issues of health, healing, and wellness are situated in an environmental context (especially the natural physical environment but also the human built and created environment), it is essential that the study of human health be understood within a broad environmental framework. [3] Within Global Health and Environment, students will also have the opportunity to look at the human body within an evolutionary framework, understanding how evolution has shaped the human body and contributed to contemporary patterns of health and disease through course work in human anatomy, paleoanthropology, osteology, genetics, biological development and studies of non-human primates. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Applied Linguistics
Requirements: Units required: 15. All students participating in the minor must have a declared primary major. Minors must receive a grade of C+ or higher in all Applied Linguistics courses; all courses taken for APL credit must be taken for a letter grade, including language courses. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Applied Microeconomics
Requirements: Total Units Required: 22-24; Grade Requirement: All courses in the minor (including Mathematics) must be completed with the letter grade option, and a grade of at least C– must be earned in each course. Required Courses: ECON 1501, ECON 1502, ECON 4001, MATH 1510 or MATH 1515, MATH 1520, and MATH 4830 or MATH 2130. Elective Courses: One (3-unit) Economics elective with ECON 1501 and/or ECON 1502 as a prerequisite, and one (3-unit) Economics elective with ECON 4001 as a prerequisite. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Arabic
Requirements: The minor in Arabic requires a minimum of 18 total units, in addition to prerequisites. A minimum of 9 units must be at the 3000 level or above. Students must earn grades of B- or higher in each language course to advance to the next level, and no course taken Pass/No Pass can count toward the minor. The goal is to achieve language proficiency at the 2000 level or above. Students who place into ARAB 2011 Intermediate Arabic II or higher are required to complete two consecutive semesters of Arabic language instruction at Washington University. [8, 10] There is also a required foundational course to be chosen from either JIMES 2081 Introduction to Jewish Civilization: History and Identity or JIMES 2100 Introduction to Islamic Civilization. [8]
Description: As a minor in Arabic, you can expect to gain familiarity with the language, and foray into Near Eastern literature, culture, history and civilizations. [1] Whether you focus on just one of these areas or sample a little of each, you will deepen your appreciation of these complex and diverse societies and cultures. [1] This minor is housed in the Department Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Studies. [1]
ScholarshipAmount: Multiple full-tuition and partial-tuition scholarships are available through Signature Scholar Programs; the Howard Nemerov Writing Scholars Program offers $3,000 scholarships. [22, 23]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships are available, such as the Signature Scholar Programs which also consider leadership and community service. [2, 22, 25]

ProgramName: Minor in Archaeology
Requirements: To minor in Archaeology, students must complete at least 27 units of relevant coursework comprised of: 10 units of core courses, 2-5 units of methods and skills courses, 5 units of theory courses, and 10 units of elective courses. [2] The process for adding a minor is to declare it through the university's Workday system. [14]
Description: The Minor in Archaeology provides an introduction to the study of the material remains of past societies and is appropriate for students of all majors who are interested in the ancient world. This minor is not intended for students who are majoring in archaeology, and it is not a prerequisite for the major. Students who are majoring in archaeology are not eligible to have this minor. The archaeology minor is designed to be as flexible as possible to serve a variety of student interests.

ProgramName: Minor in Architectural History and Theory
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts
Description: The Minor in Architectural History and Theory introduces foundational aspects of visual literacy and critical analysis of architecture in terms of its cultural resonance and social impact. [3] Students study the built environment, including cities, buildings, and landscapes on every continent throughout human history. [3] The program is designed for students interested in preservation or the history and theory of architecture. [1] It aims to help students develop expertise in visual analysis and verbal expression, which is ideal for a general liberal arts education or for pre-professional preparation to write, teach, and curate as an architectural historian. [3] The minor engages with diverse methods and perspectives, examining the place, time, material, technology, forms, concepts, ideals, and identities that shape and are shaped by environments and buildings. [3] The program is open to all students at Washington University in St. Louis. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Architecture
Requirements: The Minor in Architecture is open to all students at Washington University in St. Louis outside of the College of Architecture. Students interested in the minor should contact the minor advisor. A total of 15 units are required. [2]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts
Description: The Minor in Architecture is intended to introduce students to architecture fundamentals and to cultivate an appreciation for buildings, cities, and environments and their role in society. [5] The minor includes foundational coursework, such as ARCH 1144 Architecture for Non-Architects or ARCH 1110 Introduction to Design Processes I, which provides an overview of the discipline by highlighting contemporary issues of architecture worldwide with a focus on introductory methods of design and representation. [5] The minor also includes architectural history courses, highlighting the importance of global historical and cultural contexts, and open architecture electives, allowing students to explore their own interests. [5] The Minor in Architecture is open to all students at Washington University in St. Louis outside of the College of Architecture. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Art History and Archaeology
Requirements: The minor in Art History and Archaeology consists of 18 credit hours: 2 courses at the introductory level and 4 courses at an advanced level. [6] These courses may not be taken under the Pass/No Pass or Credit/No Credit option. [6] Students must earn a grade of C- or better in all classes. [6] At least two of the 3000-level courses must be completed in residence at Washington University. [6]
Description: The Department of Art History & Archaeology at Washington University in St. Louis offers a minor for students interested in the field. [3] Those who pursue the minor will examine a wide array of visual culture, placing objects within their broader political and social contexts. [4] The program requires the completion of 18 credit hours, which includes two introductory-level courses and four advanced-level courses. [3] Students are also encouraged to combine their studies with other related fields such as anthropology, classics, history, literature, philosophy, religion, and foreign languages to gain a more comprehensive education. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Asian American Studies
Requirements: The minor in Asian American Studies does not have application requirements such as a resume or statement of purpose. Instead, it has course requirements for students who are already enrolled at Washington University. The requirements include completing 12 units of core courses and 12 units of upper-division courses. [2]
Description: As a minor in Asian American Studies, you will enrich your critical understanding about both individual experiences and collective histories of Asian Americans in regional, national, and transnational contexts. As an inter- and multi-disciplinary program, it underlines transnational contexts and comparative perspectives for the study of Asian American experiences. [6] The Asian American Studies minor at WashU is designed to build and sustain the spirit of critical inquiry in and beyond the classroom to students' professional and personal lives. [7] As an inter- and multi-disciplinary program, the minor privileges an intersectional approach that showcases the varied ethnic, national, linguistic, and systemic collaborations that constitute Asian Americanness. [7] Reflective of the collective strength of our faculty, the minor facilitates intellectual exchanges and academic inquiries surrounding Asian American histories, migration, cultures, race, labor, justice, gender, sexualities, disabilities, popular culture, representations, food, environment, materiality, and many other interdisciplinary areas. [7] Through community engagement, research, critical thinking, and professional engagement, the minor focuses on holistic student growth that continues the spirit of intervention, action, and change through scholarly and community settings. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Astrophysics and Astroparticle Physics
Requirements: To declare the Minor in Astrophysics and Astroparticle Physics, students must be enrolled at Washington University. The general requirements for minors within the Physics department state that all courses listed for the minor must be completed with a grade of C- or better, and at least half of them must be completed in residence at Washington University. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Bioinformatics
Requirements: Total Units Required: 23-24 units. The minor is a collaboration between the Department of Biology and the Department of Computer Science & Engineering. Arts & Sciences students will be assigned an advisor in Biology, while students from other schools will be advised by the Computer Science & Engineering department. A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses to count toward the minor. A maximum of one course taken outside of Washington University may be applied. [7]
Description: Mindful of the emerging opportunities at the interface of biology and computer science, the Department of Biology and the Department of Computer Science & Engineering have fashioned the minor in bioinformatics. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Biology
Requirements: To declare a minor in Biology, students must submit a declaration through the university's online portal, WebSTAC. [7] The requirements to complete the minor are a total of 32 units, with 18 units in biology and 14 units in chemistry. [10] All courses for the minor must be taken for a letter grade, and a grade of C- or better must be achieved in all of them. [10, 11] Required courses include Principles of Biology I & II, General Chemistry I & II with labs, and Organic Chemistry I with lab, in addition to 10 units of advanced biology electives. [11]
Description: As a biology minor, you will study the vital processes of all organisms and the environments in which they flourish. Biologists study living things at levels ranging from interactions among whole populations of organisms to the molecular mechanisms of cellular chemistry. [12]

ProgramName: Minor in Biomedical Engineering
Minor in Biomedical Physics
Requirements: Given the lack of a centralized general application requirements page on the specified Washington University in St. Louis websites, specific institute-level document requirements like a resume, statement of purpose, or writing sample are not explicitly defined as universally required or optional. These requirements are typically determined at the individual school or program level. For undergraduate applicants, the university utilizes a holistic review process. Washington University has extended its test-optional policy for undergraduate applicants, allowing them to choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores. [16]
Description: This minor is for students interested in the discussion and application of methods and techniques from physics to topics in the areas of biology and medicine. The program may be of interest to the pre-medicine student or the research-oriented science major.

ProgramName: Minor in Business of the Arts
Description: The Olin Business School offers a Minor in the Business of Arts to any undergraduate day division student. The Business of the Arts minor equips you to successfully navigate the “creative tension” between the artistic pursuit and economic necessity.

ProgramName: Minor in Business of Entertainment
Requirements: To pursue the Business of Entertainment Minor (for non-BSBA students), individuals must be current students at Washington University. The primary requirements involve completing prerequisite courses, including Calculus II and a statistics course. [11] After fulfilling the prerequisites, students can declare the minor online through Workday. [2] There is no mention of a separate application process or submission of documents like a resume or statement of purpose to declare the minor.
Description: The minor, which will be open to undergraduates in all of Washington University's divisions, is designed to provide students with an understanding of the entertainment field and to prepare them for success in the business side of the industry. [5] Following the creation of a business of sports minor, the addition of a business of entertainment minor to the business school curriculum continues a general push to create interdisciplinary opportunities that will give students skills that are applicable to their lives after graduation. [5] To further the minor's interdisciplinary reach, students will be required to take three of their 15 units outside of Olin. [5] The course options, which include classes in the film and media studies and American culture studies departments, seek to provide perspective on the media industry and its culture. [5] The business of entertainment's keystone course, the Economics of Entertainment, will be offered this fall and is taught by MacDonald. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Business of Social Impact
Requirements: To declare the Minor in Business of Social Impact, there are no application requirements specified on the official Washington University in St. Louis website. Students must complete 15 credits, including required courses such as MGT 4604 Business of Social Impact and OB 4720 Defining Moments: Lessons in Leadership and Character From the Top, along with electives from designated groups. [3, 5]
Description: The Business of Social Impact minor is offered to students in any undergraduate division at Washington University. This minor is for students who want to use business as a tool to create social and environmental impact. The minor in Business of Social Impact will equip students with the mindset, knowledge, and skills to create a better, more just, and more sustainable world.

ProgramName: Minor in Business of Sports
Description: This undergraduate minor prepares you for whatever challenges come your way in the increasingly demanding field of sports management. The sports industry generates more than $70 billion in revenue in North America annually. And it continues to grow and attract enthusiastic new fans every season. The Business of Sports program equips you to better understand the business aspects of sports management so you can rise to the top of this dynamic field. If you're looking for an exciting future career in sports, this is the program for you. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Chemistry
Requirements: To complete a minor in chemistry, students must take a total of 41 units, with 27 in chemistry and 14 in math and physics. [13, 16] All chemistry courses for the minor must be taken in residence at Washington University, and a minimum grade of C- is required for each course. [13, 16] The required courses include General Chemistry I and II with labs, Organic Chemistry I and II with labs, Physics I and II with labs, and Calculus I and II. [16] Additionally, students must complete 9 units of chemistry elective courses at the 3000 level or higher, spanning at least two subdisciplines. [13, 16] Research courses like CHEM 4900 and CHEM 4950 cannot be used for the elective requirement. [13, 16]
Description: The Department of Chemistry at Washington University provides a strong foundation in the core areas of chemistry: organic, physical, inorganic, nuclear, and theoretical. [11] Special emphases in the department include emerging interdisciplinary fields such as organometallic, bioorganic, biophysical, macromolecular, polymer, environmental, and materials chemistry. [11] The minor requires 41 units, with 27 in chemistry and 14 in math and physics. All chemistry coursework must be taken in residence at Washington University, and a minimum grade of C- is required in each course to count toward the minor.
Accredidation: Washington University in St. Louis has been accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC) since 1913. [9] Additionally, the undergraduate and graduate level teacher certification programs, including for Chemistry, are accredited by the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE). [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Children's Studies
Requirements: To complete the Minor in Children's Studies, a student must take a total of 16 units. [2] A grade of C- or higher is required for a course to count toward the minor. [2] The required courses are CHST 3000 (Interdisciplinary Introduction to Children's Studies) and CHST 4000 (Senior Seminar in Children's Studies). [2] Additionally, students must complete 6 units of core courses from a specified list and 6 additional units from either the core list or a list of electives. [2] A maximum of 3 units from another institution may be applied toward the minor with approval. [8]
Description: As a children's studies minor, you will learn about children and childhood while drawing on the expertise of faculty from across WashU. Minors will develop a sophisticated interdisciplinary understanding of childhood and the issues surrounding the treatment and status of children throughout history. This minor is housed in the Department of English. [6]

ProgramName: Minor in Chinese Language and Culture
Minor in Classics
Requirements: To declare a minor in Classics, students must complete 15 units of coursework with a grade of C- or better. [4] This includes specific requirements for introductory and advanced language courses in Greek or Latin. [4] Up to 6 credits from study abroad or transfer credits may be applied. [4]
Description: As a classics minor, you will gain unique access to the lives and thoughts of ancient Greek and Roman people by studying the Greek and/or Latin languages and reading ancient texts in the original. [2] You will learn to interpret diverse ancient literary and historical writings as you gain a deep understanding of the world they came from. [2] Classics majors explore big questions about power, gender, art, religion, education, cultural change, and more, and develop valuable critical and writing skills. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Comparative Arts
Description:
The minor in Comparative Arts explores the dynamic interactions among literature, film, media, architecture, the visual arts, music, theatre, and the performing arts. It also

crosses national boundaries, artistic domains, and traditional notions of high and low culture. Courses in comparative arts examine works of literature alongside one or more other arts from multiple national traditions. By focusing on the interrelationship of the arts, the minor in comparative arts asks fundamental questions: What is creativity? How does something new emerge from encounters with existing traditions? How do we think theoretically about how the medium affects the message? Why are so many poets also accomplished painters or musicians, and why are a no small number of scientists also poets? Why do we consider some adaptations to be works of art in their own right but dismiss others as kitsch? Do styles belong to particular periods, forms, or cultures? What makes an artist or an art form "American" or, even more broadly, "African"? Conversely, can a cultural movement ever be truly global? The minor is ideal for students who want to explore human creativity without boundaries, bringing literature together with film, media, and the visual and performing arts with as much freedom and flexibility as possible. Humanities majors will gain new perspectives on their major fields through our interdisciplinary approach. Students in STEM fields will find the study of comparative arts particularly useful in thinking about questions of perception, sensation and sense-making, and in experimenting with different forms to express their ideas.

ProgramName: Minor in Comparative Literature
Requirements: Total Units Required: 15. All Comparative Literature and Thought (CLT) minors must take two core courses in Literature and Arts (including one required course) and two core courses in Thought for a total of 12 units in the Humanities Core. CLT minors must take a fifth CLT course. [7, 10] The fifth course may be taken from the same roster of core courses or from more advanced courses in CLT. [7, 10]
Description: Comparative Literature and Thought (CLT) immerses students in modern and contemporary literary and intellectual cultures and in the textual and philosophical traditions that animate those cultures. The curriculum attends to the emergence of a global textual and media culture as well as to the ways in which nations, subcultures, and individuals embrace and resist that global emergence. That foundational curriculum focuses on a set of themes and problems that have long preoccupied students<ctrl100> and scholars: the nature of textual culture, the philosophical and ethical engagements of literature and the arts, the pressure of politics on literature and thought, the reciprocal pressure of literature and thought on politics, the specific bearing of language on intellectual life, and the transformations and excitations produced whenever texts are translated to another language or to another medium. The introductory core of the CLT curriculum engages a minor in CLT with literature, intellectual history, social and political thought, and cultural theory. [9, 7] The minor requires five courses, four of which must be drawn from the core curriculum; the fifth course may be taken from the same roster of core courses or from more advances courses in CLT. [9]
MaxFails: Receiving unsatisfactory or failing grades in more than one course may result in Academic Notice. Failing grades in the majority of courses may result in Academic Time Away. [29]

ProgramName: Minor in Computer Science
Requirements: Before being admitted to the minor, there must be evidence that students have enough experience to be sure the Minor will be a good fit for them. Examples of such experience include: completion of the majority of a CSE course, like CSE 1301 or a CSE 1301 equivalent transfer course, or passing AP CS-A with a 4 or 5, or other comparable experience and passing the CSE Placement exam. For students admitted after August 1, 2024, the minor requires 15 units comprised of two core courses (CSE 1301 Introduction to Computer Science and CSE 2407 Data Structures and Algorithms) and three elective courses. For students admitted before August 2024, the minor requires two core courses (CSE 1301 and CSE 2407) and three elective courses. All courses used for the computer science minor must be taken for a grade, and the student must earn a C- or better.
Description: If a student's goal is a basic foundation in computer science for application to another field but they are not planning a career as a practicing computer scientist, the minor in computer science is a good choice. The minor consists of five CSE courses: four core courses and one elective. The core courses provide an introduction to computer science concepts and problem-solving techniques. The electives offer flexibility to integrate computer science studies with a major area. [8, 9]
MinGPA: A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses to count toward the minor. [10, 14] The university also requires a minimum 2.0 semester GPA for a student to remain in good academic standing. [11]
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarships can range up to the full cost of tuition. [13] For example, the Howard Nemerov Writing Scholars Program offers up to 10 scholarships of $3,000. [13]
ScholarshipType: The university offers school-specific, merit-based scholarships, such as the Alexander S. Langsdorf Fellowships for the McKelvey School of Engineering. [13] Other types include ROTC scholarships. [18]

ProgramName: Minor in Creative Writing
Requirements: The Writing Minor requires a total of 15 units. [7] Students are expected to take courses for letter grades and must receive a grade of C or better in each. [9] At least 9 of the units counted for the minor must be completed in regular courses that are home-based in the Writing program. [7] One of the five required courses must be either L13 311 Exposition or L13 312 Argumentation. A maximum of two courses (6 units) may be taken at the 200-level. [9] College Writing, which is required for most first-year students, does not count toward the minor. [9] With departmental approval, up to 6 units of specific journalism courses or an internship may be counted toward the minor. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Dance
Description: As a dance minor, you will study dance as an independent and collaborative art and as a global phenomenon expressed in a wide variety of contemporary and traditional forms. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Data Science in the Humanities
Requirements: To declare a minor in Data Science in the Humanities, students should consult with the administering program, Comparative Literature and Thought, as specific declaration procedures and prerequisites are not detailed on the main bulletin pages. General information indicates the minor is offered through the Humanities Digital Workshop. [6]

ProgramName: Minor in Design
Description: The Minor in Design allows students to mix and match courses in areas such as communication design, fashion design, and the illustrated book studio to suit interests and schedules. [3] This 15-unit course is open to all WashU students, including College of Art students majoring in studio art. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Drama
Requirements: Total Units Required: 15. Students must earn a grade of C- or better in all required and elective drama courses in order for them to apply toward minor requirements. Required foundation courses (9 units) include a course in acting or improvisation, Introduction to Theater Production, and Introduction to Theater & Performance Studies. Students must also complete at least 6 credit units at the DRAMA 3000 level or above. [2, 5]

ProgramName: Minor in Earth and Planetary Sciences
Requirements: To declare a minor, students must be currently enrolled at Washington University. The requirements for the minors in the Department of Earth, Environmental, and Planetary Sciences are based on course and credit completion. For the Planetary Science Minor, a total of 15-17 units are required, and for the Earth Science Minor, 15-17 units are required. [2, 3] A minimum grade of C- is required for coursework to count toward the minors. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Minor in East Asian Studies
Requirements: Total Units Required: 18 units. Students must earn a grade of C- or above in all courses for the minor, and pass/fail grades are not permitted. The requirements include two semesters of Chinese, Japanese, or Korean language. At least 9 units must be at the 300-level or above. Students must also complete one civilization course (Chinese, Japanese, or Korean Civilization), one course on the premodern era (from an approved list), and one course on the modern era (from an approved list). An additional upper-level elective course from the East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) department is also required. [6]
Description: Under the unified EALC minor, students may choose to study across disciplinary and geographic boundaries, or they may pursue a more focused approach to their studies. [7] Our language programs continue to offer their full sequence of courses in Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. [7] Students undertake language study in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean, and take one core Civilization course and a 300-level EALC Seminar, along with two literature courses of their choosing. [7] The EALC minor allow students the flexibility to study across regions. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Economics
Requirements: Total Units Required: 22-24. All courses for the minor, including mathematics, must be taken with the letter grade option and a grade of at least C- must be earned in each. [7] The minor has two tracks: General Economics or Applied Microeconomics. Required courses for the General Economics track include ECON 1501, ECON 1502, ECON 4001, ECON 4002, and one elective. The Applied Microeconomics track requires ECON 1501, ECON 1502, ECON 4001, one elective with ECON 4001 as a prerequisite, and another elective. Both tracks also have mathematics requirements, including MATH 1520 and ECON 4830 (or MATH 2130). [9]
Description: As a general economics minor, you will undertake a broad study of the production, consumption, and transfer of wealth. You will study both micro- and macro- economics to attain a broad, holistic perspective of the field of study.

ProgramName: Minor in Education
Requirements: Total Units Required: 18. All courses for the Educational Studies minor must be taken for a letter grade, and per Arts & Sciences requirements, students must earn at least a C– for coursework to count toward the minor. [8, 13]
Description: The Department of Education at Washington University in St. Louis offers an undergraduate minor in Educational Studies for individuals interested in the study of educational processes and institutions. Students in this program utilize perspectives and methods from various disciplines to examine questions about educational institutions, educational processes, and the social and cultural factors that influence them. The program serves as an entry point into the multidimensional field of education, analysis, the individual, and the collective. As an educational studies minor, students will explore the historical, social, cultural, psychological, and public policy aspects of education.

ProgramName: Minor in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: The official university bulletin does not specify any application documents like a resume, statement of purpose, or writing sample for declaring a Minor in Electrical Engineering. The process is typically an internal declaration for currently enrolled students.
Fees: $68,240 per year for the 2025-26 academic year.
Description: This minor consists of fundamental courses in core electrical engineering areas of devices and circuits, applied physics, and signals and systems. Elective choices allow further depth in advanced devices, optics, signal processing, and control systems or greater breadth within electrical engineering. [3]
ScholarshipAmount: The Langsdorf Fellows program offers 100% tuition for four years. [2] Other academic scholarships for the McKelvey School of Engineering range up to the full cost of tuition. [38] An annual gift of $10,000 or more can fund a named scholarship. [22]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Energy Engineering
Requirements: A minor in energy engineering requires the completion of at least 18 units selected from specific course lists. It is open to any undergraduate student pursuing an engineering major, a major in the sciences (biology, chemistry, physics) in Arts & Sciences, or the environmental studies major. [9]
Description: The goal of this minor is to provide students with a course work experience that will enhance their background, knowledge and skills in the topical area of energy engineering. The minor encompasses courses in several fields of science and engineering, including the Department of Energy, Environmental & Chemical Engineering; the Department of Electrical & Systems Engineering; and the Department of Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science. [2, 11] A minor in energy engineering requires the completion of at least 18 units selected from the lists of courses. It is open to any undergraduate student pursuing an engineering major, a major in the sciences (biology, chemistry, physics) in Arts & Sciences, or the environmental studies major. [2, 11]

ProgramName: Minor in English
Requirements: Washington University in St. Louis accepts the Common Application or the Coalition Application. Applicants must also submit an application fee or fee waiver, a high school transcript, a counselor recommendation, and teacher recommendations. The personal essay submitted with the application serves as the statement of purpose. While not explicitly required for all applicants, a separate resume of activities may be submitted.
Description: As an English minor, you will study materials of literary history, stretching from Chaucer to Shakespeare, Austen and Blake, to Woolf and Yeats, Emily Dickinson and Mark Twain, and the most recent literature by writers such as David Foster Wallace, Toni Morrison, J. M. Coetzee, and Seamus Heaney. [10]

ProgramName: Minor in Entrepreneurship
Requirements: To declare the minor, students must be enrolled in an undergraduate division of Washington University other than the Olin Business School. A minimum of a 2.0 average GPA in all business minor coursework is required to earn the minor. [13] Students must declare their minor online through Workday. [14]
Description: The Entrepreneurship Minor is designed for students who wish to participate in the commercial entrepreneurship process as a collaborator rather than a founder. [8] The learning goal is to introduce non-Olin students to the language of business and allow them to contribute on entrepreneurial teams. [8] The students have the opportunity to build on ideas, skills, inventions, and perspectives from their primary discipline to enhance the venture. [8]

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Engineering Science
Requirements: The Minor in Environmental Engineering Science requires the completion of 21 units of courses. [5, 6] This program prepares students for entry-level positions as environmental engineers, scientists, or analysts and provides a foundation for graduate study. [5, 6, 7]
Description: The EECE department sponsors an undergraduate minor in environmental engineering science. This 21-unit program prepares the student to seek an entry-level position as an environmental engineer, scientist or analyst. The minor also provides a solid foundation for undertaking graduate study in environmental engineering. [3, 5, 10]

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Studies
Requirements: To declare the minor in Environmental Analysis, students should contact the Environmental Studies office. More information can be found on the program's website.
Description: The Environmental Studies Minor is a flexible, 18-credit program of study that offers exposure to interdisciplinary environmental challenges and problem solving. It is highly accessible because it includes a choice of introductory level courses and is flexible because there is a wide degree of choice in elective categories, including courses in analysis and communication. As for all ArtSci minors, students must have at least 9 units of 300+ coursework unique to this minor.

ProgramName: Minor in Film and Media Studies
Requirements: To declare the Minor in Film and Media Studies, a student must be enrolled at Washington University in St. Louis. The minor requires a total of 15 units. A minimum grade of C- or higher is required for all courses to count toward the minor. [8, 9] Internships and independent study do not count toward the minor. [8, 9]
Description: As a minor in film and media studies, you will critically engage with moving images, whether it be cinematic or televisual. You will engage in an in-depth study of film theory, criticism, and history. Students with an interest in directing or screenwriting may choose to take classes to explore the production side of the medium. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Finance
Requirements: To declare a Minor in Finance, students must meet with the designated minor advisor, Shawn Brodie, before making a request in the Workday system. [2] The minor must be declared by the end of the student's junior year. [2] Non-BSBA students are required to complete the minor courses with a 2.0 GPA or better to have the minor conferred. [2]
Description: Non-BSBA degree students are eligible to pursue a minor in one of the specific fields of business listed below. [13] A minimum of a 2.0 average GPA in all business minor coursework is required. [13] Non-BSBA minors in Accounting, Entrepreneurship, Finance, Health Care Management, Managerial Economics, Marketing, Organization and Strategic Management, or Supply Chain, Operations, and Technology may not pursue a second major from Olin in the following disciplines: Accounting, Entrepreneurship, Finance, Health Care Management, Managerial Economics, Marketing, Organization and Strategic Management, or Supply Chain, Operations, and Technology. [13] Satisfy all prerequisites. [13] Courses taken in the School of Continuing & Professional Studies or at another university do not satisfy the requirements for any of the five required minor courses. [13] Take all 15 units of required minor courses for grades (i.e., no Pass/No Pass). [13] Minor prerequisites may be taken as Pass/No Pass. [13]

ProgramName: Minor in French
Requirements: Total Units Required: 18. Students must complete courses taken for the minor with a grade of B– or higher and are expected to maintain a B average or better in all French courses. Courses taken Pass/No Pass do not count toward the minor. [8]
Description: As a French minor, you will study great texts with an eye to gender roles, traditions, communities, individual freedom, social obligations, and many other topics of critical importance today You will also study the French language. This minor is housed in the Department of Romance Languages and Literatures. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Germanic Languages and Literatures
Requirements: Total Units Required: 16. [3] Students must earn a grade of C- or higher. [3] Students who intend to minor in German must complete 16 units of coursework (GERMAN 2020 and above) with a grade of C- or higher. [3] With the exception of GERMAN 3400 and its 1-unit discussion section (GERMAN 3401), only courses taught in German will count toward the minor. [3] At least 3 of the 16 required units must be at the 4000 level. [3] At least half of the courses at the 3000 level and above must have been acquired either in residence at Washington University or in overseas programs affiliated with Washington University. [3, 6]
Description: As a Germanic languages and literatures minor, you will study the German language intensively and explore German literature and culture from the Middle Ages to the present. [3] Additionally, you will have the opportunity to study German film, history, philosophy, and gender studies. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Global Film and Media Studies
Requirements: Total Units Required: 15. A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses to count toward the minor; pass/no pass grades do not count toward the minor. [3] Required courses are FILM 2200 Introduction to Film Studies and FILM 3400 History of World Cinema. [3] Students must also complete elective courses, including two courses at the 3000 or 4000 level dealing with national or regional cinemas and one course at the 3000 level or higher that analyzes film or moving image media from different countries or parts of the world. [3]
Description: Film and Media Studies offers a minor in Global Film and Media Studies that encourages students interested in visual culture to learn about film and media as global phenomena beyond the confines of the U.S. A number of classes available in this minor will emphasize how specific aspects of a country's cultural heritage and aesthetic traditions are expressed through commercial, narrative cinema. [2] The aim of this minor is to foster understanding of the global development of moving image visual forms that may be in adaption of, or in self-conscious opposition to, U.S. feature film or electronic media practice. Other modes of moving image production can also be studied, such as documentary film/media, avant-garde film, television and video games. [2] In addition to courses on specific national or regional cinemas or electronic media forms, other courses will offer students the opportunity to compare and contrast moving image texts from different cultural and historical contexts. [2, 3] Minoring in this area can help students see film and media within the changing cultural, social, and political terrain, moving from the local to the global. [2] They will also gain understanding of the intersection of production and reception, textual conventions (or transgressions) and audience expectations. [2] They will learn how to situate the longstanding commercial dominance of U.S.-based media forms within an understanding of adaptive, contrarian, and transformational responses to those forms. [2] Students will also learn how moving image texts within and across national boundaries treat issues like stereotyping, cultural hybridity, orientalism, economic neocolonialism, neo-liberalism, and cultural globalization. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Health Care Management
Requirements: Prerequisites: Calculus II: MATH 1520 Calculus II; Microeconomics: MEC 2900 Microeconomics, ECON 1501 Introduction to Microeconomics, or ECON 4001 Intermediate Microeconomic Theory; Statistics I: DAT 1200 Managerial Statistics I, ESE 3260 Probability and Statistics for Engineering, POLSCI 2400 Data Science for Politics, POLSCI 3630 Quantitative Political Methodology, SDS 2020 Elementary Probability and Statistics, or SDS 3020 Elementary to Intermediate Statistics and Data Analysis (AP credit for SDS 2020 [2200] will fulfill this prerequisite). [7, 8]
Description: The program is open to both business and non-business students who can choose to major or minor in healthcare management. [14] The primary difference between the two options is that students who major in the subject will conduct individual research in healthcare management issues under the guidance of a faculty member. [14] The research project is optional for those who chose to minor. [14] The creation of the degree option came about from the demand of the students and the marketplace. [14] In addition to case studies, clinicians and business people come into class to talk about the issues they face. [14] On top of that core class, students add courses in healthcare economics and policy, healthcare management and at least one other course in biomedical engineering, biology or anthropology. [14]

ProgramName: Minor in Hebrew
Requirements: Six courses are required for the Minor in Hebrew. Students must receive a grade of C- or above for it to count towards the minor. Students who place out of third or fourth-year Hebrew by language placement exam must still take a total of six courses. Four Hebrew language courses above the intermediate level (Hebrew 4). Two Hebrew literature or culture courses taught in English. [1]
Description: The Department of Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Studies (JIMES) is an interdisciplinary program that explores the historical experience, literary, religious, and cultural expression, and political and material life of Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern civilizations. [2] The program is unique in the United States as it integrates Islamic and Jewish studies. [2] There are two tracks offered for the major: the Comparative Jewish and Islamic Studies track and the Modern Middle Eastern Studies track. [2] Students who minor in Hebrew can expect to gain proficiency in the language, study the area's literary and cultural landmarks, and gain familiarity with the historical context. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in History
Requirements: Total Units Required: 18. Students must complete 6 units of introductory courses and 12 units of upper-level courses. A grade of C- or higher is required, and Pass/No Pass grades are not accepted. All 18 units must be separate courses that are not double-counted toward a major or another minor. [13]
Description: As a history minor, you will study a wide variety of regions and areas, ranging from the ancient world to the present, and across Africa, Asia, the Mideast, Europe and the Americas. You will study the past in a way that informs, challenges, and inspires. [8] The Department of History at Washington University in St. Louis is committed to studying the past in a way that informs, challenges, and inspires. [10] Situated at the core of the university, the department is committed to a comprehensive and diverse curriculum that not only imparts important knowledge, but cultivates skills that are crucial for life and work in today's twenty-first century world. [10] We believe that a critical understanding of the past is foundational not only to an education, but to responsible global citizenship. [10] Undergraduates can major or minor in history. [10]

ProgramName: Minor in Human-Computer Interaction
Requirements: The human-computer interaction (HCI) minor is designed to give any undergraduate student at Washington University a multidisciplinary understanding of the principles and applications of HCI. [5] Students must complete two pillar courses, one integration course, and three approved electives. [8] Each of the pillar and integration courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. [5, 8] Only one course that is also counting for another major or minor can be counted toward the HCI minor. [17]
Department: College of Art and the McKelvey School of Engineering
Description: The Human-Computer Interaction minor is designed to give any undergraduate student at Washington University in St. Louis a multidisciplinary understanding of the principles and applications of human-computer interaction. [2] The HCI minor is intended for students who are interested in the design of user-centered interactive technologies and those desiring jobs that include user interface creation, Product Design, UX/UI Design, App Development, Virtual and Augmented Realities, etc. [2, 3] The Minor in Human-Computer Interaction (18 units) is a collaboration between the College of Art and the McKelvey School of Engineering, with a mix of required and optional courses in each school. [2, 7] Students are able to gain a multidisciplinary understanding of the principles and applications of human-computer interaction (HCI), and they are introduced to the techniques and processes necessary to create effective user interfaces: requirements gathering, ideation, prototyping, visual design and evaluation. [3, 5] This minor may appeal to students in the College of Art—particularly designers and/or computationally intrigued artists—who are interested in gaining a more in-depth knowledge of the 'back-end' development skills. [2] It will also be of interest to Engineering students looking for more experience with aesthetics and 'front-end' design skills. [2] In addition to these primary audiences, this minor allows students from other departments on campus to support their studies with a clear track in a hybrid pursuit in design and programming. [3, 4]

ProgramName: Minor in Interdisciplinary Environmental Analysis
Requirements: Declaring a minor is done online via WebSTAC by currently enrolled students and requires department approval. [3, 4] The program requires 18 total units for completion. [8]
Description: This minor was developed to prepare students to tackle real-world environmental challenges by providing more robust opportunities for interdisciplinary knowledge and skill development. The minor is structured to provide students with opportunities to strengthen their critical analysis and problem-solving skills through participation in team-based, experiential, often community-engaged learning around “wicked” real-world problems. Most courses do not have pre-requisites*. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Italian
Requirements: The Italian minor requires the completion of 18 units, 12 of which must be taken in residence. [11] Students must complete courses taken for the minor with a grade of B- or higher and are expected to maintain a B average or better in all Italian courses. [8, 11] Courses taken Pass/No Pass do not count toward the Italian minor. [8, 11]
Fees: $64,500 per year for the 2024-2025 academic year (full-time undergraduate). This is not specific to the minor program.
Description: As an Italian minor, you will study the great Italian texts and will do so with an eye to gender roles, traditions, communities, individual freedom, social obligations and many other topics of critical importance today. You will also study the Italian language. This minor is housed in Romance Languages and Literatures. [15]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, and scholarships based on specific interests or talents. [8]

ProgramName: Minor in Japanese Language and Culture
Requirements: Two semesters of one of the chosen languages: Chinese, Japanese, or Korean; At least 9 units must be from 3000-level courses or above. Students are required to complete one of the following Civilization courses (3 units): Chinese Civilization, Japanese Civilization, or Korean Civilization. Students must earn at least a B- or better in language courses to continue to the next level. [8]
Description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures at Washington University offers a unified undergraduate minor in East Asian Languages and Cultures, allowing students to explore the linguistic and cultural traditions of China, Japan, and Korea. [11] Students in the minor can pursue a focused study of the Japanese language and can select from a variety of non-language courses to enhance their understanding of the nation. [11] The program aims to provide an impressive range of courses in modern Japanese up to the advanced level, in addition to classical language study. [11] Students are also encouraged to broaden their cultural knowledge by taking relevant courses in other departments such as anthropology, art history, film and media studies, history, performing arts, and religious studies. [11]

ProgramName: Minor in Jazz Studies
Requirements: The Minor in Jazz Studies requires a total of 18 units. [8] A grade of C- or better is required for all courses to count toward the minor. [8] The required courses include MUSIC 1130 History of Jazz, MUSIC 1260 Jazz Theory I, MUSIC 1261 Jazz Theory II, MUSIC 3070 Jazz in American Culture, and MUSIC 3190 Improv I. [8, 10] An additional 3 units must be chosen from a list of specified upper-level courses. [8] Up to 6 credits from study abroad or transfer may be allowed with department approval. [8] Other upper-level credits in music or related studies, such as African and African-American Studies, may be approved by the department chair. [8, 10]
Description: This course will address the role of jazz within the context of twentieth-century African American and American cultural history, with particular emphasis on the ways in which jazz has shaped, and has been shaped by, ideas about race, gender, economics, and politics. [4] We will make use of recordings and primary sources from the 1910s to the present in order to address the relationship between jazz performances and critical and historical thinking about jazz. [4] This course is not a survey, and students should already be familiar with basic jazz history. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Studies
Requirements: The minor in Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern studies requires a minimum of 18 total units, with a minimum of 12 units at the 3000 level or above. [2, 4] Students must choose one of two concentrations: Comparative Jewish and Islamic Studies or Middle Eastern Studies. [2, 4] A grade of B- or higher is required for each language course to advance, and no course for the minor can be taken Pass/No Pass. [2, 4]
Concentration: Students who wish to minor in Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern studies will select one of two tracks: The Comparative Jewish and Islamic Studies Track or The Middle Eastern Studies Track. [2]
Description: Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Studies is an interdisciplinary program whose purpose is to explore the historical experience; literary, religious and cultural expression; and political and material life of the Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern civilizations. [2] Our program is unique in the United States because it integrates Islamic studies and Jewish studies. [2] There are two tracks offered in the major and minor, encouraging students to tailor their experience more closely to their interests: the Comparative Jewish and Islamic Studies track and the Modern Middle Eastern Studies track. [2] Whether students favor the study of language, literature, religion, history or politics, they will find in our courses a way to deepen their appreciation of these complex and diverse societies and cultures. [2] Students also will be encouraged to explore the interaction of Jews and Muslims with neighboring societies and cultures in the Middle East, Europe, North Africa, and other parts of the world. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Korean Language and Culture
Requirements: To declare the minor, students must complete two semesters of Korean, take the course KOREA 2230 Korean Civilization, and complete at least 9 units from courses at the 3000-level or above. A grade of B- or better is required in language courses to advance to the next level. [9]
Description: Washington University in St. Louis does not offer a standalone 'Minor in Korean Language and Culture.' Instead, students can pursue an 'East Asian Languages and Cultures Minor' and choose to focus on Korean. [8, 13] This unified minor allows for the study of Chinese, Japanese, or Korean languages and cultures. [8] The program is designed to provide students with a high level of proficiency in the Korean language and the ability to read and understand various cultural texts within their historical context. [13, 14] The curriculum for the minor requires 18 units, which includes two semesters of language study, a civilization course (such as KOREA 2230 Korean Civilization), a course on the premodern era, a course on the modern era, and an upper-level elective. [9, 10] Students must achieve a grade of B- or better in language courses to advance to the next level. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Landscape Architecture
Requirements: The Minor in Landscape Architecture is open to all students at Washington University in St. Louis, regardless of major. [7, 8, 9] At least 12 of the 15 credit units must be applied exclusively to the minor and cannot be counted toward another major or minor. [7, 8] Students interested in the minor should contact the minor advisor. [7, 8]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts
Description: The Minor in Landscape Architecture introduces foundational aspects of practice and scholarship central to shaping landscapes and the broader built environment. The discipline of landscape architecture thrives in diversity, embracing the nuances and complexities of material, biological, and climatological systems. This minor exposes students to a range of design scales, from the urban environment to the garden scale, with a focus on public space, infrastructure, and new and old media. [5, 6] Courses introduce how the design of landscape affects the social, cultural, and ecological dimensions of the world. History and theory complement science and the arts to equip students with the tools, knowledge, and innovative skills to enrich any major. [5, 6] The Minor in Landscape Architecture is open to all students at Washington University in St. Louis, regardless of major. [5, 6]

ProgramName: Minor in Latin American Studies
Requirements: The minor in LAS requires students to complete 18 units. At least 15 units must be at the 3000 level or higher, and at least 3 units must be at the 4000 level. [9] All units must be exclusive to the minor and may not be double counted, unless the College of Arts & Sciences regulations state otherwise. [9] To count for LAS, courses must have an LATAM number or receive authorization from the LAS Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS), who determines which requirements can be fulfilled by each available course. [9]
Description: As a Latin American studies minor, you will pursue an in-depth study of Latin America across diverse disciplines, theoretical approaches and historical periods. [7] You will consider the region both in its specificity and in its connections to the world, through the study of Latin America's processes of internationalization and its changing position in global scenarios. [7] The minor in Latin American Studies (LAS) allows undergraduate students pursuing other major programs to complement their existing curriculum with a study of Latin America across diverse disciplines and how the region engages with the Western world — to which it belongs — at large. [4] The minor in LAS is conceived as an option for students across a variety of disciplines in the social sciences, the humanities, the sciences, the pre-med program, and business and engineering to add knowledge about Latin America to their professional portfolio. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Legal Studies
Requirements: The minor in legal studies requires six courses (18 graded units), at least three of which (9 units) must be upper-division (3000- or 4000-level) courses. Two of the six courses may be drawn from the student's major, but they cannot be double-counted. The six courses must also be distributed across three of four thematic subject areas. [3]
Description: An an-interdisciplinary program, the minor in Legal Studies is designed to guide students towards courses that will deepen and expand their understanding of the law as practiced, especially its influence on social and economic institutions, while also providing students with the critical skills needed to excel in law school. Recognizing the critical role that law plays in human society, it examines the ways people in different cultures and historical periods have used the law and understood its purposes. As such, the minor encourages students to draw not only upon the humanistic and social scientific offerings of the College of Arts & Sciences, but also to take advantage of courses in the schools of Business, Engineering, and Social Work.

ProgramName: Minor in Linguistics
Requirements: Students must complete a total of 15 units to complete the minor. At least 9 of these must be at the 3000 level or above. Students must receive a grade of C- or higher in a course to count it toward the minor. Pass/No Pass grades do not count toward the minor. The maximum number of credits from outside Arts & Sciences that students may apply to the minor is 3; this includes credits from other U.S. institutions and from approved Study Abroad programs. [8]
Description: The Linguistics Minor at Washington University in St. Louis is designed for students who are interested in the nature of language and want a basic familiarity with the field. It is particularly suitable for those majoring in foreign languages or other language-related fields such as anthropology, cognitive science, computer science, psychology, and speech and hearing science. The program requires a total of 18 semester hours. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Marketing
Requirements: Prerequisites for the Minor in Marketing (Non-BSBA) include: Calculus I, Microeconomics, and Statistics I. [7, 9]

ProgramName: Minor in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: The minor in MSE builds upon the fundamental insights into material structure and properties gained through required introductory courses in chemistry and materials science. Students then select at least two courses from specialization "pick lists" to gain depth in a particular application area. A free elective provides the opportunity to gain additional depth in the fundamentals or exposure to another application area. Students will be approved for the minor after discussing appropriate course selection with the advisor for the minor. [1]
Department: McKelvey School of Engineering, Department of Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science
Description: Materials Science & Engineering (MSE) is an interdisciplinary-field that applies the fundamental knowledge of the physical sciences to create engineering innovations. In general, the term engineering refers to actively designing a system for a given application; MSE enables the design of systems from the atoms up. MSE focuses on the interrelationship between a material's structure (from the subatomic level to the macro scale) and the properties or behaviors that the material exhibits. Materials synthesis and processing techniques enable engineers to control and change the material structure in order to obtain the desired properties. Understanding the structure–properties–processing relationship requires a fundamental knowledge of the underlying chemistry and physics, and it is key to obtaining materials with the desired performance for engineering applications in a wide variety of fields, from computing to medicine to energy. The minor in MSE builds upon the fundamental insights into material structure and properties gained through required introductory courses in chemistry and materials science. Students then select at least two courses from specialization "pick lists" to gain depth in a particular application area. A free elective provides the opportunity to gain additional depth in the fundamentals or exposure to another application area. [2]
CostPerCredit: $1,930 per credit for part-time students (1-11 undergraduate credits). [19]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, and Field-Specific scholarships are common types available to undergraduate students. [2, 10, 13, 15]

ProgramName: Minor in Mathematics
Requirements: Total Units Required: 27. All required courses (both lower- and upper-level) must be taken for a letter grade and completed with a grade of C– or better. [8]
ScholarshipAmount: Up to the full cost of tuition

ProgramName: Minor in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: Students pursuing the minor in mechanical engineering must complete a total of 15 units of coursework. [2] Courses selected for the minor program may count toward program requirements of the student's major. [2] The subjects selected for a minor in mechanical engineering are expected to constitute a coherent program within the field of mechanical engineering. [2] Courses taken under the Pass/No Pass grading option cannot be used for a minor program. [2] Required courses include MEMS 2510 or BME 2400, MEMS 2520 or PHYSICS 5011, and MEMS 3530, for a total of 9 units. [2] Two electives must be chosen from a list that includes MEMS 3400, MEMS 3110 or BME 3200, MEMS 3410, MEMS 2610, and MEMS 4310. [2]
Description: The minor in mechanical engineering complements a major in a field related to mechanical engineering, such as biomedical engineering, electrical engineering, physics, chemistry or architecture. The minor is intended to provide students with a credential that could enhance their opportunities for employment or graduate study. [2] Completion of the minor demonstrates that the student has pursued a structured program approved by the faculty of the Department of Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science. [2] Students pursuing the minor in mechanical engineering must complete a total of 15 units of coursework as described below. Courses selected for the minor program may count toward program requirements of the student's major. The subjects selected for a minor in mechanical engineering are expected to constitute a coherent program within the field of mechanical engineering. Courses taken under the Pass/No Pass grading option cannot be used for a minor program. [2]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available, including the Danforth Scholars Program, the Ervin Scholars Program, and the Rodriguez Scholars Program.

ProgramName: Minor in Mechatronics
Requirements: To be admitted to Washington University, where a student can then pursue a Minor in Mechatronics, the application file must contain the Common Application or Coalition Application, a nonrefundable $75 fee (which is waived for students applying for financial aid), a teacher recommendation, a school report, and official transcripts. [5] WashU has a test-optional policy for applicants for the fall semester of 2026, meaning students can choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Medical Humanities
Requirements: Important components of a student's application also include the following: The student's academic performance (transcript), including course selection, grades, and class rank, if provided by the secondary school; Counselor and teacher recommendations; Essays; Extracurricular and community involvement, including positive impacts on home and community (students who work for pay and/or have time-consuming family responsibilities should include this in their activity list); Standardized testing, if provided. [6]
Description: The study of medical humanities approaches health, disease and medical care as culturally embedded human experiences that vary across time and place. In addition to exploring health, disease and medical care as core human experiences, the program of study is designed to provide a solid grounding in the textual-historical approach essential to all humanities scholarship. Medical humanitiesGTG (Global Thematic Group) is a vibrant, interdisciplinary group of faculty, graduate students, and undergraduates that is organized by the Center for the Humanities in Arts & Sciences and that has strong ties to the School of Medicine. The group combines disciplinary diversity with thematic unity to engage students with a set of tightly related “big” topics and issues. These include the contested meanings of health and disease; the ethical dimensions of medicine; illness narratives; debates over health and development; the role of medicine in war, empire and nation building; the relationship between religion and medicine; exchange and friction between biomedicine and other healing traditions; and the burden of disease as it relates to gender, race and class.

ProgramName: Minor in Medieval and Renaissance Studies
