Requirements: Total Units Required: 18. Students must maintain a grade of C- or better, and Pass/No Pass grades do not count for the minor. [2] Those pursuing the minor must complete two years of college-level study in a language such as Spanish, French, Italian, Latin, German, Arabic, or Greek. [2] Students are required to take six additional courses. Three of these must be from a specific list of foundational courses, and the other three must be medieval or renaissance studies courses from at least two different departments or programs. [2] At least one course must focus significantly on non-Western material. [2]
Description: The minor in Medieval and Renaissance Studies offers students the opportunity to gain a broad and global understanding of the medieval and Renaissance world through inquiry in multiple disciplines, including literature, history, philosophy, religious studies, art history, and music. [11] As a minor in medieval and renaissance studies, you will gain a broad understanding of the early modern world, through a study of literature, history, philosophy, art history, and music. [12] Some topics examined include the rise of urban life, the flowering of vernacular languages and new literary genres, the growing emphasis on education and the transformation of religious doctrines and institutions. [12] Students may choose from multiple offerings on medieval and Renaissance topics that range in geographical reach to include the West, the Near East, the Far East, and the Global South. [13] Interested students may pursue the Medieval and Renaissance Studies Minor under the auspices of Comparative Literature and Thought. [11]

ProgramName: Minor in Music
Requirements: To declare a minor, current students should first indicate their intention in the Workday system. Following that, they need to email Jessica Flannigan (flanniganj@wustl.edu) for approval. [10] The program requires the completion of 18 total units, and courses must be passed with a grade of C- or better to count toward the minor. [7]
Description: The Music - General Studies Minor is a varied course of study where music is approached as a liberal and fine art, rather than as an isolated, separate subject. Students in this program explore critical issues of tradition, individual composers, compositional craft, aesthetic interpretation, and music's social and cultural significance through a wide range of courses. The curriculum includes required courses in music theory and music history, as well as elective courses, a portion of which must be at the upper level.

ProgramName: Minor in Nanoscale Science & Engineering
Requirements: The minor is open to undergraduate students pursuing an engineering degree or a related Arts & Sciences major (e.g., chemistry, physics, biology, environmental studies, pre-med). [1] The program requires the completion of 18 units of coursework, which includes courses selected from Fundamentals, Synthesis and Applications, and Characterization, Structure and Modeling categories, a cleanroom lab class, and a mandatory faculty-supervised independent study project over at least two semesters. [1]
Description: Nanotechnology deals with materials, structures and devices with dimensions that are in the 1- to 100-nm length scale. [2] These entities have properties (physical, chemical and biological) that are very different from their bulk counterparts, and they can be tuned to obtain novel and desired functionalities. [2] The goal of this minor is to enhance the student's background, knowledge and skills in the topical area of nanotechnology. [2] The minor includes courses in several fields of science and engineering; it encompasses all of the departments in the McKelvey School of Engineering as well as several departments in Arts & Sciences. [2] It is open to undergraduate students pursuing an engineering degree or a related Arts & Sciences major (e.g., chemistry, physics, biology, environmental studies, pre-med). [2] The minor in nanoscale science and engineering involves the following components. [2] Starting with courses covering the fundamentals, students gain knowledge in synthesis and applications as well as characterization, structure and modeling. [2] Two additional requirements are a cleanroom lab class (MEMS 5611 or MEMS 5801) and the completion of a faculty-supervised independent study project over the course of at least two semesters. [1] The mix of courses should provide the student with a significant background in nanotechnology, and it should promote independent thinking through the student's work on a research or educational project. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Operations and Supply Chain Management
Accredidation: The Olin Business School at Washington University in St. Louis has earned triple accreditation from the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), the EFMD Quality Improvement System (EQUIS), and the Association of MBAs (AMBA). [2, 11, 12]

ProgramName: Minor in Philosophy
Requirements: To declare a minor in Philosophy, students must use the online Workday system. There are no application documents required. The requirements to complete the minor are course-based.
ScholarshipAmount: Multiple full-tuition and partial-tuition scholarships are available through the Signature Scholar Programs. [8, 16, 19]

ProgramName: Minor in Philosophy of Science
Requirements: Total Units Required: 18 units. 12 units must be taken at the 3000 level or higher; 3 units must be taken at the 4000 level. A grade of C- or better is required, and Pass/No Pass grades do not count toward the minor requirements. [7]
Description: A philosophy of science minor works well in conjunction with a major in the natural sciences. As a minor, you will pursue philosophical issues relating to the natural and physical sciences. This minor is housed in the Department of Philosophy. [8]

ProgramName: Minor in Philosophy-Neuroscience-Psychology
Requirements: Total Units Required: 15 units; 9 of the 15 units must be at the 3000 level or above. [2] Grade Requirement: C- or above; Pass/No Pass grades do not count toward the minor requirements. [2] There are also introductory, philosophy, neuroscience, and psychology course requirements. [2]
Description: As a philosophy-neuroscience-psychology (PNP) minor, you are provided with an opportunity to examine the mind from multiple perspectives. PNP is a unique interdisciplinary program dedicated to the conviction that answers to the deep questions about minds and their nature depend on the adoption of a variety of perspectives. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Physics
Requirements: A minor in physics consists of the first four courses of the core sequence plus one additional physics course. [2] Students must complete all coursework for the Physics minor with a grade of at least a C-. [9] The total units required are 17-19. [9]
Description: As a physics minor, you will explore the vast range of nature, from sub-nuclear particles to the most distant galaxies. You will consider with the most fundamental aspects of our universe: the properties of atoms, nuclei, and elementary particles; the nature of fundamental forces of interaction between these particles; and the collective behavior of atoms in solids, liquids, and gasses. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Political Science
Requirements: Students must complete a minimum of 15 graded units of course work with a C or better, including at least 9 advanced units. [7, 9] No more than 3 units may be counted from among the following: POLSCI 2998 Teaching Practicum in Political Science, POLSCI 4912 Directed Readings, POLSCI 4913 Directed Research, summer school, courses in the School of Continuing & Professional Studies, or credits from another institution (including study abroad). [7]
Fees: $64,500 per year for full-time undergraduate students (2024-2025)
Description: As a political science minor, you will increase your understanding of politics, political institutions, and political processes. [12] You will examine political behavior and use different methodologies to try to understand such issues as: who gets what resources and why, how do political actors make decisions, and how does politics affect political, economic, and social outcomes?. [12]
Accredidation: Washington University in St. Louis has been accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC) since 1913. [15]

ProgramName: Minor in Psychological & Brain Sciences
Requirements: To declare the Minor in Psychological & Brain Sciences, a student must get the declaration form from the Undergraduate Advising website, fill it out with the courses taken and to be taken, and submit it. The minor requires the completion of 18 credit hours of coursework in psychology. [2]
Description: As a psychological and brain sciences minor, you will study a large and diverse field that is empirical, theoretical, and practical. You'll consider topics as diverse as the biological bases of behavior; cognitive neuroscience; learning, memory, cognition, motivation, emotion, sensation, and perception; the study of social interactions, persuasion, and attitudes; aging and development; personality; clinical, abnormal, and health psychology; and leisure and work experiences. [3] For those students who have a broad or general interest in Psychological & Brain Sciences (P&BS), we recommend taking several courses from the five core areas of psychology: Social/Personality; Mental Health/Affective; Biological/Neurological Bases of Behavior; Behavior and Cognition; and Lifespan Development. For those students who want to focus in a more specific area, courses can reflect the area of interest.

ProgramName: Minor in Public Health
Department: A collaboration between Arts & Sciences, the Brown School, and the planned School for Public Health. [27]
Description: The Public Health & Society minor at Washington University in St. Louis provides an interdisciplinary approach to understanding health. [5] The program addresses how health intersects with history, economics, politics, culture, biology, environment, and ecology. [5] Students in the minor will explore topics such as the major threats to human health, how societies respond to these threats, the interplay of various factors on health, and the reasons behind health disparities. [5] The curriculum, which requires 18 credit units for completion, is designed to develop critical reading, effective communication, and a broad understanding of public health in its social contexts. [5, 3] Core requirements include courses like Foundations in Public Health, Introduction to Public and Global Health, and Public Health Theories, Models, and Frameworks. [3] Students must also complete 9 credits of elective courses, with at least one course from the "Social, Cultural, and Historical Analysis" category. [3] All courses for the minor must be letter-graded and completed with a grade of C or higher. [3]
CostPerCredit: $2,843 per credit unit for units beyond 21 per semester. [11]
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarships can range up to the full cost of tuition, with specific programs offering amounts such as $3,000. [10, 14]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available. [5, 14]

ProgramName: Minor in Religion and Politics
Requirements: To declare the Minor in Religion and Politics, students should use the Workday system and then meet with the Center's Director of Undergraduate Studies. [2] The program requirements include completing 15 units of coursework. [4] This consists of one required introductory course, 12 additional units (nine of which must be at the 3000/4000 level), and attendance at five events sponsored by the John C. Danforth Center on Religion and Politics. [2, 4] All coursework for the minor must be taken for a letter grade, with a C- or higher. [4]
Description: The Center offers a minor in religion and politics that provides an opportunity for sustained exploration of a number of issues, including church-state relations, religion's role in shaping gender and sexuality debates, religion and electoral politics, public conflicts over the nexus of religion and science, and religion's entwining with reform movements (from abolition to environmentalism). The Centerʼs interdisciplinary minor attracts students from many disciplines, including natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities; whether pre-med, pre-law, or pursuing futures in education, business, or the arts, they report that their studies are enriched by our curriculum.
MinGPA: All courses for the minor must have a grade of C- or higher. [2, 4]

ProgramName: Minor in Religious Studies
Requirements: Total Units Required: 18 units; 12 must be at the 3000 level or higher. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Robotics
Requirements: The program for the Minor in Robotics provides a fundamental understanding of robotic operation and preliminary training in the design and use of robots. [9] There are two robotics minors, one offered by Electrical & Systems Engineering (ESE) and one by Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science (MEMS). [10] For more specific information, the bulletin advises contacting the relevant faculty members. [9] To add a minor, students must log into the Workday system. [11]

ProgramName: Minor in Russian Language and Literature
Description: The Russian Language and Literature minor program is for students who want to achieve a high level of proficiency in the Russian language and study Russian literature. [9] The program offers elementary through third-year language courses and a number of courses on 19th- and 20th-century Russian literature (in translation) on a wide variety of topics. [9] As a minor, students will develop a broad understanding of the world, while exploring the diversity and richness of other cultures. [8] Students are strongly encouraged to study abroad. [9] The minor is an independent program administered by Global Studies, and students are encouraged to consider a major in Eurasian studies (through Global Studies), comparative literature and thought, or history, all of which can be pursued with a focus on Russia and the former Soviet Union. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Sociology
Description: Sociology is a social science that studies the sources and consequences of human behavior. It is a discipline that is particularly attuned to the social patterns that profoundly shape the choices available to individuals. The Minor in Sociology is a valuable complement to any major. The curriculum is a good foundation for careers in a variety of fields, including law, business, education, social work, and public policy.

ProgramName: Minor in South Asian Languages and Cultures (Hindi)
Minor in Spanish
Requirements: The Spanish minor requires the completion of 18 units, with at least 12 units taken in residence. Students must maintain a B average or better in Spanish and complete all courses with a grade of B- or higher. Courses taken on a Pass/No Pass basis do not count. [8, 10] Required courses include 6 units of "Cultures and Communications in the Spanish-Speaking World" (SPAN 3020 and SPAN 3030), 9 units from "Debating Cultures" (SPAN 32xx) and/or "Researching Cultures" (SPAN 36xx) courses, and a 3-unit 4000-level seminar. [8, 10]
Description: As a Spanish minor, you will study significant Spanish texts and cultures while developing your language skills. Your studies will delve into important themes such as gender roles, cultural traditions, community dynamics, and individual freedom -- topics that are critically relevant in today's world. The Spanish minor is offered through the Department of Romance Languages and Literatures. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Speech and Hearing
Requirements: The minor in speech and hearing is for current undergraduate students. It requires a minimum of 15 units of coursework. A grade of C- or higher is necessary for a course to count toward the minor. [3]
Department: Program in Audiology and Communication Sciences (PACS) in the School of Medicine

ProgramName: Minor in Strategic Management
Requirements: Prerequisites for the Organization and Strategic Management Minor (Non-BSBA) include: Calculus II, Microeconomics, and Statistics I. [1, 2]
Description: The Organization and Strategic Management Minor for non-BSBA students provides an understanding of organizational behavior and strategic leadership. The curriculum includes required courses such as 'Individual in a Managerial Environment,' 'Organization Behavior Within the Firm,' 'Negotiation,' and 'Leadership in Organizations.' Students can also choose from electives like 'Management Communication,' 'Women in Leadership,' 'Thinking Creatively and Leading Creative Teams,' and 'Mindfulness and Performance in the Workplace.' [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Systems Science & Engineering
Requirements: Units required: 15. This minor consists of fundamental courses in control systems and operations research. [1] In the area of control systems, students will be introduced to design techniques for controlling engineering and socioeconomic systems such as airplanes, automobiles, nuclear reactors, ecological systems, communication networks, the nation's economy and biological systems. In the area of operations research, students are introduced to techniques for optimally managing business resources and controlling business networks such as supply chains. [2] Students must take ESE 2170, ESE 4031 or ESE 4150, and ESE 4410. [1] In addition, students must take 6 units from a list of approved ESE courses. For more information, contact the director for the minor, Shen Zeng. [2]
Description: The Minor in Systems Science & Engineering (ESE) consists of fundamental courses in control systems and operations research. [1] In the area of control systems, students will be introduced to design techniques for controlling engineering and socioeconomic systems such as airplanes, automobiles, nuclear reactors, ecological systems, communication networks, the nation's economy and biological systems. In the area of operations research, students are introduced to techniques for optimally managing business resources and controlling business networks such as supply chains. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Text and Tradition
Minor in Urban Design
Requirements: The Minor in Urban Design is open to all students at Washington University in St. Louis, regardless of major. Students interested in the minor should contact the minor advisor. A total of 15 credit units are required. [4, 5]
Department: Sam Fox School of Design & Visual Arts
Description: The Urban Design Minor provides a platform for students to explore issues related to the urban condition that is unfolding in the twenty-first century. [3] Within this framework, students explore urbanization processes in the context of design applications and tools, critical urban issues, urban history, theory, and their application to real-world scenarios. [3] Aging infrastructure networks; pressures on access to education; overextended healthcare systems; loss of public investments; false securities in the housing market; spatial exclusion based on class, race, and gender; the dispossession of local inhabitants from common resources; food supply interruptions; the vulnerability and degradation of the environment; and wasteful forms of consumerism for the sake of capital accumulation all seem to be thriving themes in and around urbanization today. [3] Over the last three decades, the field of urban studies has received overwhelming attention from design disciplines as well as disciplines outside the world of design. [5] This has led to an outpouring of scholarly and political discourse, challenging the image as well as the perception of what is considered urban today. [5] The Minor in Urban Design is open to all students at Washington University in St. Louis, regardless of major. At least 12 of the 15 credit units must be applied exclusively to the minor and cannot be counted toward another major or minor. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Urban Studies
Requirements: The Common Application or Coalition Application is required. A $75 non-refundable application fee or fee waiver is also required. Applicants must submit a high school transcript.

ProgramName: Minor in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
Requirements: Total units required: 18 units, 12 of which must be taken in courses numbered 3000 or higher. Individual programs are designed in consultation with an advisor. All courses must be in WGSS or a WGSS-approved course in another department. All courses taken for the minor must be taken for a grade, and students must earn a grade of C- or higher. [13]
Description: As a women, gender, and sexuality studies (WGSS) minor, you will examine how gender affects many aspects of the world in which we live, such as literature, art, history, political structures, social relations, and economic institutions. [16] You will explore women's and men's experiences, concerns, and perspectives and see how these vary among different social groups and at different points in time. [16]

ProgramName: Minor in World Music, Dance, and Culture
Description: The minor in world music, dance, and culture is offered by the Department of Performing Arts (PAD). This minor can be completed by taking 15 units of coursework. No more than 3 units can be taken in a given summer. Students in this minor will learn a diverse range of art forms from around the globe. This minor is for students who are interested in the performing arts as a global phenomenon, and it is a great opportunity for students who are already taking our world music and dance courses to get recognition for their work. [11, 15]

ProgramName: Minor in Writing
Description: Total Units Required: 15 units; Grade Requirement: Students are expected to take courses for letter grades and to receive a grade of C or better in each. Required Courses: Students must take one of the following courses: WRITING 3000 Argumentation (3 units) or WRITING 3001 Exposition (3 units). Elective Courses: Students must complete 12 additional units, at least 6 of which must be at the 3000 level or higher. With department approval, up to 6 units of journalism courses in writing or editing offered by the School of Continuing & Professional Studies can be counted toward the minor. An off-campus internship (WRITING 2999 Journalism: Communications Internship) oriented toward writing may also be counted toward the minor. Regardless of level, at least 9 units counted toward the minor must be completed in regular courses home-based in Writing. For undergraduate scholars in the Howard Nemerov Program, two semesters of the 1000-level Nemerov seminar may count as 3 units of 2000-level work toward the writing minor and two semesters of the 3000-level Nemerov seminar may count as 3 units of 3000-level work toward the writing minor. A maximum of 6 Howard Nemerov units may count toward the writing minor. Students who wish to take a writing minor in addition to an English major are advised to take English and American literature courses (ELIT) exclusively for the major and writing courses (WRITING) exclusively for the minor. (Note: 1000-level WRITING courses do not normally count toward the writing minor.) Students who wish to combine writing with their English major are encouraged to consider an English major with a concentration in creative writing.
